## 2. Shared arithmetic and analytic contract

Use \(K=\mathbf Q(\sqrt{-3})\), \(\mathcal O=\mathbf Z[\omega]\),
\(\omega=e^{2\pi i/3}\), \(\lambda=1+2\omega\), and \(q_a=Na\).
An ideal sum uses the fixed primary generator and counts each ideal once;
an element-row sum retains all six units. The fixed bad set contains the
target conductor primes, primes above six, and the subsequently fixed
small-prime cutoff. It is chosen before the asymptotic scale. The Fourier
character, measure, Gauss phases and classical inputs are stated in
Appendix A.1–A.2 and used without a change of convention.

Every integer power of a residue character, including powers zero and six
and negative powers, is zero at a nonunit. Only the absent modulus-one
factor is identically one. Removing a phase therefore never removes its
zero set. A presented character keeps primitive-conductor zeros, redundant
presentation zeros, fixed bad-prime zeros and all displayed moving zeros.
A common puncture may depend on frozen outer labels but is fixed across
the live row sum. Moving arithmetic support is charged as width; it is not
a smooth-profile seminorm.

Let \(\beta\) be the supremum of \(1/2\) and the real parts of the
positive-real-part zeros in the finite-order, trivial-infinity Eisenstein
Hecke family, omitting the principal pole. Primitive and presented
characters have the same positive-half-plane zeros, because the extra
Euler factors have no zero there. Appendix B proves \(\beta\le7/8\)
from the original inputs. Write \(\kappa=2\beta-1\). Every use of the
source family is in the standing case \(\beta\ge51/100\); if that
condition fails, Theorem T already follows by the ordinary norm pullback.

### 2.1 The literal global source

Fix a nonzero ray modulus \(\mathfrak M\), a subgroup containing global
units, fixed anchor characters \(\eta,\eta_0\), and \(Q\subseteq\mathfrak M\).
Put \(Q_0=Q\cap\mathfrak q_{\eta_0}\), and require
\(Q_0\ne0,\mathcal O\) and \(Q_0\subseteq(72)\).
For each slot, \(\vartheta_i\) is a character of this fixed ray quotient
and \(\nu_i=\vartheta_i\overline{\eta_0}\), with both zero sets retained.
Its pool \(\mathcal P_i^{\rm can}\) is the original identity ray class
of good primes at scale \(P_i=Z^{w_i}\). The common smooth \(W\) is
supported in \([1,2]\). The normalized slot is
\[
Q_i(z)=P_i^{-1/2}\sum_{\mathfrak p\in\mathcal P_i^{\rm can}}
 \nu_i(\mathfrak p)c_z(\mathfrak p)
 W(N\mathfrak p/P_i)
 (N\mathfrak p/P_i)^{-33/50+iv_i},
\tag{S1}
\]
where \(c_z(I)=\eta(I)\chi_I(m_{\rm bad}^{6}z)\), with \(m_{\rm bad}\)
a fixed nonzero element containing the prescribed bad-prime support.
The sixth power retains exactly its zero mask and does not alter a
nonzero sextic value. A common whole-product norm phase \((NI)^{it_0}\)
may multiply this coefficient in every occurrence; its real height \(t_0\) is
a separate common parameter and is included in the bound \(V\) and
the polynomial height control. The
two ordinary factors have independent norm phases:
\[
A_j(z;X_j,p_j,t_j)=X_j^{-1/2}
 \sum_{I\ne0}c_z(I)(NI)^{it_j}p_j(NI/X_j),\qquad j=1,2.
\tag{S2}
\]
The profiles have the original fixed annular supports inside
\([1/4,9/4]\). They remain independent. Both factors have the same
whole row-feature orientation at this source inlet. A physical reflection
must restore that orientation before applying the source.

A row is *fixed inducing* when the primitive character inducing its actual
natural presentation has conductor dividing \(Q_0\). Define
\[
\mathrm{initialKeep}_{\eta,Q_0}(z)
 =\{z\ne0:\text{the natural presentation }c_z
       \text{ is not fixed inducing}}.
\tag{S3}
\]
Additional common Euler deletions preserve this primitive inducing predicate.
The source energy is the literal positive sum
\[
\mathcal E_Z
=\sum_{z:\mathrm{initialKeep}_{\eta,Q_0}(z)}
 |A_1(z)A_2(z)|^2\prod_{i\in T}|Q_i(z)|^2\Re\Phi(Nz/Z),
\tag{S4}
\]
including all roots, units and natural zeros. Here \(\Phi\) is Schwartz,
\(\Re\Phi\ge0\), and \(\operatorname{supp}\Phi\subset(-\infty,b_\Phi]\)
for a fixed \(b_\Phi\ge2\). Finite row subsets are allowed by positivity.

Write \(\ell_Z(X)=\log_Z\max(1,X)\). The assertion \(G(B,L,c)\)
means that for every positive loss \(\epsilon\),
\[
\mathcal E_Z\le C\,\mathcal D(\Phi)
 \mathcal S_{\mathcal F}(p_1,p_2)^2
 (1+|t_1|+|t_2|+V)^J Z^{1+\epsilon}
\tag{S5}
\]
throughout
\[
\ell_Z(X_1)+\ell_Z(X_2)+L\sum_{i\in T}w_i\le B,
\qquad \sum_{i\in T}w_i\le c,
\qquad0\le w_i\le\mathrm{mesh},\quad |v_i|\le V,\quad |t_0|\le V.
\tag{S6}
\]
The profile control is the product of the two finite Schwartz-seminorm
controls; its square gives the quartic homogeneity of (S4).
One may take
\(\mathcal D(\Phi)=16(1+\pi)^2\max_{0\le a\le2}\sup_x|x|^a|\Phi(x)|\).
The allowed real powers and all further ordinary shortenings retain the
same bounded-range contract. The source is not an arbitrary coefficient
or arbitrary prime-pool theorem.

The order of choices is part of (S5). Requested loss and bounded geometric
ranges determine the mesh **before** the finite slot type. After the finite
type and common marked profile are fixed, take the finite union of profile
orders and the maximum height degree. Fixed compatible characters, ray
data and support caps determine constants and onset. Those precede the
live slot subset, widths, heights, ordinary profiles and lengths, radial
test and retained row family. All statements below respect this order;
neither a live growing number of slots nor boundary-uniform source
constants are asserted.

For a packed sublattice row \(Vz\) at radial scale \(K\), positive
enlargement uses \(U=N(V)K=Z^M\). The actual keep and all masks are
packed first. There is no omitted lattice-density factor. The canonical

### 2.2 Common analytic operations

Compact joint logarithmic profiles admit Fourier expansions with a finite
weighted \(L^1\) norm. Minkowski, Cauchy and the common-profile moment
therefore permit independent unit-modulus norm powers and rowwise smooth
parameters at a finite seminorm cost. The proof and required derivatives
are in Appendix A.1 and the moment proofs. A moving arithmetic mask may
not be hidden in this control. Every tail is estimated on the original
expression with a fixed polynomial envelope before selecting the decay
order.

The actual row decomposition is \(z=u e^6\), with \(u\) sixth-power-free.
No coprimality between \(u,e\) is required. Its character is the original
core character with the exact additional mask \(\mathbf1_{(I,e)=1}\).
All root sums below include this mask. Bounded nonempty ordinary scales
retain the unit; if an annulus is empty it contributes zero. In particular
a nonempty profile supported below \(9X/4\) has \(X\ge4/9\), so
subunit central normalization is bounded.

The natural unmarked paired moment is available for all bounded ordinary
lengths, with independent profiles/heights and polynomial-size common
puncture fixed across the row sum. It excludes principal inducing rows,
and includes fixed nonprincipal characters. Its full proof is Appendix
A.5; its marked extension and the inducing-predicate treatment are
Appendix A.7. These scopes are not interchangeable with an arbitrary
selected operator norm.

### The foundational boundary

The following theorem is the PR95 natural selected-cell norm, at the exact evidence scope already adopted by the supplied proof and used in its half-price source construction. ### 3.1. Original feature and finite operator

Let \(\mathcal O\) be the Eisenstein integers and \(NI\) the norm
of a nonzero integral ideal. We give the ordinary row feature explicitly.
For a prime ideal \(\mathfrak p\ne(\lambda)\), let
\(c_{\mathfrak p}\) be the cubic residue character: on a nonzero residue
\(z\), its value is the unique complex cube root of unity whose
Eisenstein reduction is \(z^{(N\mathfrak p-1)/3}\). Put its value
at zero equal to zero. Let \(q_{\mathfrak p}\) be the quadratic
character of \(\mathcal O/\mathfrak p\), zero at zero; in
characteristic two it is one on every nonzero residue. Set
\[
 \chi_{\mathfrak p}(z)=c_{\mathfrak p}(z)^2q_{\mathfrak p}(z),
 \qquad \chi_{(\lambda)}(z)=0.
\tag{SN0a}
\]
At primes outside six this is the usual sextic residue character of
Appendix A.1: squaring gives the cubic character and cubing the quadratic
character. At the dyadic prime \((2)\), of norm four, it is the
square of the cubic character; that raw source coordinate is not silently
deleted. The fixed physical bad-prime mask later deletes dyadic columns
where required by the source contract.

Define, including all multiplicities,
\[
 \mathsf X(z,0)=0,\qquad \mathsf X(z,\mathcal O)=1,
 \qquad
 \mathsf X(z,I)=\prod_{\mathfrak p^a\parallel I}
                    \chi_{\mathfrak p}(z)^a\quad(I\ne0).
\tag{SN0b}
\]
This is the original \(\chi_I(z)\) on the supported ordinary ideals.
On all ideals it is the exact natural feature denoted `idealRowHom` in
the supplied source interface. It contains no Gauss factor or completion.
The source definition and bad-prime dictionary are recorded, with pinned
original bytes, in `consolidation/feature_sources/SOURCE_BINDINGS.json`;
they are provenance for (SN0a)–(SN0b), whose definitions are local here.

Every prime factor present in \(I\) retains its zero at
\(z\in\mathfrak p\), even for exponents divisible by six.
The unit ideal is the absent product and has value one. A column divisible
by \((\lambda)\) is zero. The feature is multiplicative in each
variable and has modulus at most one; all fixed ray phases and further
presentation masks stay in the actual coefficients. In particular,
multiplying ordinary polynomials merges their ideals and never replaces
this feature by a power.

A **natural free row** is one of the original nonzero element rows whose principal ideal is sixth-power-free. Units, every allowed residue class, bad-prime states, and all valuations from zero through five are included. No squarefree or supported-row restriction is imposed on this natural row set. For a finite family \(\mathcal F\) of such rows and a finite family \(\mathcal S\) of ordinary integral ideals, define

\[
 \mathcal N(\mathcal F,\mathcal S)
 =\left\|\big(\mathsf X(z,I)\big)_{I\in\mathcal S,z\in\mathcal F}\right\|_{\ell^2(\mathcal F)\to\ell^2(\mathcal S)}^2.
\tag{SN1}
\]

Thus, for every complex row vector \((a_z)\),

\[
 \sum_{I\in\mathcal S}
  \left|\sum_{z\in\mathcal F}a_z\mathsf X(z,I)\right|^2
 \le\mathcal N(\mathcal F,\mathcal S)\sum_{z\in\mathcal F}|a_z|^2.
\tag{SN2}
\]

The adjoint inequality gives the corresponding ordinary-source estimate; conjugating all entries preserves the operator norm. The source family is arbitrary: it may contain the unit and nonsquarefree ideals, and ideals in different factors may share primes. It need not avoid the fixed bad primes. A zero-ideal index may be retained as its zero source coordinate or erased exactly; it contributes nothing for these nonzero rows.

### 3.2. Literal selected-slot descriptor

For a fixed finite number \(n\) of slots, a descriptor consists of real widths \(w_i\), real energy labels \(e_i\), finite sets \(\mathcal S_i\) of nonzero ordinary ideals, and common coefficients \(b_i(I)\). At scale \(Z\ge1\), put

\[
 Q_i(z)=\sum_{I\in\mathcal S_i}b_i(I)\mathsf X(z,I).
\tag{SN3}
\]

For a mesh \(\omega\ge0\) and coefficient bound \(C_{\rm slot}\ge0\), the literal bounds are

\[
 \begin{gathered}
 0\le w_i\le\omega,\qquad
 NI\le2Z^{w_i}\quad(I\in\mathcal S_i),\\
 \sum_{I\in\mathcal S_i}|b_i(I)|^2\le C_{\rm slot}.
 \end{gathered}
\tag{SN4}
\]

The finite row family belongs to one common individual-amplitude cell if

\[
 Z^{e_i}\le|Q_i(z)|^2
 \qquad(z\in\mathcal F,\ 1\le i\le n).
\tag{SN5}
\]

Its total width and slope hypotheses are

\[
 0<w_{\min}\le\sum_iw_i,
 \qquad v\sum_iw_i\le\sum_ie_i.
\tag{SN6}
\]

The energy labels need not be nonnegative. Slot width zero is permitted, and all slots remain in the descriptor. The ordinary source variable \(I\) in (SN1) does not enter the choice of the amplitude cell or its row family.

### 3.3. Natural selected-cell theorem, with full order of choices

For every fixed

\[
 A>0,\qquad P\ge3A+1,\qquad
 0<g<1/2,\qquad\varepsilon>0,
\]

there exists an **early** \(\omega_0>0\) with the following property. For every later finite slot number \(n\), every \(C_{\rm slot}\ge0\), and every fixed \(w_{\min}>0\), there are constants \(C>0\) and \(Z_0\) such that, simultaneously for every

\[
 Z\ge\max(1,Z_0),\quad0\le\omega\le\omega_0,
 \quad\frac12+g\le v\le\frac34,
\tag{SN7}
\]

for every literal descriptor satisfying (SN4)–(SN6), every finite selected natural row family \(\mathcal F\), every finite ordinary source family \(\mathcal S\), and every pair of real scales

\[
 \begin{gathered}
 1\le Y\le Z^A,\qquad N(z)\le Y\quad(z\in\mathcal F),\\
 1\le X\le Z^P,\qquad NI\le X\quad(I\in\mathcal S),
 \end{gathered}
\tag{SN8}
\]

one has

\[
 \boxed{\displaystyle
 \mathcal N(\mathcal F,\mathcal S)
 \le C Z^{\varepsilon}\bigl(X+Y^{1-v}X^v\bigr).}
\tag{SN9}
\]

The constants are uniform in every descriptor, common coefficient mask, admissible \(v,Y,X\), finite row selection and finite ordinary source family quantified after \(C,Z_0\). Dependence on \(n,C_{\rm slot},w_{\min},A,P,g,\varepsilon\) is permitted; dependence of the early mesh on the later slot number, later coefficient bounds, later positive total-width floor, row labels or source ideals is not permitted.

This theorem has a fixed positive gap. It asserts neither \(v=1/2\), a gap tending to zero with \(Z\), nor \(v<1/2\). It supplies the original sextic feature and its complex conjugate. It does not license separate natural-row bounds for its square, cube or fourth power.

### 3.4. Exact coefficient and quotient adapters

The following consequences are elementary and are proved here so that applications of the input retain the original source.

**Common masks.** If \(|m(I)|\le1\), replacing \(b_i(I)\) by \(b_i(I)m(I)\) leaves the support and widths unchanged and decreases its squared coefficient mass. The response of the new descriptor must still be checked on the selected rows; it is not inferred from the old response for an arbitrary mask. Fixed anchor characters, common punctures and presentation-zero factors are handled as these actual common coefficients. Independent real heights belong to their corresponding coefficient functions as unit-modulus norm phases. They do not change the squared coefficient mass: \(C_{\rm slot}\) is fixed from the original profile and bounded real-power interval, independently of all live heights. Polynomial height dependence enters only the subsequent finite smooth-profile and Sobolev controls, after the selected norm. Allowing the norm constant to depend on a height-dependent coefficient bound would not establish the stated polynomial height uniformity and is not used.

**Literal quotient descendants.** Fix an element \(a\). Put

\[
 b_i^{(a)}(I)=b_i(I)\mathsf X(a,I),\qquad
 Q_i^{(a)}(z)=\sum_Ib_i^{(a)}(I)\mathsf X(z,I).
\tag{SN10}
\]

Since \(|\mathsf X(a,I)|\le1\), the descriptor bounds are preserved. Multiplicativity in the element argument gives the exact identity

\[
 Q_i^{(a)}(z)=Q_i(az).
\tag{SN11}
\]

Therefore any actual descendant family \(\mathcal F_a\) for which \(az\in\mathcal F\) inherits the same individual energy labels and total slope under this quotient descriptor. One must still check that the descendants are in the natural row class and their norm bound is the claimed \(Y\). This is a transfer along an exact product-row identity, not transportation of a zero label or replacement by arbitrary powers of a character. Shared-prime zeros are retained in \(\mathsf X(a,I)\).

**Merged ordinary ideals.** For finite polynomials in the original feature,

\[
 \left(\sum_I b(I)\mathsf X(z,I)\right)
 \left(\sum_J c(J)\mathsf X(z,J)\right)
 =\sum_H\left(\sum_{IJ=H}b(I)c(J)\right)\mathsf X(z,H).
\tag{SN12}
\]

This follows term by term from multiplicativity in the ideal variable. Every product fibre is merged as written, including units and shared primes. No squarefree projection, coprimality deletion or feature power appears. Cauchy within each fibre, followed by the ordinary ideal-divisor bound, gives for fixed \(\eta>0\) and \(NH\le T\)

\[
 \sum_H\left|\sum_{IJ=H}b(I)c(J)\right|^2
 \le C_\eta T^\eta
       \left(\sum_I|b(I)|^2\right)
       \left(\sum_J|c(J)|^2\right).
\tag{SN13}
\]

Indeed there are at most \(d(H)\le C_\eta(NH)^\eta\) ideal factorizations \(H=IJ\); expanding the resulting nonnegative sum gives the product on the right. Repeating the argument a fixed finite number of times yields the corresponding fixed-word coefficient mass, with a late constant and an arbitrarily assigned small power. The original detector coefficients, including the exact Möbius sign for an inverse polynomial or coefficient one for an ordinary polynomial, remain inside the convolution.

**Restrictions and conjugation.** Restricting \(\mathcal F\) or \(\mathcal S\) contracts the corresponding coordinate projections and therefore cannot increase (SN1). Thus original fixed-inducing predicates, initial keep, rays and finite source cuts may be retained. Both the feature and all coefficients may be conjugated: complex conjugation is an isometry, so the same operator bound holds. This proves the orientation adapter without identifying independently extracted heights or profiles.

An aggregate product-response condition is not literally (SN5). Its passage to common individual cells, including inactive-slot padding and a positive retained active width, is a separate finite histogram argument in the half-price proof. That argument must be supplied before invoking (SN9); the product condition is not substituted silently for the selected-cell hypothesis.


## 4. Native initiation and the complete half-deletion source

The source construction has two independent parts. Appendix C proves the
complete arithmetic assembly: a priced packed energy, with its geometric

section supplies that packed energy. The argument uses actual amplitudes
on the packed rows; it does not transport an earlier row-selection mask
through Poisson.

### 4.1 The generic assembly interface

For a strictly preceding parent \(G(B_0,L_0,c_0)\), define
\[
D(P,S,M)=\max\left(0,\min\left(S,
       \max\left(S-c_0M,{P+L_0S-B_0M\over L_0}\right)\right)\right).
\tag{HP1}
\]
For nonnegative \(P,S\), this is the width which must be deleted to
enter the parent, clipped at deletion of all slots. The full parent is
used only when \(P\le B_0M\); if even the empty-slot point is outside
the parent, the unrestricted paired ordinary moment supplies the empty
product. This fallback is essential.

A *price* \(\Pi(P,S,M)\) bounds the literal packed energy by
\(\mathcal A Z^{M+\Pi+\epsilon}\), where \(\mathcal A\) is exactly
the radial, profile and polynomial-height control of (S5). In Appendix C's
source geometry, the retained ordinary width is \(P\), the retained
slot width is \(S\), and \(M=1+t-6u\) is the actual packed height.
The selected width \(u\) is paid when
\(\Pi(P,S,M)\le u+\epsilon/16\), on the full perturbed geometric
domain. A monotone locally Lipschitz price permits the small Fourier and
whole-slot errors already charged in that domain.

The four reference reserves for a child \(G(B,L,c)\), at root singleton
width \(W\) and selected width \(u_0(W)\), are
\[
\begin{aligned}
1-B+(L-2)W-\tfrac92u_0,&\qquad
\tfrac1{20}+\tfrac32(1-B)+(\tfrac32L-\tfrac52)W-\tfrac92u_0,\\
1-B+(L-1)W-4u_0,&\qquad
\tfrac13-2W-3u_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{HP2}
\]
Their positive uniform reserves pay, respectively, the complete reference
interval, second reference, diagonal budget and positive reference upper
endpoint. Appendix C supplies the actual common-divisor normalization,
the masked packing identity, both restoring directions, LOW's constant
\(2/9\) comparison, HIGH's reference choice and all zero, fixed-inducing
and tail contributions. Consequently this interface is an implication for
the original source, not merely its nonexceptional positive leaf.

### 4.2 A native source for every strict intercept

**Lemma HP-N.** In the standing case \(\beta\ge51/100\), for every
\(0<B<1\),
\[
G(B,4,1/10)
\tag{HP3}
\]
holds, including zero total marked width.

**Proof.** The natural canonical moment in Appendix A.7, after the
already proved initialization \(\beta\le7/8\), supplies the native
price \(\Pi(P,S,M)=\tfrac34S\) for all admitted bounded ordinary
lengths. One can view the parent as \(G(B,5,-1)\): it is vacuous,
because a nonnegative width cannot be at most a negative multiple of
the positive row height. Thus no prior improved endpoint or positive-cap
source is required.

Use child slope \(4\), cap \(1/10\), crossing zero and
\(u_0(W)=11W/25\). In the actual perturbed geometry, if \(f\) is
the frozen width, the selection satisfies
\[
{11\over25}(W-f)\le u\le {11\over25}(W-f)+m,
\quad 0\le S\le W-f-u,\quad0\le W\le1/10.
\]
Hence \(\tfrac34S\le u\), since
\(\tfrac34(W-f-u)-u\le-\tfrac1{50}(W-f)\).
Use the floor \(\epsilon/16\), mesh at most \(1/1000\), and
geometric tolerance at most \(1/100\). The height satisfies
\[
1+t-6u\ge1-1/100-6(11/250+1/1000)>7/10,
\qquad 1+t-6u\le3.
\]
The upper bound is the actual defect bound \(t\le1+6u+1/100\).
The four expressions (HP2) are
\[
1-B+W/50,\quad
1/20+3(1-B)/2+38W/25,\quad
1-B+31W/25,\quad
1/3-83W/25.
\]
They have the common positive lower bound
\(\min(1-B,1/750)\). All choices precede the live slots. The
complete assembly of Appendix C now gives (HP3). Its zero-width branch
uses the ordinary paired moment directly, so a strict positive width
has not been assumed. This is a mathematical transcription of Joseph
Bebel's supplied native initiation; no formal declaration is used in
place of the argument. ∎

### 4.3 The aggregate selected norm at an arbitrary fixed gap

Use the natural selected-cell norm of §3 with fixed caps
\(A>0\), \(P_{\rm norm}\ge3A+1\). For
\(0<g\le1/8\) and requested loss \(\lambda>0\), it implies the
aggregate estimate
\[
\mathcal N(\mathcal R_{\rm high},\mathcal I_X)
 \ll Z^\lambda\{X+Y^{1-v}X^v\},
\quad 1/2+g\le v\le3/4,
\tag{HP4}
\]
whenever the actual product of the original selected slot responses is
at least \(Z^{vS}\). The early mesh is independent of the subsequent
finite slot number. All ordinary source ideals, units, common root masks
and natural zeros remain.

Here is the finite passage from cells to the aggregate, including its
choice order. Put
\[
b=\min\{g/4,\lambda/[8(A+1)]\}.
\]
Choose the cell mesh for gap \(g/2\) and loss \(\lambda/4\),
and reduce it to at most one. Only afterwards fix the slot number
\(N\), a coefficient bound \(C_{\rm slot}\ge1\), and lower aggregate
width \(s_{\min}>0\). Choose
\(t=\min(bs_{\min}/(N+1),1/2)\) and \(n=\lceil2/t\rceil\).
The actual slot bound is \(|Q_i|^2\le256C_{\rm slot}Z^{w_i}\).
At the late onset \(256C_{\rm slot}\le Z^t\), it is at most
\(Z^{w_i+t}\), with \(w_i\le1\) and \(nt\ge2\).

Define the label of a response to be the largest \(j\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\)
with \(Z^{jt}\le|Q_i|^2\), or zero if that set is empty. For label
zero replace that slot, on this entire cell, by the unit polynomial
\(1\), width zero and energy zero. Positive-label slots retain their
original polynomial, width and coefficient mass. Thus the cell has one
common legal descriptor, independent of the ordinary source ideal; the
replacement is used to invoke the norm and does not assert equality of
physical integrands.

Put \(E=\sum_i j_i t\), and let \(S'\) be the sum of widths of
positive-label slots. The label bounds and the original aggregate response
imply
\[
 vS\le E+Nt,\qquad E\le S'+Nt,\qquad
 Nt\le b s_{\min}\le bS.
\]
It follows that
\[
 S'\ge(v-2b)S\ge s_{\min}/4,
 \qquad E\ge(v-b)S\ge(v-b)S'.
\]
Consequently the padded cell satisfies the selected-cell slope condition
at \(v-b\ge1/2+g/2\), with lower width \(s_{\min}/4\).
There are at most \((n+1)^N\) label vectors. Apply the cell theorem to
each actual restricted row family and sum its squared row norms. This
argument covers arbitrarily small nonzero responses; it does not attempt
to place unbounded negative logarithms in a finite histogram.

The envelope changes by at most \(Y^b\le Z^{Ab}\), since
\[
X+Y^{1-v+b}X^{v-b}
 \le Z^{Ab}\{X+Y^{1-v}X^v\}\qquad(X,Y\ge1).
\]
The exponent is \(\lambda/4+Ab\le\lambda\). The finite label
count multiplies the constant. It is chosen after the dictionary and
before live data. This proves (HP4), including bounded row radii, with
no live growing slot family and no norm theorem at \(v=1/2\).

### 4.4 LOW: delete the smallest actual responses

Fix the original packed state, positive row profile and keep. Put
\(U=Z^M\), \(P=\ell_Z(X_1)+\ell_Z(X_2)\), and
\(S=\sum_iw_i\), with \(0<M_{\min}\le M\le M_{\max}\).
There is one fixed \(C_Q\ge1\), independent of rows, roots and
heights, such that \(|Q_i(z)|^2\le C_Q^2Z^{w_i}\). Set
\(B_i=|Q_i|^2/C_Q^2\), and choose \(q=1/2+g\).
Partition this very same packed energy according to
\(\prod_iB_i\le Z^{qS}\) or \(>Z^{qS}\).

On LOW a zero factor makes the row zero. Otherwise delete all zero-width
slots and order the positive-width slots by
\(\log B_i/(w_i\log Z)\). Delete the smallest prefix whose width
\(e\) reaches \(D=D(P,S,M)\). Then
\(D\le e\le D+\mathrm{mesh}\), or every slot is deleted and
\(e=S\). The deleted normalized mass is at most \(Z^{qe}\).
Indeed, if \(l_0\le0\) is the total zero-width logarithm, \(A\)
is the positive-width logarithm and \(A_e\) its sorted-prefix sum,
weighted ordering gives \(A_e\le eA/S\). Thus
\[
l_0+A_e\le(e/S)(l_0+A)+(1-e/S)l_0\le qe\log Z.
\tag{HP5}
\]
When \(S=0\), the assertion is immediate from \(B_i\le1\).
No lower bound on a nonzero response or on its logarithm is used.

Partition LOW by the deleted subset. On each of these at most \(2^N\)
parts, the surviving subset has common original coefficients, keep and
profiles. Apply the complete parent source if \(P\le B_0M\);
otherwise \(D=S\) and apply the unmarked ordinary pair. Positivity
permits each row restriction. Assign the whole-slot overshoot and parent
loss before the finite slot type. This proves
\[
\mathcal E_{\rm LOW}\ll\mathcal A Z^{M+qD+\epsilon}.
\tag{HP6}
\]
The factors \(2^N,C_Q^{2N}\) are fixed constants, not scale powers.

### 4.5 HIGH: convolve ordinary ideals and sum every root

Both ordinary factors use the same row feature. Convolving their actual
coefficients gives
\[
A_1(u)A_2(u)=\sum_I c(I)\chi_I(u),\quad
\operatorname{supp}c\subseteq\{NI\le(81/16)Z^P\},\quad
\sum_I|c(I)|^2\ll Z^\epsilon\mathcal P(p_1,p_2)^2.
\tag{HP7}
\]
For each factor the squared coefficient mass follows from ideal counting
and central normalization. Cauchy on the complete multiplication fibre
costs the fixed-factor ideal-divisor bound. This proves the last estimate;
it retains units, shared primes and all ordinary ideals. At a fixed sixth
root \(e\), replace \(c(I)\) by
\(\mathbf1_{(I,e)=1}c(I)\). This is exactly the original root mask,
because \((I_1I_2,e)=1\) is equivalent to both factors being coprime
to \(e\). Its coefficient square mass contracts.

The actual root factory gives the same masked prime polynomials on the
core \(u\), even when \((u,e)\ne1\). With
\(Y\ll Z^M/(Ne)^6\), (HP4) at \(v=q\) and (HP7) yield
\[
\mathcal E_e\ll\mathcal A Z^{S+\epsilon}
 \{Z^P+Y^{1-q}Z^{qP}\}.
\tag{HP8}
\]
There is a second bound on the identical root subset:
\[
\mathcal E_e\ll\mathcal A Z^{S+\epsilon}Y.
\tag{HP9}
\]
To prove it, use the trivial original prime-product bound and enlarge the
positive row set to the nonprincipal core rows with its fixed-across-core
puncture. Apply Appendix A.5's full paired moment. The initial keep
continues to exclude principal/fixed-inducing rows; none is added by
this enlargement. The ambient scale is \(Z\), so bounded \(Y\) and
ordinary lengths as large as fixed powers of \(Z\) are included.
Fixed support factors such as \(81/16\) are put into the admitted
scale before applying the norm; an empty core family contributes zero.

Combine (HP8) and (HP9) **before** summing roots. For \(0\le P\le M\),
ideal counting and a split at \(Ne=Z^{(M-P)/6}\) give
\[
\sum_e\min\{Z^P,Z^M/(Ne)^6\}
 \ll Z^{(5P+M)/6}.
\tag{HP10}
\]
The other norm term sums to
\[
Z^{(1-q)M+qP}\sum_e(Ne)^{-6(1-q)}
 \ll Z^{(1-q)M+qP},
\tag{HP11}
\]
because \(q\le5/8<5/6\). The exponent in (HP10) is at most that
in (HP11), since their difference is \((5/6-q)(M-P)\ge0\).
If \(P\ge M\), the full unmarked pair bounds the energy by
\(\mathcal A Z^{M+S+\epsilon}\). Therefore HIGH always has price
at most
\[
H_{1/2}(P,S,M)=S+(P-M)/2.
\tag{HP12}
\]
For \(P\le M\), the actual price \(S+q(P-M)\) is no larger
than (HP12); for \(P\ge M\), the preceding unmarked price \(S\)
is no larger. No first norm term, root or cross term has been discarded.

The aggregate estimate was used for \(S\ge s_{\min}>0\). If
\(S<s_{\min}\), the trivial prime product and unmarked paired
moment cost \(Z^{M+s_{\min}+\epsilon}\). Choose \(s_{\min}\)
from the final loss before slots, and use the nonnegative price below.
This pays all small and empty slot sets.

### 4.6 The exact half price, with unbounded total slot width

**Theorem HP.** A complete preceding parent with
\(0<B_0<1\), \(L_0>1\), \(0<c_0<1/6\) supplies
\[
\boxed{\Pi_{1/2}(P,S,M)=
 \max\{D(P,S,M)/2,\ S+(P-M)/2\}.}
\tag{HP13}
\]
It is a full priced packed-source estimate with the shared contract of
§2, not a norm at the boundary slope.

**Proof.** Put \(T=\Pi_{1/2}\). The HIGH estimate is (HP12). For LOW,
\[
qD\le T+2gM_{\max}.
\tag{HP14}
\]
If \(S\le2M_{\max}\), use \(D\le S\) to bound
\(qD=D/2+gD\le T+2gM_{\max}\). If \(S\ge2M_{\max}\), then
\[
qD\le3S/4\le S-M_{\max}/2\le S+(P-M)/2\le T.
\]
Choose a fixed \(g>0\) with \(g\le1/8\) and
\(2gM_{\max}\) below its assigned share of the final loss. This
choice precedes the selected-cell mesh, the parent mesh, the dictionary
and every live parameter. Thus (HP6), the complete HIGH estimate and
the small-slot payment prove (HP13). No bound on total slot width was
silently chosen before the dictionary.

The deletion function is monotone in \(P,S\), and its finite
Lipschitz constants follow from maxima, minima and the affine functions
in (HP1). The HIGH term has coordinate constants \(1/2,1,1/2\).
Taking the maximum gives the generic price needed by Appendix C; a
specialized adapter with a smaller hardcoded slot constant is not used.
Independent ordinary heights enter only through common coefficients
and the already fixed profile/height controls. Original sublattice
packing is restored by its positive enlargement before the split.
All roots, shortenings, principal/reference payments and coefficient-box
operations are those proved in Appendix C. ∎


## 5. Complete global sources on the open parameter domain

### 5.1. Statement and analytic inputs

Under the standing case \(\beta\ge51/100\), the literal global source contract holds for

\[
\boxed{G(B,L,c)\quad\text{whenever}\quad
0<B<1,\qquad L>\max(1,2B),\qquad0<c<1/6.}\tag{UF1}
\]

Every source retains both original ordinary factors, their literal ideal coefficients and real annular weights, all selected original primes, every natural sixth root, common root masks, natural and presentation zeros, the initial keep, independent ordinary profiles/heights, shortenings, reflection/Fourier operations and coefficient boxes. Its early mesh precedes the finite slot dictionary. Each strict triple has a finite proof. No uniform constant is asserted as \(B\uparrow1\), \(L\downarrow2B\), or \(c\uparrow1/6\), and no boundary source is used by this theorem.

The locally proved native source gives

\[
B<1,\quad\beta\ge51/100\quad\Longrightarrow\quad G(B,4,1/10),
\tag{UF4}
\]

including zero marked width. The full packed half-price theorem gives, from any strictly preceding parent \(G(B,L_0,c_0)\),

\[
\Pi(P,s,M)=\max\left\{
\tfrac12\operatorname{deletionNeed}(B,L_0,c_0;P,s,M),
s+\tfrac12(P-M)\right\}.
\tag{UF3}
\]

The price is derived using a fixed positive selected-norm gap chosen from the requested final loss; no selected operator norm at the one-half boundary is assumed. The following finite induction applies the complete source-step assembly to this price. Its scalar checks are proved uniformly in the stage index and in the full closed marked-width interval.

### 5.2. A finite source path with bounds uniform in its index

First suppose
\[
            \max(1,2B)<L<4,\qquad0<c<1/6.
\]
Put
\[
\begin{aligned}
 c_{\rm seed}&=\min(c,1/10),&d_L&=4-L,&d_c&=c-c_{\rm seed},\\
 D_*&=\tfrac32(L-2B),&
 r_1&=(1-B)(1-2c),&
 r_4&=\tfrac13-2c .
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{UF5}
\]
Here \(c_{\rm seed},d_L,D_*,r_1,r_4\) are positive and \(d_c\ge0\).
Restricting the native source (UF4) to cap \(c_{\rm seed}\) gives the complete initial parent.

Choose the explicit constants
\[
\begin{aligned}
 K&=1+\frac{d_L}{D_*}
       +\frac{d_c}{(1-6c)c_{\rm seed}},\\
 a&=\min\left\{\frac12,\frac1{120c},
                    \frac{r_1}{9c},\frac{r_4}{6c}\right\},\\
 N&=\left\lfloor K/a\right\rfloor+1,\qquad A=K/N .
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{UF6}
\]
Then \(N\ge1\) is a finite integer and \(0<A<a\).
Set
\[
 d=d_L/N,\qquad e=d_c/N,\qquad
 L_i=4-id,\qquad c_i=c_{\rm seed}+ie
       \quad(0\le i\le N).                                       \tag{UF7}
\]
The intercept is \(B\) at every stage. The selector is \(u_0=AW\),
the crossing is zero, and the last source is exactly \(G(B,L,c)\).
Every stage has
\[
 L\le L_i<L_{i-1}\le4,\quad
 c_{\rm seed}\le c_{i-1}\le c_i\le c<1/6,\quad
 D_i:=\tfrac32(L_{i-1}-2B)\ge D_*>0.                              \tag{UF8}
\]

The number \(N\) can be very large near a strict boundary. No iteration
over that number is needed to verify the algebra: the following bounds
hold for every integer \(1\le i\le N\) and every real \(0\le W\le c_i\).
They give a genuine finite induction, not an infinite limiting argument.
Constants and onset may depend on this fixed finite \(N\), as the literal
source contract allows.

### 5.3. LOW payment and the actual retained parent cap

At stage \(i\), write \(L_0=L_{i-1}\), \(c_0=c_{i-1}\), and
\[
 P=B-L_iW,\qquad s=W-u_0,\qquad M=1-6u_0,\qquad u_0=AW.
\]
The half-price LOW overshoot denominator is \(D_i>0\). The coefficient
of \(W\) in the LOW payment reserve is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 L_0A-\tfrac12\{d+(6B-L_0)A\}
 &=D_iA-\tfrac12d\\
 &\ge\frac{D_*K-d_L/2}{N}>0 .                                   \tag{UF9}
\end{aligned}
\]
The final strict inequality follows directly from
\(K=1+d_L/D_*+d_c/((1-6c)c_{\rm seed})\).
The payment itself is nonnegative at \(W=0\), as required; a strictly
positive payment at zero width is not asserted or needed.

For the parent cap, the exact reserve is
\[
 R_C(W)=c_0(1-6AW)-(W-AW)
       =c_0+\{-1+(1-6c_0)A\}W.                                  \tag{UF10}
\]
Its slope is negative because \(0<c_0<1/6\) and \(A<1/2\).
At the child endpoint \(W=c_i=c_0+e\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 R_C(c_i)
   &=-e+(1-6c_0)Ac_i\\
   &\ge\frac{(1-6c)c_{\rm seed}K-d_c}{N}>0 .
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{UF11}
\]
Every factor used for the lower bound is nonnegative. In particular,
the cap increase has been paid by the actual retained parent cap, not
by an artificial requirement that caps decrease. Define the positive
uniform cap reserve
\[
 r_C=\min\left(c_{\rm seed},
        \frac{(1-6c)c_{\rm seed}K-d_c}{N}\right)>0 .                        \tag{UF12}
\]
Then \(R_C(W)\ge r_C\) throughout every stage and full width interval.

### 5.4. Reference, height and HIGH gates

Let \(u_0=AW\), and write the four literal reference reserves as
\[
\begin{aligned}
 R_1&=1-B+(L_i-2)W-\tfrac92u_0,\\
 R_2&=\tfrac1{20}+\tfrac32(1-B)
                         +(\tfrac32L_i-\tfrac52)W-\tfrac92u_0,\\
 R_3&=1-B+(L_i-1)W-4u_0,\\
 R_4&=\tfrac13-2W-3u_0 .
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{UF13}
\]
The unselected first reserve satisfies the exact decomposition
\[
 1-B+(L_i-2)W
 =(1-B)(1-2W)+(L_i-2B)W\ge r_1.                                 \tag{UF14}
\]
Here \(L_i>2B\), \(W\ge0\), and \(W\le c<1/6\) justify every sign.
Therefore the choice \(A<r_1/(9c)\) gives
\[
 R_1\ge r_1-\tfrac92Ac>\tfrac12r_1>0 .
\]
The remaining reserves obey
\[
\begin{aligned}
 R_2&=\tfrac32R_1+\tfrac1{20}+\tfrac12W+\tfrac94u_0>0,\\
 R_3&=R_1+W+\tfrac12u_0>0,\\
 R_4&\ge r_4-3Ac>\tfrac12r_4>0 .
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{UF15}
\]
Thus a single positive reference tolerance, for example the minimum of
\(r_1/2\) and \(r_4/2\), works uniformly in all indices and widths.

The nominal height has the positive reserve
\[
 r_H=\tfrac1{10}-6Ac>\tfrac1{20},\qquad
              M=1-6u_0\ge9/10+r_H .                             \tag{UF16}
\]
This uses \(A<1/(120c)\).
The half HIGH and complete root-cone identities are
\[
\begin{aligned}
 u_0-\{s+\tfrac12(P-M)\}
        &=\tfrac12R_1+\tfrac54u_0
          \ge\tfrac12(r_1-\tfrac92Ac)=:r_J>0,\\
 M-P-2s&=R_1+\tfrac12u_0>0 .
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{UF17}
\]
The first reference condition therefore pays HIGH; no additional
unproved source-length estimate is inserted.

These are bounds over the whole closed real interval \(0\le W\le c_i\).
They do not infer an interval statement from sampled contacts.

### 5.5. The full perturbed ledger

Use the full half-price theorem (HP13). Its HIGH coordinate Lipschitz constants are \(1/2,1,1/2\); the deletion-need Lipschitz constant, enlarged to at least one, controls the complete price. The generic source assembly uses this full price directly.

At any stage and any requested child error \(\varepsilon>0\), put
\[
\begin{aligned}
 m&=\min(r_H,r_J),&
 \mathrm{floor}&=\varepsilon/16,\\
 \mathrm{meshCap}&=m/12,&
 \mathrm{tailCap}
 &=\min\{m/4,r_C,1,L_0\varepsilon/24,\varepsilon/32\}.
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{UF18}
\]
All are positive and precede the actual geometry and finite slots.
The actual source-side geometry is
\[
\begin{gathered}
 u_0\le u\le u_0+\mathrm{mesh},\quad s\le W-u,\quad
 P_C\le B-L_iW+\mathrm{tl},\\
 M=1+t-6u,\qquad
 -\mathrm{tl}\le t\le1+6u+\mathrm{tl}.
\end{gathered}
\]
The chosen budgets give \(9/10\le M\le3\). More explicitly, the lower
height loses at most \(6\mathrm{mesh}+\mathrm{tl}\le3m/4\le3r_H/4\);
the upper height follows from \(M\le2+\mathrm{tl}\le3\).

The perturbed parent-cap reserve is still complete:
\[
 s-c_0M
 \le-r_C+(6c_0-1)(u-u_0)+c_0\mathrm{tl}
 \le-r_C+c_0\mathrm{tl}\le0 .                                   \tag{UF19}
\]
The overshoot coefficient is negative, and \(c_0<1\),
\(\mathrm{tl}\le r_C\).

Let \(F=P_C+L_0s-BM\). The inherited defect calculation, now with zero
crossing and constant intercept, gives
\[
 F\le dW+(6B-L_0)u+(B+1)\mathrm{tl}.
\]
Equations (UF9) and (UF8) imply, first at \(u_0=AW\) and then at
\(u\ge u_0\),
\[
 \frac{F}{2L_0}
 \le u+\frac{(B+1)\mathrm{tl}}{2L_0}
 \le u+\varepsilon/16 .
\]
Since (UF19) holds, the complete inherited inequality
\(\operatorname{deletionNeed}\le\max(0,F/L_0)\) applies. The right
side \(u+\varepsilon/16\) is nonnegative, so the same LOW payment holds
when \(F<0\). This includes width zero and the entire small-width floor.

For HIGH, the exact perturbed bound is
\[
 s+\tfrac12(P_C-M)-u
       \le-r_J+\mathrm{mesh}+\mathrm{tl}\le0 .
\]
Indeed the two perturbations total at most \(m/3\le r_J/3\).
The unchanged more conservative ledger allowance
\(5\mathrm{mesh}+2\mathrm{tl}\le11m/12\le r_J\) is also valid.
Finally \(\varepsilon/16\le\varepsilon/(16(3/4))\), so the generic
floor field remains paid. These estimates prove the full `LedgerAt`,
not merely its nominal counterpart.

### 5.6. Complete induction and quantifier order

At each stage take the generic data with constant intercept \(B\),
parent \((L_{i-1},c_{i-1})\), child \((L_i,c_i)\), crossing zero,
\(H_{\min}=9/10\), \(H_{\max}=3\), \(L_{\mathrm{plain}}=4\),
\(\kappa=3/4\), selector \(AW\), and price (UF3).
The face, crossing, envelope, selector, and reference fields follow
from (UF8) and (UF13)--(UF17). The selector is monotone on
\([0,c_i]\) and lies between zero and \(W\) because \(0<A<1\).
The generic source-step ledger is fully paid by (UF18)--(UF19).

Assume only that the strictly preceding parent is complete. The full half-price theorem supplies the packed positive-energy estimate at price (UF3), with row exponent between \(9/10\) and \(4\) and ordinary source range bounded by \(4\). Apply the locally proved generic cube-free source assembly: its contrary-side second-divisor provider, diagonal supplier, principal/reference suppliers and zero-width complement have exactly these inputs. The constant-intercept, zero-crossing geometry is permitted because its crossing obligation is \(0\le s_0\), \((L_0-L)s_0\le B_0-B\), with a parent-cap condition only when \(s_0>0\); here both sides are zero. The source-step theorem therefore gives the complete child from the complete parent.

This composition preserves all reference, diagonal, second-divisor,
principal, floor, profile, small-height and large-height sectors.
Both original ordinary factors and every selected original prime retain
their coefficients, masks, roots, and natural zeros. The complete source
is global; restricting it to an original detector band uses positivity.
There is no Poisson transport of an original zero label.

and reference tolerances. Only then choose the finite slot type,

The supplier and assembly then choose finite seminorm controls,
constants, polynomial height degrees and onset before the live widths,
shortenings and heights. A finite union and maximum combine these

and the external tail order is chosen last. Each stage is a theorem for

through \(N\) stages.

Finite induction from the complete native source (UF4), restricted to

### The domain-inclusion lemma

Write a source face as

\[
 F=(B,L,a,b,c_-,c_+),
\]

meaning that at row exponent \(M\ge0\), its two ordinary exponents and total marked width satisfy

\[
 aM\le m_1,m_2\le bM,\qquad c_-M\le s\le c_+M,
 \qquad m_1+m_2+Ls\le BM.
\]

The complete global source \(G(B,L,c)\) has face \((B,L,0,B,0,c)\); the counting inlet uses the broad face \((B,L,0,1/2,0,c)\). All other data in these contracts are literal and identical: ideal coefficients and real annular powers, original ray-prime pools, fixed masks and holes, inducing predicates, natural/presentation zeros and initial keep, both ordinary profiles and their independent real heights, root masks, reflection/Fourier operations, shortenings, and coefficient boxes.

**Lemma D1 (exact face inclusion).** Let \(G(B_u,L_u,c_u)\) be a complete global source with \(B_u\ge1/2\). A broad face with parameters \((B_b,L_b,c_b)\) is supplied by this source if

\[
 0\le c_b\le c_u,\qquad
 B_b+\max(L_u-L_b,0)c_b\le B_u. \tag{D1}
\]

**Proof.** The ordinary bounds \(0\le m_i\le M/2\) lie in \([0,B_uM]\), and \(0\le s\le c_bM\le c_uM\). Moreover

\[
\begin{aligned}
 m_1+m_2+L_us
 &=(m_1+m_2+L_bs)+(L_u-L_b)s\\
 &\le \{B_b+\max(L_u-L_b,0)c_b\}M\le B_uM.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus every admissible input to the broad face is an admissible input to the same complete global estimate, with the same coefficients and data. Restriction of a quantified estimate proves the claim. Its early mesh, seminorm orders, constants, height degrees and onset retain their original order and uniformity. No new row selection, coefficient class, moment, or lower-width bound is introduced. ∎

The same argument gives global-to-global inclusion if additionally the weaker ordinary upper bound is at most \(B_u\). For present purposes only the broad face is required. In particular a small slope \(L_b<2B_b\) does not preclude inclusion on a bounded marked cap: the correct test is (D1), not a comparison of slopes alone.

## 7. The complete same-zero count

The count is a statement about the original zero/amplitude fibres. Its inverse and plain witnesses belong to the same zero, character presentation and height. No zero label is transported by Poisson, and the underlying moment estimates retain their original coefficients, masks, natural and presentation zeros, all roots, independent profiles/heights, shortenings and zero-width alternatives.

### 7.1. The scalar curves and exact crossings

For \(0\le\delta\le3/4\), \(0\le p\le1/2\), put \(V=5/6-\delta>0\). The natural branch, available on the whole closed rectangle, is

\[
\begin{gathered}
D_O=3-p-\frac{2p}{3\kappa},\qquad
A_O=2(1-p)\left(1-\frac p{3\kappa}\right),\\
J_O=VD_O+\delta A_O,\qquad
N_O=(1-\delta)J_O+V\delta A_O/2,\qquad R_O=N_O/J_O,
\end{gathered}\tag{C1}
\]

where \(7/10\le\kappa\le3/4\). Its denominator is positive throughout the domain. The complete natural inverse/plain argument establishes this bound, with the same actual witness and all small-width fallbacks.

Let a complete broad source face have intercept \(B\), slope \(L>1\) and declared count cap \(\bar z\). Set

\[
\eta=10^{-7},\qquad z=\bar z-\eta,\qquad
s_-=3/100,\qquad m_H=173/400.
\tag{C2}
\]

The source's actual width at a plain witness length \(m\) is always

\[
z(m)=\min\{z,(B-2m)/L\}.\tag{C3}
\]

The two count modes are represented by one set of formulas:

| Mode | \(D\) | \(A\) | \(C_0\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Affine | \(3-p-4p/L\) | \(2-4p/L\) | \(1-2pB/L\) |
| Capped | \(3-p\) | \(2\) | \(1-2pz\) |

In either mode define

\[
\begin{gathered}
Z_0=1-C_0,\quad U=(1-p)C_0,\quad
J=VD+\delta(1-p)A,\quad T=J+\delta U,\\
N=(1-\delta)J+V\delta U,\quad
R_N=AT+(Z_0-p)J,\quad D_J=DJ,\quad M_N=DT-R_N.
\end{gathered}\tag{C4}
\]

The candidate count is \(R=N/J\). With \(t_*=T/J\), \(r_*=R_N/D_J\), and \(m_*=M_N/D_J\), direct substitution proves

\[
m_*=t_*-r_*,\qquad
1-\delta[p+(1-p)r_*]
=1-\delta A m_*-\delta Z_0
=1-\delta+V(t_*-1)=R.
\tag{C5}
\]

The middle expression is the literal affine or capped plain curve in its designated segment. The clipped continuation (C3), rather than a constant cap extended past its cone, is used outside that segment.

### 7.2. Complete admission and free nonnegative witness floor

Choose a fixed \(\mu\ge0\). For an affine branch set

\[
 m_L=\max\{\mu+\eta,(B-Lz)/2+\eta\},
\qquad
 m_U=\min\{11/25-\eta,m_H-\eta,
                 (B-L(s_-+\eta))/2-\eta\}.
\tag{C6a}
\]

For a capped branch set

\[
 m_L=\mu+\eta,\qquad
 m_U=\min\{11/25-\eta,m_H-\eta,(B-Lz)/2-\eta\}.
\tag{C6b}
\]

On an upward closed window \(Q=[\delta_0,\delta_1]\times[p_0,1/2]\) inside the full rectangle, require all fifteen of the following polynomials to be strictly positive:

\[
\begin{gathered}
D,\ A,\ C_0,\ J,\ T-J,\ (12499/10000)J-T,\\
R_N-(23/37)D_J,\ D_J-R_N,\ M_N-m_LD_J,\ m_UD_J-M_N,\\
N-(1-2\delta m_H-2\delta p s_-)J,\ UJ_p-U_pJ,\\
11/25-m_H-\eta,\ B-2m_H-L(s_-+\eta)-2\eta,\ \Xi,
\end{gathered}\tag{C7}
\]

where \(\Xi=1\) in affine mode and \(\Xi=(z-s_--\eta)D_J\) in capped mode. Require also \(\eta<z<7/37\), actual source-cap inclusion, and the literal source/inducing/height hypotheses. The numerical condition \(B>22/23\) appearing in some earlier convenient wrappers is not part of the general source-face theorem: the full PR95 bank has faces below it. Here the exact general face and all guards (C7) are used. Lemma D1 supplies those actual broad faces without a wrapper restriction.

**Theorem C (complete count).** Under these hypotheses, the original detector count on \(Q\) is bounded with exponent \(R=N/J\), arbitrary requested small loss and the original finite polynomial height factor. The lower witness floor may be any fixed \(\mu\ge0\). It does not change the physical bookkeeping floor \(2/5\).

**Proof.** Set \(m_{\rm Lo}=m_L-\eta\) and \(m_{\rm Hi}=m_H\). These satisfy \(m_{\rm Lo}\ge0\) and \(2/5\le m_{\rm Hi}<1/2\). Positive denominators and the cutoff/inverse guards give

\[
1<t_*<12499/10000<3/2,\qquad 23/37<r_*<1,
\qquad m_L<m_*<m_U.
\tag{C8}
\]

For \(0\le\epsilon\le\eta\), therefore \(m_{\rm Lo}+\epsilon\le m_L<m_*\). The actual same-zero witness relation is

\[
t_*-r-\epsilon\le m,\qquad r\le t_*+\epsilon.
\tag{C9}
\]

Before splitting the witnesses, check that the marked widths are actual whole-slot selections in the original fibre. At row scale \(U=Z^d\), write the physical prime widths as \(z_i=\ell_i/d\), their total as \(L_{\rm supply}=\ell/d\), and their binned squared amplitudes as

\[
 |Q_{u,i}|^2\ge U^{2z_i g_i-o(1)},\qquad
 0\le g_i\le\delta/2,\qquad
 \sum_i z_i g_i=\delta pL_{\rm supply}.
\tag{C9a}
\]

Arrange the common cell labels \(g_i\) in decreasing order. The average on any initial subinterval of the resulting step function is at least its average on the whole interval. For each desired \(0\le s\le L_{\rm supply}\), take this initial interval of length \(s\) and discard its last fractional slot. The resulting genuine subset \(I\) has total width in \([s-\mathrm{mesh},s]\) and

\[
 \prod_{i\in I}|Q_{u,i}|^2
 \ge U^{2\delta p s-\delta\,\mathrm{mesh}-o(1)}.
\tag{C9b}
\]

The selection depends only on the fixed amplitude cell and widths; it precedes the ordinary summation variables. Whole-polynomial conjugation and multiplication by the actual fixed character put these same polynomials in the witness orientation without changing their moduli. Natural and presentation zeros, the fixed inducing exclusion, punctures and common masks remain in the resulting source.

The return geometry supplies \(\ell/d>1/5\) throughout the conductor range. For every \(r\in[r_*,1]\), the desired inverse width is less than

\[
 (1-r_*)/2<(1-23/37)/2=7/37<1/5.
\tag{C9c}
\]

If \((1-r)/2>\nu>0\), choose \(s=(1-r)/2-\nu\). Both literal inverse gates hold, including after discarding the final fractional slot:

\[
 r+2s=1-2\nu<1,\qquad
 2r+8s=4-2r-8\nu<3,
\tag{C9d}
\]

because \(r>23/37>1/2\). If \((1-r)/2\le\nu\), select no mark and use the unmarked inverse estimate; the omitted marked gain is at most \(2\delta p\nu\). In particular \(r=1\) is covered without pretending a positive marked width exists.

For the plain witness use \(s=z(m)-\nu\), if positive. Its supply follows from \(z(m)\le z<7/37<1/5\). The source face is applicable to two copies of the actual ordinary polynomial at length \(U^m\): \(2m+Ls\le B-L\nu<B\), and \(s\le z<\bar z\). The guard at \(m_H\) in (C7) makes \(z(m)>\eta\) for all \(m\le m_H\), so this width is positive whenever \(\nu\le\eta\). The natural plain continuation uses \(s=(1-2m)/(6\kappa_{\rm plain})-\nu\) when positive; for \(m\ge m_H\) its undecremented value is at most \((1-2m_H)/(6\cdot7/10)<1/5\). Otherwise its unmarked fallback is available.

The same-zero witness lemma gives \(|M_u(U^r)|^2\ge U^{\delta r-O(\epsilon)}\) and \(|S_u(U^m)|^4\ge U^{2\delta m-O(\epsilon)}\). Combining these lower bounds with (C9b) and the corresponding positive moment sums, then dividing, gives the actual cardinality exponents

\[
 \begin{aligned}
 I(r)&=1-\delta[p+(1-p)r],\\
 P(m)&=1-2\delta m-2\delta pz(m).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{C9e}
\]

The errors are precisely the witness, moment, amplitude-cell, final-slot and \(\nu\) decrements kept in (C11). For \(r\ge1\), the full unmarked inverse moment has exponent \((1+5r)/6\). Dividing by its same-zero spike gives

\[
 1-\delta+(5/6-\delta)(r-1)
 \le1-\delta+V(t_*-1)+O(\epsilon),
\tag{C9f}
\]

using \(r\le t_*+\epsilon\). Thus these are counts of the original fibre with its actual same-zero witnesses, not independent optimizations over unrelated events.

Every witness belongs to one of the following exhaustive cases.

If \(r\ge1\), the complete long unmarked inverse moment gives exponent \(1-\delta+V(t_*-1)+O(\epsilon)=R+O(\epsilon)\). If \(r_*\le r<1\), the marked short-inverse curve \(1-\delta[p+(1-p)r]\) decreases in \(r\) and is at most its crossing value \(R\). When the requested marked width is at most the small-width parameter \(\nu\), its original unmarked inverse fallback supplies the same estimate with the allowed loss; otherwise use the marked inverse estimate. Width zero is included in that fallback.

If \(r<r_*\), (C9) implies \(m>m_*-\epsilon\ge m_{\rm Lo}\). For \(m\le m_H\), the broad source and (C3) apply. Its two plain-curve slopes are \(-2\delta\) and \(-2\delta(1-2p/L)\), both nonpositive because \(L>1\). Both have magnitude at most \(2\), hence the clipped curve satisfies

\[
P(m-g)\le P(m)+2g\qquad(g\ge0).
\tag{C10}
\]

Together with (C5), this bounds the plain witness by \(R\) plus the already budgeted witness displacement. There is no gap where the cap branch passes to the affine segment, even if one segment is empty. The source-width guard in (C7) implies \((B-2m)/L>\eta\) for every \(m\le m_H\), so all \(\nu\le\eta\) are below the clipped width over the enlarged witness interval.

For \(m_H<m<1/2\), use the natural width \((1-2m)/(6\kappa_{\rm plain})\), with \(7/10\le\kappa_{\rm plain}\le3/4\). Its value at \(m_H\) is at least \(s_-\). The natural-tail polynomial in (C7) pays the count at that join. Thereafter the natural plain curve has derivative \(-2\delta(1-p/(3\kappa_{\rm plain}))\le0\). If its width is at most \(\nu\), use its unmarked plain fallback. At \(m\ge1/2\), the same unmarked moment pays the endpoint and the original bounded witness extension. Thus no inverse, plain, natural-tail or zero-width alternative is lost.

The same-zero and height bookkeeping, together with the displayed moment-to-count conversion, retains the exact aggregate loss

\[
159\epsilon+\epsilon_{\rm moment}+\mathrm{mesh}+7\nu.
\tag{C11}
\]

Its fibre constant and one finite polynomial height degree are unchanged. The early mesh precedes the finite slot type and row labels; the two ordinary profiles and real heights remain independent. The value of \(\mu\) enters only the admissible interval, so changing it cannot change those loss coefficients. This proves the count.

Finally

\[
\partial_pR=-V\delta\,(UJ_p-U_pJ)/J^2\le0.
\tag{C12}
\]

The old branch is also antitone. Since each enhanced window is upward in \(p\), its bound remains available as \(p\) increases, and the finite minimum of all available bounds is antitone. It is independent of the conductor exponent. ∎

### 7.4 Natural-count monotonicity and supremum feedback

This calculation uses the complete natural count already obtained from the same-zero inverse/plain moments. It changes no source, amplitude cell or admission window. Throughout

\[
0\le\delta\le3/4,\qquad0\le p\le1/2,\qquad
7/10\le a\le\kappa\le3/4,\qquad V=5/6-\delta>0.
\]

Write

\[
D_\kappa=3\kappa(3-p)-2p,\quad
C_\kappa=\frac{2(1-p)(3\kappa-p)}{D_\kappa},\quad
S_\kappa=V+\delta C_\kappa.
\tag{FB1}
\]

The denominators in the natural count are positive on the entire closed rectangle, including its boundary. Indeed

\[
 D_\kappa\ge3(7/10)(5/2)-1=17/4>0,\qquad
 1-p\ge1/2,\qquad3\kappa-p\ge8/5,
\]

so \(C_\kappa>0\) and \(S_\kappa\ge V\ge1/12>0\). In the notation of (C1),

\[
 D_O=D_\kappa/(3\kappa)>0,\qquad
 A_O=D_OC_\kappa>0,\qquad J_O=D_OS_\kappa>0.
\tag{FB1a}
\]

Thus the natural count (C1), after division of numerator and denominator by \(D_O\), is exactly

\[
R_O(\kappa)=1-\delta+
 \frac{V\delta C_\kappa}{2S_\kappa}.
\tag{FB2}
\]

Its antitonicity in the amplitude parameter \(p\) follows from an explicit sign calculation. Put

\[
 \begin{aligned}
 H_\kappa(p)
  &=(3\kappa+2)p^2-18\kappa p+18\kappa^2+3\kappa\\
  &=(3\kappa+2)p^2+18\kappa(1/2-p)
                       +6\kappa(3\kappa-1)>0.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{FB2a}
\]

Every term in the last line is nonnegative, and its last term is strictly positive because \(\kappa\ge7/10>1/3\). Differentiating the displayed rational functions, with \(\delta,\kappa\) fixed, gives

\[
 \partial_p C_\kappa=-\frac{2H_\kappa(p)}{D_\kappa^2}<0,
 \qquad
 \partial_p R_O
 =\frac{\delta V^2}{2S_\kappa^2}\,\partial_p C_\kappa\le0.
\tag{FB2b}
\]

The displayed derivative of \(R_O\) is zero when \(\delta=0\) and strictly negative when \(\delta>0\). Hence the natural branch is available everywhere and is antitone on the full closed amplitude interval. This establishes the positivity and monotonicity used by the complete count without an admission restriction.

For the feedback in \(\kappa\), subtracting the two rational functions gives the exact identity

\[
C_\kappa-C_a=
 \frac{6p(1-p)^2(\kappa-a)}{D_\kappa D_a}.
\tag{FB3}
\]

On \([0,1/2]\), the maximum of \(p(1-p)^2\) is \(4/27\): its derivative is \((1-p)(1-3p)\), so the only interior maximum is \(p=1/3\). Consequently

\[
0\le C_\kappa-C_a\le
 \frac{128}{2601}(\kappa-a)<\frac{\kappa-a}{18}.
\tag{FB4}
\]

A second exact subtraction, using \(S_\kappa=V+\delta C_\kappa\), yields

\[
R_O(\kappa)-R_O(a)
=\frac{\delta V^2}{2S_\kappa S_a}(C_\kappa-C_a)
\le\frac5{216}(\kappa-a).
\tag{FB5}
\]

Indeed \(V^2/(S_\kappa S_a)\le1\) and \(\delta/2\le3/8<5/12\), so (FB4) gives the displayed inherited constant (and even a slightly smaller scalar constant on this rectangle). The proof uses only the stated rectangle; it assumes no intermediate endpoint ceiling.

All enhanced count candidates have their actual source and upward admission windows fixed independently of \(\kappa\). Let \(R_*(\kappa)\) be the minimum of the natural candidate and those available enhanced candidates at the fixed point \((\delta,p)\). Choose a candidate attaining this finite minimum at \(a\). If it is enhanced, its value does not change with \(\kappa\); if it is natural, (FB5) applies. Since the minimum at \(\kappa\) is no greater than that same candidate's value,

\[
R_*(\kappa)-R_*(a)\le\frac5{216}(\kappa-a).
\tag{FB6}
\]

The new local affine count used in the algebraic endpoint construction is also fixed independently of the unknown actual supremum, so the same argument includes it. No differentiation of a changing minimizing branch is required.

In the physical return functional, the count is multiplied by \(3d/4\). Its feedback cost is therefore at most

\[
 \frac{3d}{4}\frac5{216}(\kappa-a)
 =\frac{5d}{288}(\kappa-a)
 <\frac1{50}(\kappa-a)\qquad(0\le d<1).
\tag{FB7}
\]

The strict old-source capacity cost is separate. Its exact change is

\[
 \frac{\delta p\min(d,2y-d)}{12}
      (a^{-1}-\kappa^{-1})
 \le\frac{25}{784}(\kappa-a),
\tag{FB8}
\]

because \(\delta p\le3/8\), \(\min(d,2y-d)\le y<1/2\), and \(a\kappa\ge(7/10)^2\). Thus the total old-row feedback coefficient is smaller than

\[
 \frac1{50}+\frac{25}{784}<\frac1{10}.
\tag{FB9}
\]

Enhanced physical capacities are fixed and pay only (FB7). These are exactly the bounds needed by the all-height return; they do not assert a new endpoint or boundary conclusion.


## 8. The complete physical return

Fix theta with 87/100<=theta<7/8 and put

\[
 \ell=11/3-4\theta,\qquad x=1+\ell-h,\qquad
 y=h-2\ell,\qquad k=(4+y-x)/6,\qquad\kappa_*=2\theta-1.
 \tag{GT1}
\]

Thus x+y=1-ell and

\[
 \theta-k=x/2+(y-x)/12.
 \tag{GT2}
\]

Retain the conservative scalar lower edge d_0=1/200. Choose a fixed zeta>0
and set d_+=h+zeta. The actual small-row/central-band split remains the
original one at Z^(1/100); its dyadic scalar extension uses d_0. Require

\[
 0<\ell<x\le y<1/2,\quad \ell<1/5,\quad 2x-y-\ell>0,
 \quad d_0<y,\quad h>0,\quad d_+<\min(1,2y).
 \tag{GT3}
\]

These imply 2(x+y)-1-3ell=1-5ell>0, h<2y, and 4ell<h.
They do not require ell<.171, h<.806, y>.458, or any other old decimal
box endpoint.

Choose a finite partition of [d_0,d_+]. On each closed partition interval
use either the old natural physical capacity or one specified **already
proved** complete physical source G(B_j,L_j,c_j). A source interval
[a_j,b_j] must have a_j>y. For that source independently choose an actual
physical marked cap sigma_j and a declared physical cap barsigma_j with

\[
 0<\sigma_j<\bar\sigma_j<c_j,\qquad
 \bar\sigma_j<1/5<\ell/d_+,
 \tag{GT4}
\]
\[
 0<B_j\le1,\qquad 2\le L_j\le9/2,\qquad
 B_j/2+(9/2-L_j/2)\bar\sigma_j<1,
 \tag{GT5}
\]
\[
 2y-(2-B_j)b_j>0.
 \tag{GT6}
\]

The strict barsigma_j buffer pays whole-slot rounding and permits a common
mesh below barsigma_j-sigma_j. The fallback guard is stated at barsigma_j,
which is stronger than necessary for an exact selection of width at most
sigma_j. Neither physical cap is a cap of a counting window.

The capacities on the assigned intervals are

\[
 C_O(\kappa,d)=\frac{\min(d,2y-d)}{6\kappa},\qquad
 C_j(d)=\min\left(\sigma_jd,
                    \frac{2y-(2-B_j)d}{L_j}\right).
 \tag{GT7}
\]

Retain a single common, conductor-independent count envelope
R_*(kappa,delta,p): the minimum of the natural branch (C1) and finitely many
complete enhanced branches (C4), each only on its own full admission windows
(C7). Its windows are upward in p and its derivative guard makes it
antitone. Every count source, declared count cap, witness endpoint and
admission buffer is the actual one used in that branch. The entire closed
domain is 0<=delta<=3/4, 0<=p<=1/2. The old branch is available everywhere.

For some fixed r>r_0>0, require on the entire domain at **both endpoints of
every assigned conductor interval**

\[
 E_{\kappa_*}(d,C;\delta,p)\le\theta-r,
 \tag{GT8}
\]
where the literal complete exponent is
\[
 E_\kappa=
 \frac12+\frac{13h}{75}-\frac y2-\frac\ell2-\frac{9d}{100}
 +\frac\delta2+\delta p(\ell-C/2)+\frac{3d}{4}R_*.
 \tag{GT9}
\]

Each endpoint may be proved by a finite closed rectangle cover, choosing any
admitted branch on each rectangle and clearing its positive denominator as
in the finite-certification section. Such different choices still bound the same R_*.

Finally define the actual complementary margins

\[
 \Delta_f=\theta-k-F_{\rm fl}(d_+)>0,\qquad
 F_{\rm fl}(d)=4x/25-3/20-51y/100+67d/100-3\ell/20,
 \tag{GT10}
\]
\[
 \Delta_s=S_{\rm small}-(7/8-\theta)>0,\qquad
 S_{\rm small}=y/2-13h/75-1/50,
 \tag{GT11}
\]
and, retaining the conservative principal contours and error allowances,
require
\[
 g_w=y/20-(1+h)/1000-1/4000>0,\qquad
 g_z=h/600-1/1000-1/4000>0.
 \tag{GT12}
\]

**Generic conclusion.** Under the complete source/count hypotheses and
(GT1)–(GT12), every ordinary character at every fixed positive presented
modulus is zero-free for Re(s)>theta at all heights, excluding the actual
principal pole. No extremal zero or attained supremum is assumed.

The analytic proof follows. Its only numerical obligation left to an
application is to certify its chosen source/count data and the stated
finite inequalities. The new theorem includes every complementary sector.

### 8.1 Independent caps, every shift and shortening

We prove the physical restriction with its independently chosen cap sigma_j. The proof uses the full source (S5), not a numerical wrapper with a fixed counting cap.

Fix one source interval and suppress j. Put m=y/d. By a_j>y and b_j<2y,
1/2<m<1. For t>=0 define

\[
 n(t)=1-m+t,\quad A(t)=(B-2n(t))/L,\quad
 C(t)=\min(\sigma,A(t)),\quad Z(t)=\max(0,C(t)).
 \tag{GT13}
\]

If a nonempty selected marked family has total width 0<z<=Z(t), then
z<=sigma<barsigma<c_j and 2n(t)+Lz<=B. Also n(t)>=0 and n(t)<=B/2<=1/2.
Every nonnegative shortened pair n_1,n_2<=n(t), and every remaining subset
of width z'<=z, therefore lies in the same literal G source. This is the
complete global source restricted to its actual ordinary and marked domain;
no lower marked-width window and no upper shift window is needed.

For a nonpositive ordinary exponent retain the original bounded-scale
treatment. Its natural budget has kappa_nat=3/4, supplied by the proved
7/8 bound, and hence price 6*kappa_nat=9/2. If n_1<=0, n_2<=n(t), then

\[
 n_1+n_2+(9/2)z'
 \le B/2+(9/2-L/2)z\le1.
 \tag{GT14}
\]

This pays both orientations by (GT5). The target kappa_* is not substituted
for this natural source parameter.

If Z(t)=0 there is exactly no positive-width nonempty selection. Use the
retained empty-slot reflection/clipping branch. Its actual coefficient bins
retain 0<=n(t)+ann<=2 and X_i<=U^(n(t)+ann)<=U^2, supplied by the original
bin condition 2xi+ann<=1/2. No moment for arbitrary unbounded ordinary
lengths is inferred from an empty product.

The clipping maps are monotone and 1-Lipschitz. With v=2t,

\[
 C(0)-Z(v/2)\le v/L.
\]
For 0<=a<=delta/2 and every v>=0,
\[
 \frac a2 C(0)+\frac{\delta v}{1000}
 \le \frac{\delta v}{4}+\frac a2 Z(v/2).
 \tag{GT15}
\]
Indeed the capacity loss is at most delta*v/(4L)<=delta*v/8, and
1/8+1/1000<1/4. All shifted tails keep this damping. The source calls at
positive capacity, their natural fallbacks, and the empty-selection branch
are precisely those just proved; (GT15) is not used to assert a moment
outside those domains.

The actual prime supply is unchanged: sigma<barsigma<1/5<ell/d_+<=ell/d.
The physical slot at Re(z)=17/50 is exactly the original inverse-character
annular coefficient of real power 33/50, with conjugated profile and opposite
imaginary part. This equality holds on every ideal, including every natural
zero. It is substituted into the finite pair before taking positive energy.
The original relative characters, fixed modulus and Euler factors stay fixed.

The physical free rows satisfy U^(1/100)<=N(u)<=U. After fixing the source
and its inducing data, the fixed-inducing exceptions have bounded norm and
are absent for sufficiently large U. Hence the original physical keep
implies the required source initial keep on these rows. The threshold is
allowed to depend on those fixed data. This is an eventual predicate
inclusion, not an identification of different keeps.

The two ordinary factors and both Fourier heights remain independent. The
same nonnegative radial majorant bounds the finite physical energy. The
source provides its original seminorms, polynomial height factors and common
profile controls. A physical source mesh is taken separately from every
count-source mesh, and their finite minimum is chosen before the slot type.
If original widths are at most mesh/200 and d>=1/200, the rescaled widths
are at most mesh; (Z^d)^(w/d)=Z^w preserves the same prime pools exactly.

Consequently (GT7)'s new capacity is the full physical consumer, for every
actual shift, shortening and remaining subset. The declared cap 31/500 of
the retained capP **count** branch is absent from this proof. Each new
application separately chooses a physical cap below its available global
source cap; the counting cap and all counting windows remain their literal
independent inputs. The algebraic application below makes its physical choices separately.

### 8.2 Edge reduction and actual-supremum feedback

For fixed delta,p, the count envelope is independent of d. Each capacity in
(GT7) is a minimum of two affine functions of d. Because delta*p>=0,
-delta*p*C/2 is convex in d; all other d terms in (GT9) are affine.
Therefore (GT8) bounds the whole assigned conductor interval. Different
intervals may use different already-proved physical suppliers. No equality
of capacities at a join is needed, and both estimates remain valid at any
shared endpoint. The finite partition covers every conductor exponent from
d_0 to d_+.

Suppose the actual retained primitive-family zero supremum beta exceeds

gives kappa_*<=kappa_beta<=3/4, while theta>=.87 implies kappa_*>=.74>7/10.
All enhanced sources, windows, physical intervals and capacities are fixed
independently of kappa_beta. Only the old count and natural capacity vary.

The natural-count feedback calculation in the count section, followed by the finite minimum, gives
\[
 R_*(\kappa_\beta)-R_*(\kappa_*)
 \le\frac5{216}(\kappa_\beta-\kappa_*).
 \tag{GT16}
\]
Its count cost in (GT9) is at most
5d_+(kappa_beta-kappa_*)/288 < (kappa_beta-kappa_*)/50, since d_+<1.
Every new physical capacity is fixed. On old intervals the additional
capacity cost is at most
\[

 (\kappa_*^{-1}-\kappa_\beta^{-1})

using y<1/2, delta*p<=3/8 and kappa_beta*kappa_*>=(7/10)^2.
Because 5/288+25/784<1/8, the retained reserves are

 \quad\hbox{on new intervals},
\]
\[
 E_{\kappa_\beta}-\beta\le-r_0-3\mu/4
 \quad\hbox{on old intervals}.
 \tag{GT18}
\]

Thus a finite physical partition and additional independent count branches
do not alter the feedback. No actual zero is assumed to attain beta.

## 9. The retained algebraic endpoint

With the original fixed presented modulus, ordinary character and principal-pole convention, the retained baseline theorem is

\[
\boxed{L(s,\chi)\ne0\quad\text{for all}\quad
\Re s>\theta_*:=\frac{777-\sqrt{1081}}{852},\quad s\ne1
\text{ when the actual principal pole is present}.}\tag{AE1}
\]

Equivalently \(c_*=(75+\sqrt{1081})/852\). The theorem covers every height and every ordinary character at each fixed positive presented modulus; it asserts neither the boundary nor uniform constants for growing moduli. The separate angular theorem retains its original fixed-family scope.

The proof uses the complete open source theorem, the exact source-face inclusion D1, the complete common-witness count theorem and the generic physical/complement/all-height return. The fixed source (D2) supplies all 24 inherited enhanced count faces, so every one of the 813 inherited windows is available without reproducing the older numerical source chains. The old natural branch remains available everywhere. All 1,826 original return rows are retained as the finite covering skeleton.

The preliminary theorem \(\beta\le7/8\) suffices. Under a contrary supremum above any target used below, \(\beta\ge51/100\) holds and all sources are available independently of the desired endpoint. Count and physical sources have separate roles: (D2) supplies the fixed inherited bank, while a nearby strict source selected below supplies the physical interval and the new local contact branch.

We first certify a nominal algebraic cover. Its contact is then paid by a quantitatively controlled family of strict source and return parameters. Taking the union of the resulting open half-planes gives (AE1); no boundary source or limiting uniform estimate is used.

### 9.1. Exact nominal parameters and the complete count near the contact

Write \(r=\sqrt{1081}\), and define

\[
 v_*=(61-r)/66,\qquad \ell_*=(4+r)/213,
 \quad h_* =\frac{32}{71}+\frac{838r}{76751}.                  \tag{AE3}
\]

Thus \(v_*=.4260823568\ldots\), \(h_*=.8096863494\ldots\), and

\[
 h_* =\frac{16(1/2+\ell_*)}{11+25/(5-4v_*)^2},\qquad
 \ell_*=11/3-4\theta_* .                                    \tag{AE4}
\]

Set \(x_*=1+\ell_*-h_*\), \(y_*=h_*-2\ell_*\), and
\(\kappa_*=2\theta_*-1\). The conductor edges are initially
\(d_0=1/200\), \(d_m=19/25\), and \(h_*\). At this nominal
stage only, the upper extension is zero. We subsequently replace it by
a strictly positive extension; no large-row argument uses zero extension.

For the new local branch use the nominal source parameters \(B=1,L=2\),
source cap \(4/25\), declared count cap \(1599/10000\), actual width
\(z=1598999/10000000\), witness floor \(\mu=3/10\),
\(\eta=10^{-7}\), \(m_H=173/400\), and \(s_-=3/100\).
Its true endpoints are

\[
 m_L=\frac{3401002}{10000000},\qquad
 m_U=\frac{4324999}{10000000}.                              \tag{AE5}
\]

On the closed upward rectangle

\[
 Q=[21/50,11/25]\times[49/100,1/2]
       \quad\text{in }(\delta,p),                           \tag{AE6}
\]

put \(V=5/6-\delta\) and \(H=5/2-\delta(1+2p)\). The nominal
branch is

\[
 R(\delta,p)=1-\delta+
       \frac{\delta V(1-p)}{H},\qquad J=(1-p)H>0.            \tag{AE7}
\]

This is the literal affine formula, with its actual clipped width
\(\min\{z,(B-2m)/L\}\), not a constant-width continuation beyond
the source cone. All fifteen (C7) polynomials, using (AE5), have positive
exact Bernstein coefficients on (AE6). The nominal certificate has
75 such coefficients. §9.4 supplies a uniform strict-source version
of these admissions.

### 9.2. The exact local contact inequality

At the nominal upper edge \(d=h_*\), the physical capacity is

\[
 C_* =\min\{7h_*/50,\ y_*-h_*/2\}=h_*/2-2\ell_* .          \tag{AE8}
\]

The equality and a positive cap reserve are checked exactly. With the
complete exponent GT9, substitution of (AE7) at \(p=1/2\) gives

\[
 E_*(\delta,1/2)=\frac12+\frac{\ell_*}{2}
 +\delta\left(\frac12+\ell_*\right)
 +h_*\left(\frac13-\frac{11\delta}{16}
       -\frac{5\delta}{16(5-4\delta)}\right).                \tag{AE9}
\]

Define

\[
 q_* =2+4\ell_*-11h_*/4>0 .                                \tag{AE10}
\]

The following is a polynomial identity over \(\mathbb Q(r)\):

\[
 \boxed{\theta_*-E_*(\delta,1/2)

### 10.2. Bernstein positivity on a complete closed rectangle

Let a polynomial \(P(\delta,p)\) have degree at most \(n\) in \(\delta\) and at most \(m\) in \(p\). On \([a,b]\times[c,d]\), make the exact affine substitution

\[
\delta=a+(b-a)u,\qquad p=c+(d-c)v,
\]

and write the result as \(\sum_{k=0}^n\sum_{l=0}^m a_{kl}u^kv^l\). Its tensor Bernstein coefficients are

\[
b_{ij}=\sum_{k\le i}\sum_{l\le j}
 a_{kl}\frac{\binom{i}{k}}{\binom{n}{k}}
         \frac{\binom{j}{l}}{\binom{m}{l}}
\quad(0\le i\le n,\ 0\le j\le m).
\tag{K1}
\]

Indeed \(u^k=\sum_{i=k}^n\binom{i}{k}\binom{n}{k}^{-1}
\binom ni u^i(1-u)^{n-i}\), and the analogous formula holds for \(v\). Expanding proves (K1), including all closed boundaries. The tensor basis functions are nonnegative and sum to one on the unit square. Therefore

\[
\min_{i,j} b_{ij}\le P(\delta,p)\le\max_{i,j}b_{ij}.
\tag{K2}
\]

Strict positivity of every coefficient is a sufficient proof of positivity on the entire rectangle; no sampling or mesh limit enters. The method is not asserted to be necessary or optimal.

For a branch \(R_b=N_b/J_b\), the strict nominal cell polynomial is

\[
P_b=J_b(\theta_*-E_{\mathrm{base},*})-(3d/4)N_b.
\tag{K3}
\]

The certificate provides the tensor coefficients of both \(P_b\) and \(J_b\). Their positivity gives \(J_b>0\), \(E_b<\theta_*\), and the quantitative lower bound

\[
\theta_*-E_b\ge
\frac{\min\operatorname{Bern}(P_b)}{
      \max\operatorname{Bern}(J_b)}>0.
\tag{K4}
\]

Since the actual common count is the minimum of all available branch counts, \(R_*\le R_b\), and its coefficient in the physical exponent is positive, the same bound holds for the actual exponent. This explains why choosing different admitted branches on different cells is valid.

For the 76 contact cells, the certificate uses the exact contact factorization and positive \(p\)-derivative in §9.2. It does not claim positive Bernstein coefficients at the equality point. The 1,844 other cells have 19,650 positive numerator and 9,412 positive denominator coefficients. The common lower bound in (AE15) is the least of the ratios (K4), so it is an explicit lower bound, not a claimed minimum of the underlying continuous energy margin.

### 10.3. Ordered quadratic-field and interval arithmetic

A pair of rational strings \([a,b]\) represents \(a+b\sqrt{1081}\). Addition and multiplication are

\[
(a,b)+(c,d)=(a+c,b+d),\quad
(a,b)(c,d)=(ac+1081bd,ad+bc).
\tag{K5}
\]

Division uses conjugation and the nonzero rational denominator \(a^2-1081b^2\). The integer 1081 is not a rational square. Signs are determined exactly: equal-sign terms have that sign; for opposing signs compare \(a^2\) with \(1081b^2\), retaining the sign of the larger-magnitude term. Alternatively one may use rational square-root enclosures whose squared endpoints bracket 1081. No floating-point assertion proves a sign in this argument.

For the strict perturbation, rational intervals enclose every coefficient before conversion (K1). Addition is endpointwise, multiplication takes the minimum and maximum of the four endpoint products, and inversion is used only on an interval wholly of one nonzero sign. These operations preserve enclosure. Positive lower endpoints of the Bernstein intervals therefore prove all guards for the entire parameter interval simultaneously, even when dependency among repeated parameter occurrences widens an enclosure.

The interval proof uses

\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{126618033386792}{10^{15}}&<c_*<
\frac{126618033386793}{10^{15}},\\
\frac{809686349433473}{10^{15}}&<h_*<
\frac{809686349433475}{10^{15}}.
\end{aligned}\tag{K6}
\]

These are exact quadratic-field comparisons. The 79 local admission coefficient lower endpoints are positive on \(0\le\rho\le10^{-12}\), with least value

\[
\frac{389644444334009}{66666666666700000}>0.
\]

All 36 listed geometric/complementary guards have positive interval lower endpoints on the enclosing box

\[
0\le t\le10^{-10},\qquad
0\le\rho,\zeta\le10^{-20}.
\tag{K7}
\]

The actual relations \(\rho=\zeta=t^2\) lie in this box. The strict fields \(\rho>0\), \(1-B=\rho\), \(L-2=\rho\), \(L-2B=3\rho\), and \(\zeta>0\) are proved analytically from \(t>0\), not asserted at the nominal value zero. The extra historical guard \(\theta_t<436691/500000\) is valid but no longer needed as an inherited endpoint premise; the preliminary \(7/8\) bound supplies the full feedback range.

### 10.4. Exact domain coverage

Every certificate cell is contained in its named original closed row rectangle. If the cell uses an enhanced branch, its whole box is contained in the named complete upward admission window. Each original row is tiled by its assigned cells: their interiors are disjoint and their exact rational areas sum to the original area. The same exact comparison for each edge gives the whole closed density/amplitude domain \([0,3/4]\times[0,1/2]\). A finite union of closed rectangles with full area and no overlap of interiors cannot omit a relative-open piece of the domain; any such omitted piece would have positive area. The finite union is closed, so it cannot omit an isolated boundary point either. Thus the area and containment statements certify the full closed cover, not only almost-everywhere coverage.

The edge counts are 448 for oldSmall, 448 for oldSwitch, 448 for newSwitch and 576 for newTop, totaling 1,920 cells. They retain all 1,826 original rows. On every conductor interval the capacity is the minimum of two affine functions and the count is independent of conductor. The physical exponent is consequently convex in conductor. The two endpoint inequalities therefore cover the full interval, as proved in the generic return.

### 10.5. Scope of the evidence

The preserved receipts establish the indicated finite arithmetic properties at the hashes of these unchanged data. The consolidation adds a direct exact check of the changed source-domain inclusion and comparison review of the rewritten arguments/interfaces. It does not replay the inherited validation tower or make old receipts certify new prose. The analytic theorem follows from the manuscript's source, count, physical, complement, feedback and Mellin arguments composed with the finite inequalities just specified.

## Appendix A. Arithmetic, completed reflection and the original moments

This appendix proves the original analytic inputs used above. Sections A.1–A.8
retain the coefficients and full domains of the supplied proofs, including the
more general moving-support and puncture families. Their original equation
labels and stable anchors are kept: e.g. (MF3.40) belongs to A.7, and (67)
