##### A.7.2.4 The enlarged plain-moment family

Use $\psi_k(n)=\tau(n)\chi_n(k)$ on $0<q_k\ll Z^m$, where $\tau$ combines a fixed ray character and displayed moving symbols. Their union **before** cancellations/exponent reduction has norm $\le Z^q$; width is $M=m+q$. A squarefree common mask $q_R\le Z^B$ may depend on frozen labels but is fixed over the row sum and applies to every plain and prime factor. Canceled row-character primes retain natural zeros; they do not become freely chosen row masks.

For positive slots fix nonzero integral ray modulus $\mathfrak M$, a subgroup containing global units, common annular profile $W$, anchor $\eta_0$, and ideal $Q\subseteq\mathfrak M$. Require $Q_0=Q\cap\mathfrak q_{\eta_0}$ to be nonzero, proper and contained in $(72)$. Each slot has $\nu_i=\theta_i\overline{\eta_0}$ for a fixed-ray-quotient character $\theta_i$, bounded real power $\sigma_i$ and height $v_i$:

$$
Q_{k,i}=Z^{-z_i/2}\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_i^{\rm can}}
 \psi_k(p)\nu_i(p)W(q_p/Z^{z_i})
 (q_p/Z^{z_i})^{-\sigma_i+iv_i}.
$$

Here $\mathcal P_i^{\rm can}$ is the genuine canonical good-prime pool at $Z^{z_i}$, retaining natural zeros and common puncture. MP uses this pool and common $W$; it asserts neither arbitrary subsets, separate slot profiles nor a finite-character-expansion extension. MI permits arbitrary subsets. Physical scales are separated annuli.

Put $z=\sum_i z_i$, $A=n_1+n_2+z$. The two centrally normalized plains have independent profiles and heights with polynomial costs.

**Theorem A.7.4** (Natural marked plain moment). *<a id="mf:plain"></a> The zero-slot assertion is the unconditional Theorem [A.5.1](#cf:mixed-plain-moment). For positive slots require $0<z_i\le\eta_{\rm mesh}$, with mesh chosen below before the slot system. Absorb zero-width bounded factors into fixed arithmetic data. Assume*

$$
7/10\le\kappa\le1,\qquad \beta\ge51/100,\qquad
2\beta-1\le\kappa.
$$

*The centrally normalized plain sums are*

$$
S_{k,i}(X)=X^{-1/2}\sum_{n}\psi_k(n)\mathbf1_{(n,R)=1}
 W_i(q_n/X),
$$

*with all integral ideals $n$ and the fixed bad-prime zeros understood. Then <a id="mf:eq:B3.40"></a>*

$$
\begin{array}{ll}
z=0:&\displaystyle
 \sum_{\psi_k^*\ne1}|S_k(Z^{n_1})S_k(Z^{n_2})|^2\ll Z^{M+\epsilon}
 \quad\text{for all bounded }n_1,n_2\ge0;\\[2mm]
z>0:&\displaystyle
 n_1+n_2+6\kappa z\le M
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \sum_{k\ {\rm eligible}}|S_k(Z^{n_1})S_k(Z^{n_2})\prod_iQ_{k,i}|^2
 \ll Z^{M+\epsilon}.
\end{array}\qquad\text{(MF3.40)}
$$

*A natural state has a whole-product presentation, complete natural zeros, fixed nonzero puncture and nonnegative smooth radial measure. Its width counts row-ball exponent plus displayed moving modulus before cancellation. Keep exactly nonzero rows not induced from $\mathfrak Q_0=Q\cap\mathfrak q_{\eta_0}$: fixed-inducing means a primitive finite Hecke character of conductor dividing $\mathfrak Q_0$ induces the actual row function with natural zeros. Deleting an extra puncture preserves this predicate, since additional zero Euler factors do not change the primitive inducing character. Initially,*

$$
\operatorname{initialKeep}(\eta,\mathfrak Q_0)
=\{k\in\mathcal O:k\ne0,\ \text{the natural presentation of }n\mapsto\eta(n)\chi_n(k)
\text{ is not induced from }\mathfrak Q_0\}.
$$

*The presentation retains fixed bad-prime zeros, primitive-conductor zeros, redundant moving zeros and row radical. Eligibility excludes every fixed-inducing presentation, not just principal characters or a chosen list.*

*Quantifier order: for a requested loss and bounded width/puncture/length ranges choose one mesh, uniformly for $\kappa\in[7/10,1]$, before arithmetic family, slot count, profiles or target height. After fixing a finite slot index type and common $W$, choose finite seminorms and height order before fixed character/ideal; their constant and eventual threshold precede live subset, slot characters, lengths, powers, heights, radial state and plain profiles. Positive slots allow a common whole-product norm power; independent plain twists are controlled by seminorms. Zero slots retain independent heights, all bounded lengths and every nonprincipal inducing character, including fixed-conductor rows.*

*Absorb fixed conductors in arbitrarily small width padding charged to the requested loss before the eventual threshold. Moving support remains width, never a profile seminorm.*

*The physical initial state has scale $U$, puncture one, fixed source $\eta$ and width $1+\delta$ once $q_{\mathfrak q_\eta}\le U^\delta$. Its measure is $1_{\operatorname{initialKeep}(\eta,\mathfrak Q_0)}(k)\Phi(q_k/U)$, $\Re\Phi\ge0$, with the literal natural plains and slots above, and relative character*

$$
\nu_i(n)=\theta_i(n)\overline{\eta_0(n)},
$$

*Lift $\theta_i$ from $(\mathcal O/\mathfrak M)^\times/H$; both factors retain their zeros. The prime pool is the identity ray class, cut at $\max(1,b)U^{z_i}$; $W$ selects its exact annulus. Physically $W=\overline{F.W}$, $\theta_i=1$, real power $33/50$, height $-\Im z_i$. Fixed-inducing sixth-power-free rows have prescribed good-prime valuations modulo six, hence bounded norm and leave a growing lower annulus.*

*The zero-slot endpoint restores fixed nonprincipal characters by masked lattice cancellation below. Width counts full moving support but excludes the puncture. For exceptional children fix a finite conjugation-stable $S$-supported group $\Theta$ containing fixed phases, inverses and $n\mapsto\chi_n(-1)$; it does not replace positive-slot eligibility. Taking $m=1,q=0,n_1=n_2$ gives MP in the positive family and MP0 for all nonprincipal zero-slot rows.*

*Proof.* **Extra masks.** A natural presentation has only primitive, redundant displayed, row and $S$ zeros. Delete its additional fixed $R$ mask to obtain $\psi_k^0$. Multiplicativity gives

<a id="mf:eq:B3.41"></a>

$$
S_{k,R}(X)=\sum_{d\mid R}\frac{\mu(d)\psi_k^0(d)}{\sqrt{q_d}}
 S_k^0(X/q_d),\qquad
Q_{k,i,R}=Q_{k,i}^0-Z^{-z_i/2}\sum_{p\mid R}\psi_k^0(p)\nu_i(p)W(q_p/Z^{z_i})(q_p/Z^{z_i})^{-\sigma_i+iv_i}.
\qquad\text{(MF3.41)}
$$

Total coefficient mass is $Z^{o(1)}$: $\prod_{p\mid R}(1-q_p^{-1/2})^{-1}\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon$, and a frozen slot has $Z^{-z_i/2}\ll q_p^{-1/2}$. Apply both identities and Minkowski. The affine length $A+(6\kappa-1)z$ decreases; if slots vanish the zero-slot row set contains the original eligible rows. Nonempty subunit plains clip by bounded dilation without exceeding old nonnegative lengths. Prove natural states uniformly, retaining this deletion at every child.

**Whole-factor reflection.** Use §[A.5.3](#cf:sec:D.3)'s natural reflection, with primitive $\psi_k^*$, conductor norm $Q_k$, $C_k=3Q_k/(2\pi)^2$ and redundant radical $R_{0,k}$.

<a id="mf:eq:B3.42"></a>

**(MF3.42)** is [(70)](#cf:eq:D.6), $C_kq_{R_{0,k}}\ll Z^M$, with the same full-support width.

Unit and $S$-valuations modulo six give finite ray sectors. For nonprincipal inducing characters, the central primitive reflection has scale $C_k/X$, unit root number and profile

<a id="mf:eq:B3.43"></a>

**(MF3.43)** is [(71)](#cf:eq:D.7)'s Mellin profile formula, $\widehat{W^\sharp}(s)=\widehat W(1-s)\Gamma(s)/\Gamma(1-s)$.

The proof in §[A.5.3](#cf:sec:D.3) substitutes the functional equation, sets $s\mapsto1-s$ and shifts without an $L$-pole. It gives bounded Euler derivatives at zero, rapid decay at infinity, and finite-seminorm/polynomial-height control by Stirling and $\widehat{Wy^{it}}(s)=\widehat W(s+it)$.

Deleting redundant factors before reflection and restoring geometrically gives exactly

<a id="mf:eq:B3.44"></a>

$$
S_k^0(X;W)=\varepsilon_k
 \sum_{d_0\mid R_{0,k}}\sum_{\operatorname{rad}(h_0)\mid R_{0,k}}
 \frac{\mu(d_0)\psi_k^*(d_0)\overline{\psi_k^*(h_0)}}{\sqrt{q_{d_0}q_{h_0}}}
 S_{\overline{\psi_k^0}}\!\left(\frac{C_kq_{d_0}}{Xq_{h_0}};W^\sharp\right).
\qquad\text{(MF3.44)}
$$

Its mass is $Z^{o(1)}$. Lower annuli of $W^\sharp$ have central coefficients $O(2^{-j/2})$; upper annuli decay arbitrarily rapidly. Discard above relative scale $Z^{\xi/2}$. A main scale $Y<Z^{-\xi}$ contributes $O_B(Y^{B-1/2})$ by counting and decay, for arbitrary fixed $B$. Handle row-dependent coefficients by mass, then scale suprema: integrate function and log-scale derivative over $O(\log Z)$ unit boxes, in two variables for two scales. The derivative is $-W/2-yW'$, so common-profile bounds apply. Conjugate the entire reflected factor to restore orientation. By [(MF3.42)](#mf:eq:B3.42), retained scales satisfy

<a id="mf:eq:B3.45"></a>

$$
n_{\rm ref}\le M-n+\xi.
\qquad\text{(MF3.45)}
$$

Absorb fixed endpoints and boxes in the final threshold; negative right side gives an empty range. Reflecting plains longer than $M/2$ reduces zero slots to

<a id="mf:eq:B3.46"></a>

**(MF3.46)** is the padded core [(72)](#cf:eq:D.8), with $2\xi\le\delta$: $n_i\le M/2+\xi$ and $A\le M+2\xi\le M+\delta$.

**Prime cost.** On eligible rows each slot remains nonprincipal after expanding the canonical identity-ray projector as the average of all fixed-quotient characters. Its product with $\nu_i=\theta_i\overline{\eta_0}$ has conductor dividing $Q_0$; a principal resulting row would therefore be induced from $Q_0$. Multiplication by such a fixed character preserves eligibility by inverse multiplication. The finite average changes only constants; no arbitrary-pool/profile extension follows. Under $2\beta-1\le\kappa$, move the smooth von Mangoldt contour to $s_\kappa+e$, $s_\kappa=(1+\kappa)/2$. There $|L'/L|\ll_e\log(Q(3+|t|)^2)$: on the zero-free disk centered at $2+it$ of radius $2-s_\kappa-e/4$, the Euler branch $g=\log L$ has $g(2+it)=O(1)$ and $\Re g\ll\log(Q(3+|t|)^2)$ by functional-equation strip growth. Borel--Carathéodory and then Cauchy's derivative bound on successively smaller disks containing $s_\kappa+e+it$ prove the claim; all gaps are fixed multiples of $e$. Prime powers of degree $\ge2$ cost $O(P^{1/2+\epsilon})$. Divide the annular weight by $\log(Py)$; redundant zeros delete only $O(\log Z)$ primes. Central normalization over the fixed slots gives

<a id="mf:eq:B3.47"></a>

$$
\left|\prod_iQ_{k,i}\right|^2
 \ll Z^{\kappa z+\epsilon_1}\,p_J(W)^b\langle\mathbf t\rangle^h.
\qquad\text{(MF3.47)}
$$

Contour displacement costs $2ez$, depending on total length, not slot count. Heights translate rapidly decreasing Mellin transforms; required derivative/height orders do not affect the exponent.

<a id="induction-order-and-the-centered-comparison"></a>

##### A.7.2.5 Induction order and the centered comparison

Choose floor $\rho>0$, step $\sigma>0$, padding $\delta\ll\min(\rho,\sigma)$ and bands of length $\sigma/4$. Use the zero-slot theorem first, then prove positive bands increasingly; within each band prove $A\le5M/6$ before centering. The zero-slot proof in Appendix A.5 supplies all lengths by reflection and padded-floor excess $\le\rho+\delta$. At $M\le\rho$, positive slots follow from it and [(MF3.47)](#mf:eq:B3.47), since

<a id="mf:eq:B3.48"></a>

$$
z\le M/(6\kappa),\qquad\kappa z\le M/6.
\qquad\text{(MF3.48)}
$$

Its additional terminal excess is at most $\rho/6$.

For $A>5M/6$, put $L=M/4$. If one plain is shorter than $L$, reflect the other; otherwise compare lengths $L,A-z-L$ with the same profiles, reflecting the larger comparison factor only to estimate the comparison. Since $q_\kappa=6\kappa-1>2$ and $z<(M/6)/q_\kappa<M/12$, both comparison lengths are $\ge L$. Reflection gives

<a id="mf:eq:B3.49"></a>

$$
A_{\rm comp}\le3M/2-A+2z+\xi,
\quad
\min\{5M/6-A_{\rm comp},\,M-A_{\rm comp}-q_\kappa z\}
\ge \mathfrak m(7/10)M-\xi,
\quad
\mathfrak m(\kappa)=\frac{2\kappa-1}{2(6\kappa-1)}.
\qquad\text{(MF3.49)}
$$

Indeed $t=M-A<M/6$, $z\le t/q_\kappa$ give margins $\ge M/3-t(1+2/q_\kappa)-\xi$ and $M/2-t(2+2/q_\kappa)-\xi$. Zero-slot comparison margin is $\ge M/6-\xi$. Choose $\xi<\rho\mathfrak m(7/10)/2$; each comparison then uses its already proved uncentered stage.

For both plains $\ge L$, put $X_i=Z^{n_i}$, $Y_1=Z^L$, $Y_2=X_1X_2/Y_1$. Subtract and retain the equal-product rectangles; after extracting $b_i$, the coefficient is

<a id="mf:eq:B3.50"></a>

**(MF3.50)** is the exact rectangle difference [(73)](#cf:eq:D.9), with $D_b=\mathcal D_b$ and $X_1X_2=Y_1Y_2$.

Use the same $b_i$ even when one rectangle vanishes. The comparison is already bounded on eligible rows; enlarge the positive norm of the **whole difference** to a smooth ball of all rows. In the uncentered range enlarge the original squared norm. Never Poisson-sum an eligibility indicator.

The invariant coefficient carried through the transformations is

<a id="mf:eq:B3.51"></a>

$$
\prod_{i\in I'}\nu_i(p_i)W(q_{p_i}/Z^{z_i})(q_{p_i}/Z^{z_i})^{-\sigma_i+iv_i}\,
D_b(l_1,l_2)\,\tau_1(u)q_u^{it}\,\mathbf1_{(u,R)=1}\mathbf1_{s\mid u},
\qquad u=\Bigl(\prod_{i\in I'}p_i\Bigr)l_1l_2,
\qquad\text{(MF3.51)}
$$

Here $s$ is fixed squarefree; uncentered inputs omit the second rectangle. The character, mask and norm power act on the entire product, preserving collisions by zero extension.

Use one aggregate tolerance. For fixed slot count $N$, let $H_N$ bound sums of absolute logarithmic endpoints of every slot/plain window and all finite later enlargements; set $\theta_N=H_N/\log Z$. Every slot subset's total ratio error is $\le\theta_N$. Extract plain powers using exact norms. Stage errors are $O(\theta_N)$ with numerical coefficient independent of $N$, not a loss per slot.

<a id="first-poisson-from-plain-products-to-gauss-polynomials"></a>

##### A.7.2.6 First Poisson: from plain products to Gauss polynomials

Set $H=Z^m$, $X=Z^A$. The zero-frequency argument of §[A.5.4](#cf:sec:D.4) applies unchanged to full products: zero net sextic exponents exclude multiplicity-one primes, giving a powerful ideal of norm $O(X^2)$, $O(X^{1+\epsilon})$ choices and divisor-bounded slot/plain allocations. Multiplying central $X^{-1}$ and row mean $\le H$ gives $O(Z^{m+o(1)})$.

For nonzero frequency write full products $Ca,Db$ with complete common support, $(a,b)=(ab,CD)=1$. Fix each common prime's full plain valuations and slot occurrences, extract them, freeze supplying slots and puncture every residual factor. Apply the same allocation to both rectangles; retain any scalar zero before enlargement.

Let $c,d,p$ be lengths of $C,D,\operatorname{rad}(CD)$. Let $r$ contain nonzero net exponents modulo six, length $R$, primitive character $\xi_r$; remaining common-mask divisor $e$ has $E\le p-R$. For allocated coefficients without the whole-product twist, set $\tau_C(a)=\tau(a)\chi_a(er)\overline{\xi_r(a)}$ and similarly for $\tau_D$. Poisson/CRT give, up to bounded frozen scalar,

<a id="mf:eq:B3.52"></a>

$$
\frac{H}{Xq_e\sqrt{q_r}}\sum_{h\ne0}\mathcal G_{\xi_r}(r,h)
\sum_{(a,b)=1}\frac{A_C(a)\overline{A_D(b)}}{\sqrt{q_aq_b}}
 \tau_C(a)\overline{\tau_D(b)}R(a,b)
 \mathcal G(a,h)\overline{\mathcal G(b,-h)}
 K_1\!\left(\frac{Hq_h}{q_eq_rq_aq_b}\right).
\qquad\text{(MF3.52)}
$$

Here $\mathcal G$ is the normalized sum with local values [(8)](#cf:eq:A.12), $|\mathcal G_{\xi_r}|\le1$. As in §[A.5.4](#cf:sec:D.4), Poisson after $k=ek'$ contributes $H/(q_eq_rq_aq_b)$; Gauss sums restore $\sqrt{q_rq_aq_b}$. CRT gives $\chi_a(br)\overline{\chi_b(ar)}\overline{\xi_r(ab)}$, whose $a,b$ ratio is $R(a,b)$ by reciprocity. New moving primes puncture every residual factor even if exponents cancel; their support and frequency lengths are

<a id="mf:eq:B3.53"></a>

**(MF3.53)** combines [(75)](#cf:eq:D.11) and [(76)](#cf:eq:D.12): $\widetilde q=q+R+E$, $K_0=2A-c-d+R+E-m$, with this chapter's full-product length $A=n_1+n_2+z$.

The first kernel's nominal frequency scale is $Z^{K_0}$.

For both Poisson transforms use one nonnegative norm-dyadic partition. In an outer sector retain whole weights meeting $q_h\le T_{\rm sec}Z^{\xi/2}$, $T_{\rm sec}$ the maximum nominal scale. For large $Z$, upper length is $K\le K_0+\delta_1$, $0\le\delta_1<\xi$; discarded genuine arguments are $\ge Z^{\xi/4}$, since full-product support costs $e^{2H_N}$. Apply [(MF3.4)](#mf:eq:B3.4) with raw bounds $|\mathcal G|\le\sqrt{q_a}$, $|F|\le q_uq_v$ and polynomial column/count cost, fixing that cost before decay order. Retained weights/full kernels are common to rectangles and independent of live columns.

On each dyad extend the separated Gauss bridge off coprimality using formal norms, original masks and bicharacter. Insert the complete $\sum_{s\mid(a,b)}\mu(s)$ before absolute values; let $s_0=\log_Zq_s$. Separate kernel/inverse roots in row and whole-product norms, adding an aggregate outer-ratio coordinate if needed. Each column receives one common norm power across its plains and rectangles. Then Cauchy and $|\mathcal G_{\xi_r}|\le1$ give

<a id="mf:eq:B3.54"></a>

**(MF3.54)** is [(77)](#cf:eq:D.13) with $\mathfrak g=\mathcal G$, this chapter's $A_C,\tau_C'$ and dyadic $h\ne0$ support. Its complete coefficient is [(MF3.51)](#mf:eq:B3.51).

The exchanged $D$ norm has the same form. Outside exponent is $m-A-R/2-E$; common-support and Möbius counts are $Z^{p+s_0+o(1)}$. Count radicals first, then bounded powers via $\#\{v:\operatorname{rad}v\mid c,q_v\le Z^T\}\le Z^{aT}\prod_{p\mid c}(1-q_p^{-a})^{-1}$ for small $a>0$; allocations cost divisors.

It suffices to prove

<a id="mf:eq:B3.55"></a>

**(MF3.55)** is the target bound [(78)](#cf:eq:D.14), here with loss $\epsilon_G$: $\mathcal N_C\ll Z^{A-c+\widetilde q+B_c-s_0+\epsilon_G}$, $B_c=(3c-5d-R)_+/6$.

Its exchanged counterpart and outside factors have exponent $M+\{B_c+B_d-(c+d-2p-R)\}/2$. The local comparison is

<a id="mf:eq:B3.56"></a>

$$
B_c+B_d\le c+d-2p-R.
\qquad\text{(MF3.56)}
$$

This is the primewise inequality proved after [(79)](#cf:eq:D.15), with identical multiplicities and $r_p=1_{6\nmid i-j}$; slot occurrences are already included in those multiplicities.

<a id="enlarging-a-gauss-row-norm"></a>

##### A.7.2.7 Enlarging a Gauss-row norm

Extract length $w$ from [(MF3.54)](#mf:eq:B3.54), adding moving radical $w_o\le w$ with squared scalar $Z^{-w_o}$. Put $a_0=A-c-w$; [(MF3.55)](#mf:eq:B3.55) permits the unweighted norm exponent

<a id="mf:eq:B3.57"></a>

$$
\Lambda_c=a_0+\widetilde q+w_o+w+B_c-s_0+\epsilon_G.
\qquad\text{(MF3.57)}
$$

Define $J=d-c+(K_0-K)-2w+w_o$, $J_+=\max(J,0)$. With zero slots take $w=w_o=0$, $\ell=0$, and enlarge the row norm to a smooth ball of length $K+g$, $g=J_++\sigma$.

For positive slots choose $\ell_* =\sigma/3$, mesh $<\sigma/6$, and pool $\mathcal P=\{p:Z^{\ell_*}/2<q_p\le Z^{\ell_*},p\notin S\}$. The fixed-field prime ideal theorem gives $|\mathcal P|=Z^{\ell_*+o(1)}$. For large $Z$ it avoids all live slots. For each $h\ne0$, delete the $O(\log Z)$ primes dividing $h,s$ or frozen supports.

For $p\nmid uh$, the prime-power Gauss identities [(8)](#cf:eq:A.12) and CRT give

<a id="mf:eq:B3.58"></a>

$$
\mathcal G(p^iu,h)=R(p,u)^i\chi_p(u)^{2i}\mathcal G(p^i,h)\mathcal G(u,h),
\qquad\mathcal G(u,hp^6)=\mathcal G(u,h).
\qquad\text{(MF3.58)}
$$

Replacing $h$ by $hp^6$ changes only valuations $i=1,6,7$. Assign powers to the two plains (pool and slots are disjoint), puncturing the residual product and updating both rectangles. Jensen over eligible primes and these finite allocations bounds the original square by amplified square and extracted errors. Each output $hp^6$ has boundedly many representations, since pool length is fixed positive and output length bounded; density is $Z^{-\ell_*+o(1)}$. Take $\ell=\ell_*$, $g=J_++2\sigma$, enclosing amplified rows since $6\ell_*=2\sigma$.

The extracted alternatives are exactly:

| Column valuation $i$ | Squared extraction coefficient | $w$       | $w_o$    |
|:---------------------|:-------------------------------|:----------|:---------|
| 1                    | $q_p^{-1}$                     | $\ell_p$  | $\ell_p$ |
| 6                    | $(1-q_p^{-1})^2$               | $6\ell_p$ | 0        |
| 7                    | $q_p^{-1}$                     | $7\ell_p$ | $\ell_p$ |

Here $\ell_p=\log_Zq_p\in[\sigma/6,\sigma/3]$. At valuation six, $\chi_p(u)^{12}$ is the existing common puncture; retain $R(p,u)^6$. Valuations one/seven retain a moving character counted in $w_o$. Freeze each error's $p$, take $\ell=0$, $g=J_++\sigma$, and transform without re-amplifying. The normalized prime average has no extra count. Always

<a id="mf:eq:B3.59"></a>

$$
0\le w_o\le w\le7\sigma/3.
\qquad\text{(MF3.59)}
$$

Coefficient [(MF3.51)](#mf:eq:B3.51), multiplied by $\mathcal G(u,h)$, retains its difference, puncture and $s$-divisibility.

Add zero only at the final smooth ball, never amplify it. By [(8)](#cf:eq:A.12), $\mathcal G(u,0)$ vanishes unless $u$ is sixth-power, and is $\le\sqrt{q_u}$. For nonempty upper bound $Y=e^{H_N}Z^{a_0}$ and $s\mid u$, $q_s^6\le Y$. Counting $O(Y^{1/6})$ columns gives normalized square $Z^{-a_0}Y^{4/3+o(1)}\le Z^{a_0-s_0+2\theta_N+o(1)}$, within [(MF3.57)](#mf:eq:B3.57).

<a id="second-transform-and-the-actual-children"></a>

##### A.7.2.8 Second transform and the actual children

Restore live slot sums before squaring. If $B(u)$ is the complete convolution coefficient, with $s\mid u$, [(10)](#cf:eq:A.14) gives

<a id="mf:eq:B3.60"></a>

$$
\begin{aligned}
&Z^{-\ell}\sum_h\Phi_2(q_h/Z^{K+g})
 \left|Z^{-a_0/2}\sum_u B(u)\tau_1(u)q_u^{it}\mathcal G(u,h)\right|^2
\\
&\quad=Z^{K+g-\ell-a_0}\sum_{u,v}
 \frac{B(u)\overline{B(v)}\tau_1(u)\overline{\tau_1(v)}q_u^{it}q_v^{-it}}
      {\sqrt{q_uq_v}}
\\
&\qquad{}\times\sum_jF(u,v;j)K_2\!\left(\frac{Z^{K+g}q_j}{q_uq_v}\right).
\end{aligned}
\qquad\text{(MF3.60)}
$$

At $j=0$, [(11)](#cf:eq:A.15) forces $u=v$ and $F(u,u;0)=\phi(u)\le q_u$. There are $O(Z^{a_0-s_0+\theta_N})$ supported multiples of $s$, giving exponent $K+g-\ell-s_0+\theta_N+o(1)$ and nominal excess

<a id="mf:eq:B3.61"></a>

$$
(A-M)-d-(K_0-K)-w_o-B_c+g-\ell
\le A-M+5\sigma/3+\delta_1.
\qquad\text{(MF3.61)}
$$

If $J\ge0$, $-d-(K_0-K)-w_o+J_+=-c-2w$; otherwise it is $\le\delta_1$. The largest increment is $2\sigma-\ell_*=5\sigma/3$, a terminal loss, plus $\delta$ in the zero-slot padded core.

Localize genuine nonzero $j$ at nominal $Z^{2a_0-K-g}$ by the whole-dyad rule before common extraction $u=D_2a,v=E_2b$. Put

$$
c_2=\log_Zq_{D_2},\quad d_2=\log_Zq_{E_2},\quad b_2=(c_2+d_2)/2,
\quad p_2=\log_Zq_{\operatorname{rad}(D_2E_2)},\quad G_c=(D_2,E_2),\quad g_2=\log_Zq_{G_c}.
$$

Apply the complete-support factorization

<a id="mf:eq:B3.62"></a>

**(MF3.62)** is [(12)](#cf:eq:A.16), with $(D,E)=(D_2,E_2)$ and the same residual $a,b,j$.

It holds only for $(a,b)=(ab,D_2E_2)=1$, allowing arbitrary powers and slot/plain coincidences. Extracted primes puncture residual factors; freeze supplying slots. A plain $p^5$ and slot $p$ therefore retain $\chi_p(j)^6$, not one.

Equations [(13)](#cf:eq:A.17)--[(14)](#cf:eq:A.18) force $G_c\mid j$. At equal non-six-divisible multiplicities split divided frequency into units/nonunits, radical lengths $t_2,V$ and nonunit radical $V_{\rm id}$. Set $j=G_cV_{\rm id}h'$. Extend $1_{\rm part}F(D_2,E_2;G_cV_{\rm id}h')/Z^{g_2-t_2}$ by zero off its partition; it has modulus $\le1$ by

| Common multiplicities and divided frequency | Bound     |
|:--------------------------------------------|:----------|
| $i=i,\ 6\nmid i$, unit                      | $P^{i-1}$ |
| $i=i,\ 6\nmid i$, nonunit                   | $P^i$     |
| $i=i,\ 6\mid i$, either                     | $P^i$     |
| $i>j_0,\ 6\mid j_0$, unit                   | $P^{j_0}$ |

Other unequal cases vanish. In $v=G_cV_{\rm id}$, reduce valuations modulo six: nonzero residues retain moving characters, zeros the existing puncture. Active primes lie in $t_2+V$. Factor only $\chi_n(v)$, preserving varying-row zeros of $\chi_n(h')$. Thus

<a id="mf:eq:B3.63"></a>

$$
m'=2a_0-K-g-g_2-V,\quad q'=\widetilde q+w_o+t_2+V,
\qquad M'=m'+q'=M+J-g-g_2+t_2\le M-\sigma.
\qquad\text{(MF3.63)}
$$

The pulled-back retained weight has $q_{h'}\le Z^{m'+\delta_2}$, $0\le\delta_2<\xi$. Nonempty ranges have $m'+\delta_2\ge0$; declare $m'_{\rm act}=m'+\delta_2$, $M'_{\rm act}=M'+\delta_2$. Extend weight and partition scalar by zero across this ball, keeping them signed.

The condition $s\mid u,v$ forces $s$ into the common radical, so labels cost $Z^{p_2-s_0+o(1)}$. The ledger is

| Factor                                     | Exponent  |
|:-------------------------------------------|:----------|
| Original squared central normalization     | $-a_0$    |
| Poisson factor and inverse roots           | $K+g-a_0$ |
| Amplifier density                          | $-\ell$   |
| Common-support count with fixed $s$        | $p_2-s_0$ |
| Common correlation                         | $g_2-t_2$ |
| Conversion to normalized residual products | $a_0-b_2$ |

Subtracting this sum from [(MF3.57)](#mf:eq:B3.57) leaves the inner allowance

<a id="mf:eq:B3.64"></a>

$$
M'+\Delta,\qquad \Delta=b_2-p_2+w+B_c+\ell\ge w+\ell.
\qquad\text{(MF3.64)}
$$

The last inequality uses $b_2\ge p_2$.

Extend [(MF3.62)](#mf:eq:B3.62)'s right side to individually allowed pairs, retaining original common-support masks, formal full norms, roots, kernel and pulled-back row weight. Insert full $\sum_{t\mid(a,b)}\mu(t)$; only this sum restores the genuine correlation. Its artificial common primes do not enter $D_2,E_2$ or frequency restrictions. Separate in row/whole-product norms, then allocate primes of $t$ by

<a id="mf:eq:B3.65"></a>

$$
\mathbf1_{p\mid\prod_i n_i}
=\sum_{\varnothing\ne J}(-1)^{|J|+1}\prod_{i\in J}\mathbf1_{p\mid n_i},
\qquad\text{(MF3.65)}
$$

Factors are the two plains and live slots. Selected plains become $n_i=pl_i$ without residual puncture, dividing corresponding scales in both rectangles by $q_p$. Selected slots freeze; selecting distinct primes in one prime slot vanishes. Quotients may retain $p$.

Thus each child retains a whole-product character, common mask and norm power across plains/rectangles; live slots keep original $\nu_i$ without Gauss factors. Sides may have different whole-product norm powers, but their fixed-inducing predicates agree: conjugation and multiplication by fixed-modulus characters preserve conductor divisibility, including unchanged redundant zeros. At each fixed-modulus stage enlarge $\Theta$ to all primitive characters dividing that modulus plus the finitely many fixed ray twists; it remains finite. On an exceptional row inducing $\vartheta$, freeze live slots to obtain

<a id="mf:eq:B3.66"></a>

**(MF3.66)** is the exceptional rectangle coefficient [(91)](#cf:eq:D.27), with $D_b=\mathcal D_b$, this child's $\vartheta,t$, and its complete squarefree mask $R_*$.

The polynomial-size $R_*$ is common to both variables/rectangles. Retain extracted row scalars, including zeros, until positive or absolute estimation.

**Extraction normalization.** Put $\alpha_1=a_0-c_2$, $\alpha_2=a_0-d_2$. Let $F_j$ be genuinely frozen entrance slots and $I_j$ the live slots before final allocation. Their pre-allocation plain product $T_j$ satisfies $T_j\prod_{i\in I_j}Z^{z_i}=Z^{\alpha_j+e_j}$, $e_j=\sum_{i\in F_j}\log_Z(q_{p_i}/Z^{z_i})$. Let $d_{j,i}$ be final products selected in plain $i$, $J_j\subset I_j$ newly frozen slots, and put

$$
a_{j,i}=\log_Zq_{d_{j,i}},\quad
r_j=a_{j,1}+a_{j,2}+\sum_{i\in J_j}z_i,\quad
\omega_j=\sum_{i\in J_j}\log_Z(q_{p_i}/Z^{z_i}).
$$

Use lower-endpoint dyads $Z^{t_-}\le q_t<2Z^{t_-}$. Every selected product is divisible by $t$, so

<a id="mf:eq:B3.67"></a>

$$
r_j+\omega_j\ge t_-,\qquad |\omega_j|\le\theta_N,
\qquad |e_j+\omega_j|\le\theta_N.
\qquad\text{(MF3.67)}
$$

The last bound uses disjoint subsets of current entrance slots, without recounting ancestors. Raw child normalizer is $Z^{-(\alpha_j-r_j)/2}$, extraction scalar $Z^{-r_j/2}$, formal scale product $Z^{\alpha_j+e_j-r_j}$. Signed raw rectangles may have negative individual lengths.

**Child eligibility.** Split by the same fixed-inducing predicate with complete source masks. On kept rows, [(MF3.62)](#mf:eq:B3.62)--[(MF3.65)](#mf:eq:B3.65) give exactly the whole-product character in nonzero $h'$ with pulled-back radial weight. Frozen zeros belong to its natural presentation; the extra common mask is row-fixed. Delete it by [(MF3.41)](#mf:eq:B3.41), obtaining a natural state of width $M'_{\rm act}$ with precisely the non-fixed-inducing keep set. Each plain and surviving slot has this same character/mask, and Fourier density precedes live labels/rows. Hence the smaller-width theorem applies to the actual positive norm; complementary fixed-inducing rows remain for separate evaluation.

**Nonexceptional children.** Use Cauchy, then split centered children into rectangles; only now bound common weights/scalars by one and enlarge the ball. For pre-allocation plain lengths $x_i$ and post-lengths $y_i=x_i-a_{j,i}$, put $\pi_0=\sum(-x_i)_+$, $\pi=\sum(-y_i)_+$. Omit rectangles whose plain upper support is below the first ideal; otherwise $0\le\pi_0\le\pi\le\theta_N$. The clipped reduction and total are

<a id="mf:eq:B3.68"></a>

$$
r_{{\rm clip},j}=r_j-(\pi-\pi_0)\ge0,\qquad
A_{{\rm clip},j}=\alpha_j+e_j-r_j+\pi,
\qquad\text{(MF3.68)}
$$

and its exact scalar relative to the pre-normalizer is $Z^{(-r_{{\rm clip},j}+e_j+\pi_0)/2}$. For a paired divisor dyad, the count and both scalars satisfy

<a id="mf:eq:B3.69"></a>

$$
t_--\frac{r_{{\rm clip},1}+r_{{\rm clip},2}}2
 +\frac{e_1+\pi_{0,1}+e_2+\pi_{0,2}}2\le2\theta_N.
\qquad\text{(MF3.69)}
$$

Substitute [(MF3.68)](#mf:eq:B3.68) and [(MF3.67)](#mf:eq:B3.67); there are at most four rectangle pairs. Do not assign a common clipped reduction to a signed difference.

With no surviving slot, [(MF3.69)](#mf:eq:B3.69) and the smaller-width zero-slot bound fit [(MF3.64)](#mf:eq:B3.64), $\Delta\ge0$. Otherwise side one's pre-allocation total is $A'=A-c-w-c_2$, and

<a id="mf:eq:B3.70"></a>

$$
(A'-M')-(A-M)
=g+w-d-c_2-(K_0-K)-w_o+g_2-t_2
\le6(w+\ell)+\delta_1.
\qquad\text{(MF3.70)}
$$

Use $g_2-t_2\le c_2$. In the amplified norm, $g\le d+(K_0-K)+6\ell+\delta_1$; in errors, $g\le d+(K_0-K)+\sigma+\delta_1$ and the extraction table gives $w-w_o+\sigma\le6w$. Exchange $c_2,d_2$ for the other side.

Delete extra masks. For each actual natural child with live slots put $F_{\rm act}=(A_{\rm act}-M'_{\rm act}+(6\kappa-1)z_{\rm act})_+$. Equations [(MF3.68)](#mf:eq:B3.68)--[(MF3.70)](#mf:eq:B3.70), parent capacity and aggregate endpoint bound give

<a id="mf:eq:B3.71"></a>

$$
F_{\rm act}\le6(w+\ell)+\delta_1+2\theta_N.
\qquad\text{(MF3.71)}
$$

Use [(MF3.47)](#mf:eq:B3.47) to remove whole slots until defect vanishes or no slot remains. A length-$d$ slot releases $6\kappa d$ capacity and costs $\kappa d$ energy. A greedy prefix overshoots by at most one mesh, so

<a id="mf:eq:B3.72"></a>

$$
\kappa d_z\le F_{\rm act}/6+\kappa\eta_{\rm mesh}
\le\Delta+\delta_1/6+\theta_N/3+\eta_{\rm mesh}.
\qquad\text{(MF3.72)}
$$

If slots remain use the smaller-width positive theorem; otherwise use unrestricted zero-slot bounds. Equations [(MF3.69)](#mf:eq:B3.69), [(MF3.72)](#mf:eq:B3.72) and $M'_{\rm act}-M'=\delta_2$ give edge cost $\le\delta_2+\delta_1/6+7\theta_N/3+\eta_{\rm mesh}$ plus its small-power share. Cauchy averages costs, including the single mesh.

<a id="fixed-character-rows-and-rectangle-cancellation"></a>

##### A.7.2.9 Fixed-character rows and rectangle cancellation

**Exceptional count.** Genuine second allocations avoid old moving support by original zeros, so no old character cancels $G_cV_{\rm id}$ there. For nonunit common multiplicity-one primes of radical length $v_1$, put $f=2v_1$. Their fixed row valuation is two; unramified fixed-modulus induction forces $v_p(h')\equiv4\pmod6$. More generally each good prime has a prescribed valuation class modulo six, zero outside frozen support. Units and $S$-valuations give finitely many sectors, with sixth powers free. Thus $(h')=h_0v^6$, $h_0$ fixed sixth-power-free, $q_{h_0}\ge Z^{4v_1}=Z^{2f}$. Counting gives $(m'_{\rm act}-2f)/6$; we use only

<a id="mf:eq:B3.73"></a>

$$
\#\{h'\text{ exceptional}:q_{h'}\ll Z^{m'_{\rm act}}\}
\ll Z^{(m'-f)/6+\delta_2/6+o(1)}.
\qquad\text{(MF3.73)}
$$

Below the forced initial norm the range is empty up to fixed endpoints. This counts principal and all other fixed-inducing rows, including positively added partition rows; no $t_2$ saving is used.

After full Möbius allocation, side $j$'s normalized absolute volume is $O(Z^{(\alpha_j-r_j)/2+e_j})$. Both extraction scalars and divisor count give paired volume $\le Z^{a_0-b_2+2\theta_N+o(1)}$ by [(MF3.67)](#mf:eq:B3.67), since $t_--r_1-r_2\le\omega_2$, $r_1\ge0$. Including the exceptional count, its nominal excess is

<a id="mf:eq:B3.74"></a>

$$
\frac{m'-f}{6}+a_0-b_2-(M'+\Delta)
=A-\frac56M-F_1-F_2,
\qquad\text{(MF3.74)}
$$

where

<a id="mf:eq:B3.75"></a>

$$
\begin{aligned}
F_1&=c/6+5\{d+(K_0-K)\}/6+w/3+\widetilde q/6+w_o+B_c-5g/6+\ell,\\
F_2&=2b_2-5g_2/6-p_2+t_2+V/6+f/6.
\end{aligned}\qquad\text{(MF3.75)}
$$

These expressions obey

<a id="mf:eq:B3.76"></a>

$$
F_1\ge\frac23(c+w)-3\sigma-5\delta_1/6,
\qquad F_2\ge\frac23b_2.
\qquad\text{(MF3.76)}
$$

Initially take $g=J_+$, $\ell=0$, $D_0=d+K_0-K$. For $J\ge0$, $F_1=c+2w+\widetilde q/6+w_o/6+B_c$. Otherwise $\widetilde q\ge R$ gives $B_c+\widetilde q/6\ge(3c-5D_0)_+/6-5\delta_1/6$, hence $F_1\ge2(c+w)/3-w/3-5\delta_1/6$. Restoring $g\le J_++2\sigma$, $\ell\ge0$, $w\le7\sigma/3$ costs $<3\sigma$. For $F_2$ use the exact local table of §[A.5.6](#cf:sec:D.6), with $j=j_0$:

The four pairs $(F_2,b_2)$ are $(7i/6,i)$, $((7i-5)/6+1_{i=1}/3,i)$, $(7i/6-1,i)$, and $(i+j_0/6-1,(i+j_0)/2)$ for, respectively, equal non-six-divisible/unit, equal non-six-divisible/nonunit, equal six-divisible, and unequal $i>j_0$, $6\mid j_0$/unit cases.

Each first entry is $\ge2/3$ of the second; at nonunit $i=1$, $f/6$ gives equality. Thus [(MF3.76)](#mf:eq:B3.76) holds and uncentered $A\le5M/6$ costs at most $3\sigma+O(\xi+\theta_N)$, validating comparisons.

**Masked lattice cancellation.** Apply §[A.5.1](#cf:sec:D.1) to fixed $\vartheta\in\Theta$, polynomial squarefree $R_*$, annular $W_i$ and common real $t$.

<a id="mf:eq:B3.77"></a>

**(MF3.77)** is [(65)](#cf:eq:D.1), with the same $L_i(X,t)$, $c_{\vartheta,R_*}$ and $I_i(t)$, loss $\epsilon_1$ and $\langle t\rangle=1+|t|$. It holds uniformly for $X>0$.

Its proof there is fixed-lattice Poisson followed by complete mask inversion; in particular $c_{\vartheta,R_*}=c_\vartheta\sum_{d\mid R_*}\mu(d)\vartheta(d)/q_d$. Primary/$S$ restrictions are fixed lattice classes, and already excluded primes can be omitted. Thus it applies to every retained exceptional mask.

For $U_i=X_i/q_{b_i}$, $V_i=Y_i/q_{b_i}$, $T=U_1U_2=V_1V_2$, the sum of [(MF3.66)](#mf:eq:B3.66) is the difference of the two $L_1L_2$ products. If all four scales are $\ge Z^r$, $r\ge0$, then

<a id="mf:eq:B3.78"></a>

**(MF3.78)** is the normalized rectangle bound [(66)](#cf:eq:D.2), with these $U_i,V_i,T$, loss $\epsilon_1$ and height factor $\langle t\rangle^{2J}$.

The same row, mask and norm power make main terms equal. Without a nonnegative lower scale use the all-scale volume $O(T^{1/2})$.

For centered exceptional children, pre-allocation lower lengths are $L-c-w-c_2$ and $L-c-w-d_2$. Put $r=(L-c-w-\min(c_2,d_2))_+$ and call the saving side one. Final extraction removes at most $r_1$ from either plain: use [(MF3.78)](#mf:eq:B3.78) if $r_1<r$, otherwise volume. Preserve raw equal-product scales without clipping. Exactly,

<a id="mf:eq:B3.79"></a>

$$
t_--r_1-r_2-(r-r_1)_+
=(t_--r_2)-\max(r,r_1)\le\omega_2-r.
\qquad\text{(MF3.79)}
$$

Paired volume is therefore $Z^{a_0-b_2-r+2\theta_N+o(1)}$, uniformly in live slots. Their labels never entered Fourier density; sum them now by volume with [(MF3.67)](#mf:eq:B3.67)'s normalization.

Put $v=c+w+\min(c_2,d_2)$. From [(MF3.76)](#mf:eq:B3.76), $F_1+F_2\ge2v/3-3\sigma-5\delta_1/6$. The remaining centered exceptional deficit is bounded by

<a id="mf:eq:B3.80"></a>

$$
A-5M/6-2v/3-(L-v)_+\le(A-M)_+,
\qquad L=M/4.
\qquad\text{(MF3.80)}
$$

As in §[A.5.6](#cf:sec:D.6), the maximum occurs at $v=L$ and equals $A-M$. Positive slots have $A\le M$, zero-slot padding $A\le M+\delta$; exceptional terminal cost is $\le3\sigma+\delta$, with reserved support/frequency errors.

##### A.7.2.10 Closure and uniform common mesh

Strict nominal widths decrease by $\sigma$. Actual enclosure/support corrections cost $C_*\xi$ for numerical $C_*$ independent of slot count: they involve one aggregate $\theta_N$, two frequency enclosures, at most two plain clippings and finitely many aggregate lengths in [(MF3.53)](#mf:eq:B3.53)--[(MF3.80)](#mf:eq:B3.80). Ledgers are affine or positive-part affine; positive capacity varies by at most $|\Delta M|+|\Delta A|+5|\Delta z|$, since $6\kappa-1\le5$. Greedy removal charges one mesh.

Choose $\rho,\sigma,\delta$ from the bounded real ranges and final $\epsilon$, with $\delta\ll\min(\rho,\sigma)$, so that

$$
T_{\rm term}:=\rho+\delta+\rho/6+3\sigma+5\sigma/3<\epsilon/4.
$$

Put $D=2+\lceil2M_{\max}/\sigma\rceil$, and, still before specifying the fixed slot system, choose

<a id="mf:eq:B3.81"></a>

$$
\xi<\min\{\delta/2,\rho\mathfrak m(7/10)/2,\sigma/(4C_*),
                   \epsilon/(16C_*D)\},\qquad
\eta_{\rm mesh}<\min\{\sigma/6,\epsilon/(16C_*D)\},\qquad
\epsilon_0<\epsilon/(16C_*D).
\qquad\text{(MF3.81)}
$$

These preserve comparison margins, padding and width decrease $\ge\sigma/2$. Each strict child leaves its band; depth is $\le D-2$. Same-band comparisons use earlier uncentered stages, each plain reflects at most once before centering, and errors are not re-amplified. Thus the induction is acyclic.

Now fix arithmetic data, profiles and finite slot count, then $H_N$ and boxes through depth $D$. Eventually $\theta_N\ll\xi$, tails satisfy whole-dyad inclusions and pool avoids slots. Allocate stage losses within $\epsilon_0$: e.g. at most $N+2$ mask masses get $\epsilon_0/(10(N+2))$ each; use global divisor bounds $C_N^{\omega(v)},d_{N+2}(v)^C\ll_{N,C,a}q_v^a$ for one small $a$. Prime displacement costs $2ez$, independent of slot count. These affect constants, not the already chosen mesh.

With $d$ strict calls remaining allow $E_d=T_{\rm term}+(d+1)C_*(\eta_{\rm mesh}+\xi+\epsilon_0)$. Floor, diagonal and exception fit $E_0$; [(MF3.69)](#mf:eq:B3.69)--[(MF3.72)](#mf:eq:B3.72) bound a strict edge by its child plus one allowance, including comparisons/reflection masses. Cauchy averages and triangle takes maxima, so terminal loss occurs once. Equation [(MF3.81)](#mf:eq:B3.81) gives $E_{D-2}<\epsilon$, simultaneously for every surviving slot subset.

Choose raw tails and finite profile/height orders backwards, then one final threshold for tails, endpoints and logarithms. Child extra masks lie on frozen columns or a frozen amplifier prime, hence stay polynomial through finite depth. Exceptional masks also include row radicals and are covered uniformly by [(MF3.77)](#mf:eq:B3.77). All moving support, including canceled powers, remains explicit. This proves [(MF3.40)](#mf:eq:B3.40).

The original $3/4\le\kappa\le1$ and refined $7/10\le\kappa\le3/4$ ranges are separate applications of this same descent. Arithmetic and exceptional estimates are $\kappa$-independent. Its only uses are prime bound [(MF3.47)](#mf:eq:B3.47), requiring $2\beta-1\le\kappa$; comparison [(MF3.49)](#mf:eq:B3.49), where $\mathfrak m'(\kappa)=2/(6\kappa-1)^2>0$ gives minimum $\mathfrak m(7/10)$; and removal [(MF3.72)](#mf:eq:B3.72), whose cost/capacity is $1/6$. Bounds $6\kappa-1\le5$, $\kappa\le1$ make the mesh uniform. In the original contradiction, $7/8<\beta\le1$ permits $\kappa=2\beta-1=3/4+2(\beta-7/8)$ without an improved zero-free assumption.

For completeness, fixed nonprincipal zero-slot rows are also restored directly. For a primitive nonprincipal $\vartheta$ of the fixed modulus, orthogonality gives $c_\vartheta=0$, hence $c_{\vartheta,R_*}=0$ in [(MF3.77)](#mf:eq:B3.77). Each normalized nonempty $X\ge1$ plain is $O(Z^{\epsilon_1}X^{-1/2}\langle t\rangle^J)$; bounded subunit scales use volume. Prescribed valuations modulo six give $O(Z^{m/6+\epsilon_1})$ rows by the exceptional parameterization without forced-prime savings. The fixed family is finite, so multiplying and choosing small $\epsilon_1$ restores all such rows within $Z^{M+\epsilon}$, with independent heights and common masks. Principal inducing characters remain excluded. ◻

#### A.7.3 The two incumbent ranges and the physical interfaces

**Proposition A.7.5** (Original bootstrap moment). *<a id="mf:plain-original-bootstrap"></a> Under the natural family, masks, ray coefficients, individual slot bound $0<z_i\le\eta_{\rm mesh}$ and quantifier order of Theorem [A.7.4](#mf:plain), suppose $\beta\ge51/100$, $3/4\le\kappa\le1$ and $2\beta-1\le\kappa$. Then the positive moment holds whenever $n_1+n_2+6\kappa z\le M$; the zero-slot assertion is unconditional. In particular the choice $\kappa=2\beta-1$ is valid in the original contradiction range $7/8<\beta\le1$.*

*Proof.* Restrict Theorem [A.7.4](#mf:plain) to $[3/4,1]$. The common proof above gives comparison margin $\mathfrak m(3/4)M=M/14$, removal ratio $1/6$ and total error $E_{D-2}<\epsilon$ by [(MF3.81)](#mf:eq:B3.81), with one terminal allowance. Its actual row presentation requires only $2\beta-1\le\kappa$, independently of an improved zero-free conclusion. ◻

**Proposition A.7.6** (Refined incumbent moment). *<a id="mf:plain-refined"></a> The same natural moment, with each active $0<z_i\le\eta_{\rm mesh}$, is valid for $7/10\le\kappa\le3/4$, $\beta\ge51/100$ and $2\beta-1\le\kappa$, with its mesh chosen uniformly in this interval before the slot system, profiles and target height.*

*Proof.* Restrict the same proof to $[7/10,3/4]$: $6\kappa-1\le7/2$, margin $\ge\mathfrak m(7/10)M>0$, removal ratio $1/6$. Equation [(MF3.81)](#mf:eq:B3.81) preserves the stated quantifier order. This is a separate refinement of the original range. ◻

###### Literal initial fields and positivity.

For fixed source $\eta$, take scale $U$, puncture one, width $1+\delta$ once $q_{\mathfrak q_\eta}\le U^\delta$, and keep set $\operatorname{initialKeep}(\eta,\mathfrak Q_0)$. At $X_1=X_2=U^m$, Theorem [A.7.4](#mf:plain) gives

$$
\sum_k\mathbf1_{\operatorname{initialKeep}(\eta,\mathfrak Q_0)}(k)
 \Re\Phi(q_k/U)\,|S_k(U^m)^2\prod_{i\in I}Q_{k,i}|^2
\ll \mathcal P_J(W_1,W_2)^{2}\mathcal D_J(\Phi)
 (1+|t_1|+|t_2|+\max_i|v_i|)^h U^{1+\delta+\epsilon}
$$

provided $2m+6\kappa\sum_{i\in I}z_i\le1$ and $0<z_i\le\eta_{\rm mesh}$. Here $\mathcal P_J$ uses finitely many plain Euler seminorms (common slot profile fixed in the constant); $\mathcal D_J$ controls the nonnegative radial Schwartz profile. Choose $J,h$ before heights and live subset. Absorb $\delta$ and local loss into the requested loss. This physical field is $|S|^4|\prod Q_i|^2$.

Theorem [A.7.3](#mf:inverse) admits literal relative-character slot coefficients, fixed ray Fourier coefficients and common character conjugation, all bounded and row-independent. Shared inverse primes are allocated by [(MF3.32)](#mf:eq:B3.32). At $m=1$ the gates are $r+2z<1$, $2r+8z<3$. For finitely many profiles/derivatives take maximum orders/thresholds and union seminorms. All energies use nonnegative measures and squared moduli, so retained subfamilies decrease them. Signed Möbius coefficients remain until their full identity is restored.

<a id="every-rescaled-completed-term."></a>

###### Every rescaled completed term.

Theorem [A.7.1](#mf:marked-energy) covers all original slot subsets. Priority allocation to frozen products preserves row-independent surviving coefficients, retaining exact central scalars and tuple counts outside. For physical rescaling by subset width $d$,

$$
M'=M-2d,\qquad z'=\ell-d,\qquad N'=1+\ell-d.
$$

If $M+\ell\le1$, then $M'+2z'\le N'$ for every such subset. The energy exponent is therefore $M'+(1+3\ell-2M+d)_+/4+\epsilon$. After the physical Cauchy square root, its exact compensator and assigned tuple mass give the additional exponent

$$
-d+\frac18(1+3\ell-2M+d)_+.
$$

Its slopes are $-1,-7/8$, so the maximum is $d=0$; this pays every rescaled term with its actual outside coefficient. Individual energies need not be $\le Z^{M'}$.

**Lemma A.7.7** (Actual finite source rows). *<a id="mf:finite-source-field"></a> Let $\mathcal R$ be a finite row family with an injective map $\iota:\mathcal R\longrightarrow\mathcal O$. Suppose that, for each $u\in\mathcal R$, its displayed character $\chi_u$ agrees at every ideal with the natural function $n\mapsto\eta(n)\chi_n(\iota(u))$, including the fixed bad-prime zero mask. Suppose also that $\iota(u)\in\operatorname{initialKeep}(\eta,\mathfrak Q_0)$ and $q_{\iota(u)}\le U$. Choose a fixed smooth radial majorant $\Phi\ge0$ with $\Phi\ge1$ on $[0,1]$. Then the unweighted finite-row plain times marked-prime energy is at most the initial-state positive energy in Theorem [A.7.4](#mf:plain). It consequently obeys its bound $CU^{1+\delta+\epsilon}$ and the stated polynomial height control whenever $2m+6\kappa z\le1$.*

*Proof.* The literal character identity identifies all plain and relative-slot coefficients. Injectivity reindexes without multiplicity; the radial majorant and keep indicator dominate on the image. Enlarge only the resulting nonnegative squared-modulus sum. For profiles with at most two logarithmic derivatives, the product rule for $W(y)y^{-\sigma+it}$ gives finite derivatives of $W$ times polynomials in bounded $\sigma$ and height $t$. Combine with the moment's height polynomial. Degree and constant precede live rows, subset, ray characters and heights, proving the stated finite field and uniformity. ◻

### A.8 Overlapping prime lists in the inverse moment

This coefficient-specific extension precedes affine arguments and is endpoint-independent.

**Lemma A.8.1** (Overlap adapter for the inverse moment). *<a id="ov:inverse-overlap"></a> The estimate of Theorem [A.7.3](#mf:inverse) remains valid for a fixed finite number of possibly overlapping or repeated prime lists with the same bounded annular coefficients. Both admission inequalities may use the full sum of the original slot widths.*

*Proof.* Partition finite prime tuples by exact equality pattern. Freeze each block of $k\ge2$ equal primes before the row norm. Its intersecting annuli have comparable $D_i$, giving central mass

$$
\sum_{\mathfrak p\in\bigcap_i\mathcal P_i}
       \prod_{i=1}^k D_i^{-1/2}|b_i(\mathfrak p)|
 \ll (\min_iD_i)\prod_{i=1}^k D_i^{-1/2}
 \ll D^{1-k/2}\ll1.
$$

Constants depend only on fixed slot count and profile suprema. Keep $\varphi_u(\mathfrak p)^k$ until taking the positive norm, then contract by its modulus $\le1$ with zeros retained. The inverse polynomial is unchanged and may share that prime.

Delete frozen primes from singleton lists. For $K$ singletons, color their union independently with $K$ colors. Each distinct ordered tuple receives prescribed slot colors with probability $K^{-K}$; repeated tuples never do. Its polynomial is therefore $K^K$ times the average over products on disjoint, row-independent colored lists. Apply Theorem [A.7.3](#mf:inverse), then Minkowski/Jensen, costing $K^{2K}$ in energy. For $K=0$ use UM. Deleting slots decreases both admission expressions.

Triangle over bounded-mass frozen choices and finitely many equality patterns proves the claim. This coloring extension applies only to MI; MP retains its canonical-pool contract and overlap allocation. ◻

## Appendix B. The literal probe, supported witnesses and initialization

The same probe underlies the natural initialization and the final return.
First its exact coefficients, signed Gram bound and principal signal are
proved; then its nonprincipal rows supply the witnesses and weighted
numerator. Finally the original complete comparison proves
\(\beta\le7/8\), independently of every stronger source in the main text.
The Mellin transform is always that of the reciprocal signal \(f_\eta\),
not of the error \(J_\eta-f_\eta\). Equations (188)–(223), (234)–(236)
and (240) retain their original stable labels solely for local navigation.


### B.1 The actual arithmetic coefficients and the two representations

Use the arithmetic chapter's primary generators, sextic symbols, angular $\alpha$, ray phases $G,R$, normalized Gauss sums $\gamma_j$ and additive measure. All residue-character powers, including zero/sixth, vanish at nonunits; rows keep six units. Ideal columns avoid fixed finite $S$, containing primes over six, primitive target conductor, ray moduli and a sufficiently large small-prime cutoff, chosen before scale/tuples/rows.

Let $b_*$ generate the product of the prime ideals in $S$. Choose a primitive residue character $\xi\bmod b_*$, quadratic at odd residue characteristic and cubic at the prime of norm four. Put

$$
\tau=q_{b_*}^{-1/2}g_\xi(b_*,1),\qquad
 \Xi(A)=\xi(A)\chi_A(b_*),\qquad |\tau|=1.
$$

The finite identities proved in the arithmetic chapter give

$$
\gamma_2(c)^3=\mu(c)\alpha(c),\quad
 \gamma_1(c)\gamma_2(c)=\mu(c)\alpha(c)G(c),\quad
 \chi_b(a)=R(a,b)\chi_a(b)\quad ((a,b)=1).
$$

These fix coefficient phases. Set

$$
V_G(r)=\frac{e^{-(\log r)^2/4}}{2\sqrt\pi},\qquad
 \widehat V_G(t)=e^{t^2},
$$

and choose nonnegative, nonzero, smooth annular $W_0,W_1$. For $A=cn^3$, where $c$ is squarefree and $c,n$ may share primes, define

<a id="dr:T"></a>
<a id="dr:I"></a>

$$
\begin{aligned}
 T_{m,a,\eta}(t)
 &=\sum_{c\ {\rm sf},n}
 \gamma_2(c)\overline{\alpha(A)G(A)}\eta(A)\Xi(A)^{-1}
 R(A,a)\chi_A(m)q_c^{-1/2-t}q_n^{-1-3t},\qquad\text{(187)}\\
 I_\eta(X,Y,Z)
 &=\frac1Y\sum_a
 \frac{W_1(q_a/Y)\chi_a(b_*)}
 {\tau\xi(a)\sqrt{q_{b_*}q_aX}}
 \sum_m\xi(m)q_a^{-1/2}g_{\chi_a}(a,-m)
 W_0\left(\frac{q_m}{q_{b_*}q_aX}\right)
 \frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(4)}Z^te^{t^2}T_{m,a,\eta}(t)\,dt.
 \qquad\text{(188)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The $a$ columns include prime powers and full zero-extended imprimitive Gauss sums. Annuli make $a,m\ne0$ finite; all other sums/integrals converge absolutely. Define $I_{\eta;D}$ by inserting $\mathbf1_{D\mid cn^3}$ on the whole theta index.

Choose finitely many distinct positive $\ell_i$, $P_i=Z^{\ell_i}$, and common smooth nonnegative nonzero $w$ supported in $(1,2)$. Each slot uses all primes outside $S$; distinct lengths make supports eventually disjoint. They may be as fine as any prescribed positive mesh with prescribed total $\ell=\sum_i\ell_i$. Write $w_i=w$ to index slots, $p_J=\prod_{i\in J}p_i$, and define

<a id="dr:comp"></a>

$$
I_\eta^{\rm comp}(Z)=
 \sum_{(p_i)}\prod_iw_i(q_{p_i}/P_i)
 \sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r_{\rm slot}\}}
 (-1)^{|J|}q_{p_J}^{-3/2}\overline{\eta(p_{J^c})}
 I_{\eta;p_{J^c}}(X/q_{p_J},Y/q_{p_J},Zq_{p_{J^c}}).
 \qquad\text{(189)}
$$

Weights are row-independent and the coefficient is $\overline\eta$. One slot gives divisibility minus rescaled subtraction; retain all collisions with $c,n$ and later rows.

For the physical representation, expand $\overline G$ on its fixed ray group, partition $a$ into classes $\sigma$ for $R(A,a)$, set $Q_0=q_{b_*}XY$ and take $\Omega=1$ on the product annuli. Mellin inversion of $W_0$ expresses [(188)](#dr:I) as a finite sum of

<a id="dr:physical"></a>

$$
\frac{Q_0^{-1/2}}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}\widehat W_0(iv)
 \sum_{m\ne0}\Omega(q_m/Q_0)\xi(m)(q_m/Q_0)^{-iv}
 A_{m,\sigma,v}(Y)B_{m,\sigma}(Z)\,dv,
 \qquad\text{(190)}
$$

where $B$ is a completed theta sum, with precisely the coefficients

$$
\mathcal C_V(N;m,\nu)=\sum_{c\ {\rm sf},n}
 \frac{\overline{\alpha(cn^3)}\gamma_2(c)\nu(cn^3)\chi_{cn^3}(m)}
 {\sqrt{q_c}\,q_n}V(q_cq_n^3/N),
$$

and

<a id="dr:A"></a>

$$
A_{m,\sigma,v}(Y)=Y^{-3/2}\sum_{a\in\sigma}
 \frac{\chi_a(b_*)}{\tau\xi(a)}W_1(q_a/Y)
 (q_a/Y)^{-1+iv}g_{\chi_a}(a,-m).
 \qquad\text{(191)}
$$

The identity $q_m/(q_{b_*}q_aX)=(q_m/Q_0)/(q_a/Y)$ gives $Y^{-3/2}$.

Let $\widetilde W_0(|y|^2)$ be the planar Fourier transform of $W_0(|z|^2)$ and $\mathscr M(z)=\int_0^\infty\widetilde W_0(r)r^{z-1}\,dr$, holomorphic for $\Re z>0$ with arbitrary vertical decay on compact positive substrips. Poisson gives

<a id="dr:Poisson"></a>

$$
\begin{aligned}
 I_\eta(X,Y,Z)=\frac1{(2\pi i)^3}
 \int_{(3)}\int_{(3)}\int_{(2)}
 &X^{1/2-z}Z^{s+z-1}Y^{w-1}e^{(s+z-1)^2}
 \mathscr M(z)\widehat W_1(w)\\[-2mm]
 &\quad\times\sum_u^{(6)}q_u^{-z}\overline{\xi(u)}

Its finite convolution is

$$
\mathcal F(a,A,H)=\sum_{\substack{d\bmod a\\H\equiv b_*Ad\bmod a}}

Expanding both Gauss sums in the full transform modulo $ab_*A$ gives $q_a^{1/2}\mathcal F$. Planar dilation $X/q_A$ leaves physical factor $X^{1/2}/(\sqrt{q_{b_*}}q_A)$. The primitive factor at $S$ kills frequencies meeting $S$, including zero. Write others uniquely $H=ur^6$, with primary $r$ and the unit retained in $u$; summing $r$ gives $\zeta_K^S(6z)$ without a factor six. Mellin inversion and $s=t+1-z$ yield [(192)](#dr:Poisson). On its initial lines a majorant is

$$
C_S\sum_{u,c,n,a,r}q_u^{-2}q_c^{-5/2}q_n^{-7}q_a^{-2}q_r^{-12},

times rapidly decreasing heights, justifying absolute interchange. CRT gives $g_{\xi\chi_A}(b_*A,K)=\xi(A)\chi_A(b_*)g_\xi(b_*,K)g_{\chi_A}(A,K)$; $\Xi(A)^{-1}$ and $\chi_a(b_*)/(\tau\xi(a))$ cancel fixed-prime factors, leaving $\overline{\xi(u)}$. The displayed phase identities cancel cross-prime terms, including shared primes of $a,A$.

### B.2 The local table, including all shared primes

The complete local table for [(192)](#dr:Poisson) and numerator averaging uses, at $p\notin S$,

$$
\begin{gathered}
 Q=q_p,\quad j=v_p(u)\in\{0,\ldots,5\},\quad
 \rho=\chi_p(u/p^j),\quad
 \mathfrak a=\overline{\alpha(p)}^3\eta(p)^3,\quad
 \mathfrak b=\overline{\alpha(p)}^2\eta(p)^2\overline{\chi_p(4)},
 \quad \mathfrak b^3=\mathfrak a^2,\\
 V=Q^{-6z},\quad R_p=\mathfrak a^2Q^{4-6s-6z},\quad
 W^\circ=\rho Q^{-w},\quad W=\chi_p(u)Q^{-w},\quad
 D=\eta(p)\overline{\chi_p(u)}Q^{-s}.
\end{gathered}
$$

Thus $D=W=0$ for $j>0$. Set

<a id="dr:Euler-table"></a>

$$
\begin{aligned}
 P_p^*&=\frac1{1-R_p}
 \left\{\frac{R_p(1-Q^{-1})-\eta(p)(Q-1)Q^{-s-w}
 V^{\mathbf1_{j\le1}}}{1-V}+J_j\right\},\\
 P_p&=(1-V)^{-1}+\mathbf1_{j=0}\frac{W^\circ}{1-W^\circ}+P_p^*,
 \qquad H_p=\frac{P_p(1-V)(1-W)}{1-D},
 \quad H_{\eta,u}=\prod_{p\notin S}H_p,
 \qquad\text{(193)}
\end{aligned}
$$

where

$$
\begin{array}{c|l}
 j&J_j\\ \hline
0&-\eta(p)\rho^{-1}Q^{-s}+W^\circ R_p\\
1&\eta(p)Q^{-s-w}\\
2&\mathfrak a\rho^{-3}Q^{3/2-3s}\\
3&-\eta(p)\mathfrak b\rho^{-2}Q^{2-3s-w}
                  +\mathfrak b^2\rho^{-4}Q^{2-4s}\\
4&-\eta(p)\mathfrak a\rho^{-3}Q^{5/2-4s-w}\\
5&-\mathfrak a^2Q^{3-6s}.
\end{array}
$$

For $t=e+3l$, $e\in\{0,1\}$, the local convolution is

$$
C_p(t,k,j')=\sum_{\substack{d\bmod p^k\\p^{j'}\equiv p^td\bmod p^k}}
 \chi_p(d)^k g_{\chi_p^t}
 \left(p^t,\frac{p^{j'}-p^td}{p^k}\right).
$$

Lifting a prime Gauss sum gives

$$
g_{\chi_p^h}(p^t,K)=
 \begin{cases}Q^{t-1}g_{\chi_p^h}(p,K/p^{t-1}),&p^{t-1}\mid K,\\
 0,&p^{t-1}\nmid K.
 \end{cases}
$$

For $t=0$ it is one at $k=0$, $\mathbf1_{j'=0}$ at $k>0$. For $t>0,k=0$ it is the source Gauss sum; for $k=1,j'\ge1$ it is $\chi_p(-1)^{-1}g_{\chi_p}(p,1)g_{\chi_p^{t-1}}(p^t,p^{j'-1})$, while $j'=0$ has no solution. For $k\ge2$ the last lift $d=d_0+p^{k-1}h$ sums a nontrivial additive character and vanishes. Surviving $t>0$ valuations are

$$
\begin{array}{c|cc}
 t&k=0&k=1\\ \hline
 6r+6&j'\ge t-1&j'=t\\
 6r+1&j'=t-1&j'\ge t\\
 6r+3&j'=t-1&j'=t\\
 6r+4&j'=t-1&j'=t.
\end{array}
$$

After CRT phase cancellation, with $j'=j+6m$ and $\omega_p=\chi_p(-1)$, the summand is

$$
(-1)^e\gamma_1(p)^{-e}\eta(p)^e
 (\mathfrak a\overline{\gamma_3(p)})^l
 \rho^{k-t}\omega_p^{tk-el-l(l-1)/2}C_p(t,k,j+6m)
 Q^{-(s+1/2)e-(1+3s)l-wk-6zm}.
$$

The first two strict tails sum to $R_p(1-Q^{-1})/((1-R_p)(1-V))$ and $-\eta(p)(Q-1)Q^{-s-w}V^{\mathbf1_{j\le1}}/((1-R_p)(1-V))$. Finite Gauss identities give equality terms $J_j/(1-R_p)$; $t=0$ gives the initial terms of $P_p$. This covers every valuation.

Put $c_p=\overline{\eta(p)}Q^s$, $h_p=Q^{-w}$, and

<a id="dr:G"></a>

$$
G_p=\frac{(c_p-h_p)(1-V)(1-W)P_p^*-h_p(1-VW)}{1-D}.
 \qquad\text{(194)}
$$

The local effect of the two alternatives in [(189)](#dr:comp) is the identity

$$
\overline{\eta(p)}Q^{s+z-1}P_p^*-Q^{z-w-1}P_p
 =\frac{(1-D)Q^{z-1}G_p}{(1-V)(1-W)}.
$$

Consequently its exact Poisson correction is

<a id="dr:Hcomp"></a>

$$
\mathcal H_{\eta,u,Z}=
 \sum_{(p_i)}\prod_iw_i(Q_i/P_i)Q_i^{z-1}G_{p_i}
 \prod_{p\notin S\cup\{p_i\}}H_p.
 \qquad\text{(195)}
$$

For $p\nmid u$ put $v=\chi_p(u)$, $E_p=P_p^*+D$. Substituting $c_pD=v^{-1}$ gives the quotient-free identity

<a id="dr:Delta"></a>

$$
G_p+v^{-1}H_p=\frac{(1-V)(1-W)}{1-D}
 \left[(v^{-1}-h_p)\left(\frac V{1-V}-D\right)
 +(c_p+v^{-1}-h_p)E_p\right].\qquad\text{(196)}
$$

Define $\Delta_p=G_p+\overline{\psi_u(p)}H_p$ also at row primes. Expanding $G_p=-\overline{\psi_u(p)}H_p+\Delta_p$ gives all main/error choices in [(195)](#dr:Hcomp), with main slot exactly $-\sum_pw_i(Q/P_i)Q^{z-1}\overline{\psi_u(p)}$, including zero character values.

The local table also proves normal convergence and $H_{\eta,u}\ll q_u^\epsilon$ on compact real boxes in

<a id="dr:box"></a>

$$
\Re s\ge51/100,\quad\Re z\ge17/50,\quad
 \Re w\ge-1/100,\quad\Re(s+w)\ge1+\epsilon_1.
 \qquad\text{(197)}
$$

Unramified leading defects $Q^{-s-w}$ and $Q^{4-6s-6z}$ are $\le Q^{-1-\epsilon_1}$ and $Q^{-11/10}$; all others have summable margins. Row-prime defects are negative powers, giving $q_u^\epsilon$ after a fixed cutoff; $1-W$ cancels. For $u=1$ also allow $\Re s\ge87/100$, $\Re w\ge3/4$, $\Re z\ge1/8$. Substituting the six local terms in [(195)](#dr:Hcomp) gives $\ll q_u^\epsilon Z^{(17/50)\ell}$ on $(\beta+e,1/2,17/50)$ and $\ll q_u^\epsilon Z^{v\ell}$ on $(2,2,v)$, $v>2$: selected off-row factors are bounded; the first line's exceptional $O(Q^{1/2})$ occurs only at divisor-many primes. Intervening fixed boxes have fixed polynomial height/scale bounds.

<a id="dr:Gram"></a>

### B.3 The signed Gram calculation and the physical bound

**Lemma B.2.1** (Signed physical Gram estimate). *<a id="dr:Gram-lemma"></a> For [(191)](#dr:A), with $P_a=Y^2/Q_0\ge1$,*

$$
\sum_{q_m\ll Q_0}|A_{m,\sigma,v}(Y)|^2
 \ll (1+|v|)^J\frac{Q_0}{Y}
       \left(1+P_a^{1/6}+\frac{P_a^2}{Y}\right)Z^\epsilon.
$$

*This assertion uses the displayed fixed ray coefficients.*

*Proof.* Expand the signed square. Arithmetic Fourier correlation has $F(u,v;0)=\mathbf1_{u=v}\phi(u)$ and, for $u=Cn_1,v=Cn_2$, $(n_1,n_2)=1$,

$$
F(Cn_1,Cn_2;Ck)=\chi_{n_1}(k)\overline{\chi_{n_2}(-k)}
 R(n_1,n_2)L_C(n_1,n_2;k),\qquad |L_C|\le q_C.
$$

Row Poisson contributes $Q_0/(q_uq_v)$, the Gauss pair $q_uq_vF$, giving prefactor $Q_0/Y^3$; zero frequency costs $O(Q_0/Y)$.

For nonzero frequencies extend the coefficient to residual pairs, setting it zero when a $C$-prime divides both, then insert full Möbius coprimality. On divisor $d$, write $n_i=dm_i$; natural zeros force $(d,Ck)=1$. The extension cancels in the complete divisor sum. After finite ray separation the period norm is $\ll q_Cq_k$; its complete mean vanishes unless the sixth-free part of $k$ is supported on $C,S$, since every other prime gives a nonprincipal complete character sum.

On $q_C\asymp C_0,q_d\asymp D_0,q_Cq_k\asymp RP_a$, put $N=Y/(C_0D_0)$. Two-column lattice Poisson bounds zero-mean sums by

$$
(1+|v|)^J R^{-B}C_0N^2
           \min\{1,(RP_a/N)^A\}.
$$

Below period use counting; above period integrate all nonzero dual frequencies by parts. There are $O(D_0RP_a)$ choices of $C,d,k$, and the remaining dyads use

$$
\sum_{i,j\ge0}2^{-i-j}\min\{1,(2^{i+j}/\Lambda)^A\}
 \ll_A\frac{1+\log(2+\Lambda)}\Lambda,\quad
 \Lambda=Y/(RP_a),\quad A>1.
$$

Group by $i+j=n$ and split $(n+1)2^{-n}$ at $2^n=\Lambda$. Including $Q_0/Y^3$ gives $(Q_0/Y)P_a^2/Y$; large $B$ sums $R$.

For nonzero mean, write $k=er^6$ with sixth-free $e$ supported on $C,S$. There are divisor-many $e$ and $O(Z^\epsilon(RP_a/C_0)^{1/6})$ roots. Absolute column volume gives $(Q_0/Y)P_a^{1/6}$ with summable weights $C_0^{-1/6+\epsilon}D_0^{-1+\epsilon}$. Add zero frequency; finitely many profile derivatives give $(1+|v|)^J$. ◻

We apply the completed marked energy of Lemma [A.7.1](#mf:marked-energy) with its following exact interface. For the displayed $\mathcal C_V$, product-form row-independent prime marks of total width $z$, completed length $Z^N$, and row range $Z^M$,

<a id="dr:marked-energy-interface"></a>

$$
M+2z\le N\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \sum_{0<q_m\ll Z^M}|\mathcal T(m)|^2
 \ll Z^{M+(N+2z-2M)_+/4+\epsilon}.
 \qquad\text{(198)}
$$

Lemma [A.7.1](#mf:marked-energy) includes both collision masks, all cusps, joint profiles and full kernel tails for these multiple slots.

Let $X=Z^x,Y=Z^y,M=x+y$ and assume

$$
0<\ell<x\le y,\qquad M+\ell\le1,\qquad y-2x+\ell<0.
$$

Cauchy in [(190)](#dr:physical), the Gram lemma and [(198)](#dr:marked-energy-interface) give

<a id="dr:physical-bound"></a>

$$
|I_\eta^{\rm comp}(Z)|
 \ll Z^{x/2+(y-x)/12+(1+3\ell-2M)_+/8+\epsilon}.
 \qquad\text{(199)}
$$

For subset $J$ of width $d$, the rescaled row/mark/completed exponents are $M'=M-2d$, $z'=\ell-d$, $N'=1+\ell-d$, satisfying $M'+2z'\le N'$. Outside factor, tuple mass and energy square root add

$$
-d+\frac{(1+3\ell-2M+d)_+}{8}.
$$

Its slopes $-1,-7/8$ make $d=0$ maximal. The Gram condition $P_a^2/(Y/q_{p_J})\ll1$ follows from $y-2x+\ell<0$. Integrate common Mellin profiles and sum finite rays to obtain [(199)](#dr:physical-bound) for every subset.

### B.4 The unique principal signal and its nonvanishing numerator

Only $u=1$ is principal in [(192)](#dr:Poisson): a nonunit sixth-free row has a good prime of valuation $1,\ldots,5$, hence nontrivial tame Kummer inertia. For unit $u\ne1$, CRT gives primary $n\equiv-2-3\omega\pmod{36\mathcal O}$ and $n\equiv1$ at other fixed primes. Then $q_n\equiv7\pmod{36}$ and $\chi_n(u)=u^{(q_n-1)/6}=u\ne1$. Keep all five units in the remainder.

Let $\rho_S=\operatorname{Res}_{s=1}\zeta_K^S(s)>0$. At $w=1,z=1/6$ the table simplifies, with $t=Q^{-1}$, to

<a id="dr:principal-local"></a>

$$
H_{\eta,p}(s)=\frac{1-t^2}{1-R_p}
 \left(1+\frac{t(D-R_p)}{1-D}\right),\qquad
 D=\eta(p)Q^{-s},\quad
 R_p=\overline{\alpha(p)}^6\eta(p)^6Q^{3-6s}.
 \qquad\text{(200)}
$$

In particular, for any fixed $b>2/3$,

$$
|H_{\eta,p}(s)-1|\ll_b
 Q^{-2}+Q^{-1-b}+Q^{3-6b}+Q^{2-6b}\qquad(\Re s\ge b).
$$

These powers are prime summable. Enlarge the fixed cutoff until their majorant sum is $\le\log(3/2)$; normal convergence and $\prod(1+a_p)\le e^{\sum a_p}$ give

<a id="dr:H-nonzero"></a>

$$
H_\eta(s)=\prod_{p\notin S}H_{\eta,p}(s),\qquad
 |H_\eta(s)-1|\le\tfrac12\quad (\Re s\ge b).
 \qquad\text{(201)}
$$

Thus $H_\eta$ is holomorphic and nonzero uniformly in height; $b=87/100$ suffices for all established endpoints here.

The positive residue scalar is

$$
c_S=\frac{\rho_S^2}{6}\widehat W_1(1)\mathscr M(1/6)>0.
$$

Indeed, Fourier transformation of the radial Riesz kernel, first written as a positive integral of Gaussians, gives for $0<\sigma<1$

$$
\mathscr M(\sigma)=\left(\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt3}\right)^{1-2\sigma}
 \frac{\Gamma(\sigma)}{\Gamma(1-\sigma)}
 \int_0^\infty W_0(r)r^{-\sigma}\,dr>0.
$$

Annular support/Schwartz decay justify interchange; $1/6$ in $c_S$ is the residue scaling of $\zeta_K^S(6z)$.

On this residue locus [(196)](#dr:Delta) gives $G_p/H_p=-1+O(Q^{-b})$. Define the real nonzero normalizer

$$
A(Z)=(-1)^{r_{\rm slot}}Z^{-\ell/6}
       \prod_i\sum_pw_i(Q/P_i)Q^{-5/6}.
$$

The fixed-field prime ideal theorem gives $|A(Z)|\asymp(\log Z)^{-r_{\rm slot}}$. Multiplying over fixed disjoint slots gives

<a id="dr:prime-residue"></a>

$$
\mathcal H_{\eta,1,Z}(s,1,1/6)
 =H_\eta(s)Z^{\ell/6}A(Z)(1+O(Z^{-\mu_P})),
 \quad 0<\mu_P<b\min_i\ell_i,\quad\Re s\ge b.
 \qquad\text{(202)}
$$

Put

<a id="dr:J-f"></a>

$$
h=1+\ell-x,\quad k=\tfrac56-\tfrac x3-\tfrac\ell6,
 \qquad J_\eta(Z)=\frac{I_\eta^{\rm comp}(Z)}{c_S A(Z)},
 \quad
 f_\eta(Z)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(2)}Z^{s-k}
 e^{(s-5/6)^2}\frac{H_\eta(s)}{L_K^S(s,\eta)}\,ds.
 \qquad\text{(203)}
$$

The residue power is $X^{1/3}Z^{s-5/6}Z^{\ell/6}=Z^{s-k}$. Equation [(202)](#dr:prime-residue) therefore identifies $f_\eta$ up to power-small error: the compensator gives $Z^{\ell/6}$ and $A(Z)$ has logarithmic size.

### B.5 Buffered zero bins and two witnesses at the same zero

For fixed finite-ray $\nu$, let $\varphi_u=\nu\psi_u^{\pm1}$ with its natural zeros, and set

$$
M_u(D;W)=D^{-1/2}\sum_n\mu(n)\varphi_u(n)W(q_n/D),\qquad
 S_u(N;W)=N^{-1/2}\sum_n\varphi_u(n)W(q_n/N).
$$

Preceding moments have common annular controls for real powers, scale derivatives and independent polynomial heights. In particular,

<a id="dr:unmarked"></a>

$$
\sum_{q_u\asymp U}^{(6)}|M_u(U^r;W)|^2
 \ll U^{\max\{1,(1+5r)/6\}+\epsilon},\qquad
 \sum_{q_u\asymp U}^{(6),\varphi_u^*\ne1}|S_u(U^m;W)|^4
 \ll U^{1+\epsilon}.
 \qquad\text{(204)}
$$

The long inverse exponent follows from Lemma [A.4.1](#cf:inverse-moment) by the exact amplification

$$
M_u(D;W)=\sum_{d\mid\operatorname{rad}(a)}
 \mu(d)\varphi_u(d)q_d^{-1/2}M_{ua^6}(D/q_d;W).
$$

This separates squarefree column primes dividing $a$, retaining shared-prime zeros, with coefficient mass $q_a^\epsilon$. Log-scale differentiation replaces $W$ by $-W/2-yW'$. Sobolev and the inverse moment bound $\sup_{0<E\le D}$ on balls $H\ge D^{1+\vartheta}$. Average over primary $q_a\le(H/U)^{1/6}$ for $H=\max(2U,D^{1+\vartheta})$; valuations modulo six make $(u,a)\mapsto ua^6$ injective. Its $\gg_S(H/U)^{1/6}$ preimages give $U^{1/6}H^{5/6}(UD)^\epsilon$, hence [(204)](#dr:unmarked). Row $u=1$ gives smooth Möbius sums $\ll D^{11/12+\epsilon}$; Mellin inversion with a test nonzero at a proposed zero yields preliminary $\beta\le11/12$, before $7/8$ or marked plain moments.

Fix finite conjugation-stable $\Theta$ containing all target numerator/denominator/ray/phase twists. For nonunit sixth-free $u$, $\mathcal X(u)=\{\nu\psi_u^{\pm1}:\nu\in\Theta\}$ is nonprincipal of conductor $O_S(q_u)$ with redundant zeros. Put $a_*=51/100$, small $e>0$, $I=\lceil1/e\rceil+2$. Let $B_j(u)$ maximize $a_*$ and zero real parts of $\mathcal X(u)$ up to height $3^jT$. Some $i<I$ has $B_{i+1}-B_i\le e$; round $B_i$ down on the $e$ mesh:

<a id="dr:bins"></a>

$$
a\le B_i<a+e,\qquad B_{i+1}<a+2e.\qquad\text{(205)}
$$

Labels $(i,a)$ are finite. Above the floor there is one actual zero $\rho=\sigma+i\gamma$, $a\le\sigma<a+e$, $|\gamma|\le3^iT$, supplying both witnesses. Put $\delta=2a-1$.

We record the analytic consequence of the buffer. The ordinary Hecke functional equation in this normalization is

$$
\Lambda(s,\varphi)=(3q_{\mathfrak f})^{s/2}(2\pi)^{-s}
 \Gamma(s)L_K(s,\varphi),\qquad
 \Lambda(s,\varphi)=\epsilon_\varphi\Lambda(1-s,\bar\varphi),
 \quad |\epsilon_\varphi|=1.
$$

Euler convergence and the functional equation give polynomial conductor/height growth. Continue the Euler logarithm on a zero-free disk about $2+it$. Borel–Carathéodory bounds it by $O_e(\log(2q_{\mathfrak f}(3+|t|)^2))$ on a smaller disk; Euler convergence bounds it on radius $49/100$. Three circles with another buffer reduces the logarithm to a power $<1$. Exponentiating either sign gives

<a id="dr:buffered"></a>

$$
|L_K(s,\varphi)|+|L_K(s,\varphi)^{-1}|
 \ll_{e,\epsilon}\{2q_{\mathfrak f}(3+|t|)^2\}^{\epsilon}.
 \qquad\text{(206)}
$$

Use radii $2-a-2e,2-a-4e,2-a-6e$; Cauchy gives logarithmic derivatives. For principal characters apply this to $(s-1)\zeta_K(s)/(s+1)$; to the right of $\beta+e$ it holds at all heights. Deleted factors cost $U^\epsilon$ on fixed positive half-planes and $U^{v+\epsilon}$ on $\Re s\ge-v$, by summing $O(q_p^{-\sigma})$ beyond a fixed cutoff and the divisor bound.

Mellin inversion and reflection now give

<a id="dr:saturation-upper"></a>

$$
|M_u(U^r)|^2\ll U^{\delta r+\epsilon_0},\qquad
 |S_u(U^m)|^2\ll U^{\delta\min(m,1-m)+\epsilon_0}.
 \qquad\text{(207)}
$$

For prime tests apply $-L'/L$, divide by $\log q_p$ and subtract prime powers costing $O(P^{1/2+\epsilon})$ before normalization:

<a id="dr:prime-upper"></a>

$$
\left|P^{-1/2}\sum_p\overline{\psi_u(p)}w(q_p/P)
 (q_p/P)^{it}\right|
 \ll P^{\delta/2+O(e)+\epsilon}U^\epsilon(1+T)^A.
 \qquad\text{(208)}
$$

The buffer [(205)](#dr:bins) covers the witness neighborhood; distinct norm twists keep independent heights.

**Lemma B.5.1** (Same-zero witnesses). *<a id="dr:same-zero"></a> Fix $t_0\in[1,3/2]$ for a nonfloor bin before selecting its witnesses. Each row has a presentation, a real power $\sigma\in[a,a+e)$, a common height and dyadic lengths $U^r,U^m$ such that*

$$
r\le t_0+o(1),\quad r+m\ge t_0-o(1),\quad
 0\le m\le\tfrac12+O(\epsilon_0),
$$

$$
|M_u(U^r)|^2\gg U^{\delta r-O(\epsilon_0)},\qquad
 |S_u(U^m)|^2\gg U^{\delta m-O(\epsilon_0)}.
$$

*After fixing presentations and dyads, the base profiles are common.*

*Proof.* Choose $V_\le=1$ on $[0,1]$, zero on $[2,\infty)$, and put $C_\varphi(s)=\sum_l\mu(l)\varphi(l)V_\le(q_l/U^{t_0})q_l^{-s}$. At the actual zero $\rho$ shift

$$
\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(2)}U^{40z}\Gamma(z)
 L_K^S(\rho+z,\varphi)C_\varphi(\rho+z)\,dz
$$

to $\Re z=-1/4$. The zero residue vanishes; polynomial growth, gamma decay and small height exponent make the new integral $o(1)$, since $U^{-10}$ dominates ideal counting. On the absolute line the unit contributes $1+o(1)$ and $\mu*1=\mathbf1_1$ cancels $1<q_{lk}\le U^{t_0}$. The remaining sum has magnitude $1+o(1)$ and product norm $\gg U^{t_0}$. Truncate smoothly at $U^{41}$ with error $o(1)$, then dyadically partition and Fourier-separate the product weight to select one pair/frequency with

$$
|M_u(U^r)S_u(U^m)|^2
 \gg U^{\delta(r+m)-O(\epsilon_0)}.
$$

Both factors inherit the same character, real power and height from the convolution at $\rho$. Equation [(207)](#dr:saturation-upper) and $\delta\ge1/50$ force $m\le1/2+O(\epsilon_0)$; division by each upper bound gives both lower bounds. The inverse cutoff $V_\le(U^ry/U^{t_0})$ has uniform annular transition derivatives. Dyads and rapidly decaying separating-frequency tails fit the loss. ◻

### B.6 Actual amplitude selection and source transport

At row scale $U=Z^d$, slot lengths are $z_i=\ell_i/d$. Bin squared normalized amplitudes as $|Q_{u,i}|^2\asymp U^{2z_i g_i}$, $0\le g_i\le\delta/2$; lower-than-first and error slots have $g_i=0$. Fix the amplitude mesh within the small-power loss; put $L=\ell/d$ and

$$
q=L^{-1}\sum_i z_i g_i=\delta p,\qquad 0\le p\le1/2.
$$

Order $g_i$ decreasingly. Their step-function integral over initial length $z$ is $\ge qz$; discard the last fractional slot to get a genuine subset satisfying

<a id="dr:greedy"></a>

$$
\prod_{i\in I}|Q_{u,i}|^2
 \ge U^{2qz-\delta\max_i z_i-o(1)}.
 \qquad\text{(209)}
$$

This charges one mesh. Whole-polynomial conjugation/fixed-character multiplication changes physical $\overline{\psi_u}$ to witness orientation with row-independent coefficients.

We use Lemmas [A.7.3](#mf:inverse) and [A.7.4](#mf:plain) in their precise coefficient-specific forms

<a id="dr:MI"></a>
<a id="dr:MP"></a>

$$
\begin{aligned}
 r+2z<1,\quad 2r+8z<3
 &\ \Longrightarrow\ 
 \sum_{q_u\asymp U}|M_u(U^r)Q_{u,I}|^2\ll U^{1+\epsilon},
 \qquad\text{(210)}\\
 2m+6\kappa z<1
 &\ \Longrightarrow\ 
 \sum_{q_u\asymp U}^{\rm eligible}|S_u(U^m)|^4|Q_{u,I}|^2
 \ll U^{1+\epsilon},\qquad \kappa=2\beta-1.
 \qquad\text{(211)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Explicitly, at $z=z_0+ib_i$ the physical main slot has modulus

$$
Q^-_{u,i}=P_i^{-1/2}\sum_{p\notin S}
 w(q_p/P_i)(q_p/P_i)^{-33/50+ib_i}
 \overline{\psi_u(p)}.
$$

Extracting $P_i^{z_0-1/2+ib_i}$ from [(196)](#dr:Delta) gives this polynomial up to unit phase. Since $w$ is real, $Q^+_{u,i}=\overline{Q^-_{u,i}}$ has the same modulus and height $-b_i$.

Apply the following physical transport to the same-zero presentations after fixing target $\eta$ and finite $\Theta$. Whole conjugation when $\varepsilon=-1$ gives both witnesses character $a_j\psi_u$, where $a_j=\eta_j$ or $\overline{\eta_j}$, preserving coefficients, profile, height and zeros.

Induce all $a_j$ to one $\mathfrak q$ containing every $S$-prime and divisible by $72\mathcal O$ and their conductors. Use full residue-unit group $H$, $Q=\mathfrak q$, anchors $\eta_0=\eta=a_j$, and trivial $\vartheta_i$. Then $Q'=Q\cap\mathfrak q_{\eta_0}=\mathfrak q\subseteq72\mathcal O$, relative coefficient $\mathbf1_{\mathfrak q}\overline{a_j}$, and on good primes

$$
(a_j(p)\psi_u(p))\overline{a_j(p)}=\psi_u(p).
$$

Nonunits retain zeros; the identity pool is the probe's full good-prime pool.

Take $v_i=-b_i-t$. Source slots are $P_i^{it}Q^+_{u,i}$ at shift $33/50$; its two plains are the transformed copies of $S_u$. Energy is exactly $|S_u|^4|Q_{u,I}|^2$ in both orientations. Growing nonunit sixth-free rows have a conductor prime outside $\mathfrak q$ and satisfy literal keep; units/small exceptions are paid below. Intersect marked HIGH and analytic meshes before slots, then maximize finite dictionary height degrees and union seminorms. A sufficiently small target-dependent height exponent works; no common degree for infinitely many targets is required.


The moment-to-count conversion is now exactly the one in §7. For the
plain witness use the complete source's actual clipped width
\(\min\{z,(B-2m)/L\}\), with its cap, witness interval and
admission guards (C7). The source-domain inclusion of §6 supplies every
inherited face without a prior decimal endpoint. The short inverse,
long inverse, plain and natural-tail cases, including all zero-width
fallbacks, are proved there. The physical supply condition
\(\ell/d_+>1/5\) dominates both the inverse selection
\((1-r)/2<7/37\) for \(r>23/37\) and every actual count
width \(z<7/37\). Thus every selected subset comes from the actual
original prime pool. The natural count and its feedback are (C1).


### B.7 Weighted numerator and conductor allocation

For each main/error term of [(195)](#dr:Hcomp), define its actual numerator by full $w$ inversion:

<a id="dr:N"></a>

$$
\mathcal N_u(Y;s,z)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(3)}Y^{w-1}
 \widehat W_1(w)L_K^S(w,\psi_u)
 \mathcal H^{\rm term}_{\eta,u,Z}(s,w,z)\,dw.
 \qquad\text{(216)}
$$

Bound the $w$-independent denominator afterwards. The following coefficient calculation admits a plain moment.

Write $t=Q^{-w}$. Away from the row let $v=\chi_p(u)$ and $d_p=\eta(p)v^{-1}Q^{-s}$. Direct expansion of [(193)](#dr:Euler-table) gives $H_p=H_{p,0}+H_{p,1}t+H_{p,2}t^2$, where

<a id="dr:Hcoeff"></a>

$$
\begin{aligned}
 H_{p,0}&=\frac{1-R_p/Q-d_p(1-V)}{(1-R_p)(1-d_p)},\\
 H_{p,1}&=\frac{\eta(p)Q^{-s}(1-QV)-vV+vR_p/Q}
 {(1-R_p)(1-d_p)},\qquad\text{(217)}\\
 H_{p,2}&=\frac{v\eta(p)(Q-1)Q^{-s}V-v^2R_p(1-V)}
 {(1-R_p)(1-d_p)}.
\end{aligned}
$$

On $\Re s=a+16e,\Re z=z_0=17/50$ these imply

<a id="dr:Hcoeff-bound"></a>

$$
|H_{p,0}-1|+\sum_{k=1}^2|H_{p,k}|Q^{k(a-1)}
 \ll Q^{-1-\epsilon_e}.
 \qquad\text{(218)}
$$

The largest linear exponent is $-1-16e$; other candidates $a-1-6z_0,2-4a-6z_0,4-6a-6z_0,-a-6z_0$ are $<-1$ for $a\ge51/100$. For quotient-free error estimates write $E_p=E_0+E_1t$ with

$$
E_0=\frac{R_p}{1-R_p}\left(\frac{1-Q^{-1}}{1-V}-d_p\right),\qquad

$$

Insertion in [(196)](#dr:Delta) proves

$$
\sum_{k=0}^3|\Delta_{p,k}|Q^{k(a-1)}\ll Q^{-a}.
 \qquad\text{(219)}
$$

The constant is $\ll Q^{-a}+Q^{-6z_0}+Q^{4-5a-6z_0}\ll Q^{-a}$. Each additional $t$ weighs $Q^{a-1}<1$, and $1-6z_0<-1$.

At a row prime $p^j\Vert u$, $1\le j\le5$, write $J_j=A_j+B_jt$. For $j\ge2$ the exact coefficients are

\end{aligned}
$$

$$

At row primes $\Delta_p=G_p$. The primitive conductor's good-prime exponent is one. Allocate $\min(k,j-1)$ powers of shift $Q^k$ to $h_r\mid\Lambda_u=q_u/q_{\operatorname{rad}(u)}$, the rest to $h_0$. With $\delta=2a-1$,

### B.9 The supremum and original seven-eighths comparison

Let $\mathcal H$ be the presented finite-order Eisenstein Hecke family with prescribed Euler factors and natural zeros. Its actual zero supremum is

$$
\beta=\sup\left(\{\tfrac12\}\cup
 \{\Re\rho:\chi\in\mathcal H,\ \Re\rho>0,\
 L_K(\rho,\chi)=0,\ (\chi,\rho)\ne(1,1)\}\right).
$$

Absolute convergence of the Euler product in $\Re s>1$ gives $1/2\le\beta\le1$. The principal pole at one is excluded throughout.

**Lemma B.9.1** (Primitive targets approaching the supremum). *<a id="init:primitive-supremum"></a> The same supremum is obtained from primitive targets. If $\varepsilon>0$ and $\beta-\varepsilon\ge1/2$, there is a primitive target with a zero $\rho$ satisfying $\Re\rho>\beta-\varepsilon$.*

*Proof.* A presentation induced by $\chi^*$ has $L_K(s,\chi^*)$ times finitely many $1-\chi^*(\mathfrak p)(N\mathfrak p)^{-s}$. These are one when the value is zero and otherwise vanish only on $\Re s=0$. Primitive and presented positive-half-plane zeros coincide. Supremum approximation then supplies the asserted primitive zero; no attainment is needed. ◻

The original marked-moment range is

<a id="init:original-moment-range"></a>

$$
\beta\ge\frac{51}{100},\qquad \kappa\ge\frac34,
 \qquad 2\beta-1\le\kappa.
 \qquad\text{(I.1)}
$$

Proposition [A.7.5](#mf:plain-original-bootstrap) proves this range before initialization, retaining full row/moving width, literal slots, fixed-inducing exclusion and profile/height control. Proposition [A.7.6](#mf:plain-refined) supplies the later refined range separately.

**Lemma B.9.2** (Noncircular moment parameter). *<a id="init:moment-parameter"></a> In the contradiction case $\beta>7/8$, the choice <a id="init:kappa"></a>*

$$
\Delta=\beta-\frac78,\qquad
 \kappa=\frac34+2\Delta=2\beta-1
 \qquad\text{(I.2)}
$$

*satisfies [(I.1)](#init:original-moment-range), with $3/4<\kappa\le1$.*

*Proof.* Expansion gives the identity; $\Delta>0$ and $\beta\le1$ give $3/4<\kappa\le1$. Condition $2\beta-1\le\kappa$ holds with equality before the desired conclusion. ◻

The same analytic return serves later improvements. Constants may depend on the target except those explicitly common.

**Lemma B.9.3** (A common-reserve Mellin contradiction). *<a id="init:mellin-return"></a> Let $1/2\le\theta<\beta$, and suppose $k_0$ is real. Suppose there are common numbers $\omega,\sigma_0>0$ with $\omega<\beta-\theta$ such that each primitive target has a probe $J_\eta$ and a function $H_\eta$, holomorphic on $\Re s>\theta$, satisfying <a id="init:signal"></a>*

$$
|H_\eta(s)-1|\le\frac12,
 \qquad
 f_\eta(Z)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(c)}
 Z^{s-k_0}e^{(s-5/6)^2}
 \frac{H_\eta(s)}{L_K(s,\eta)}\,ds,
 \qquad\text{(I.3)}
$$

*on an absolute line $c>1$, with the stated vertical convergence. Assume that $f_\eta$ decays faster than every power at zero and that, for large $Z$, <a id="init:two-probe-bounds"></a>*

$$
J_\eta(Z)\ll_\eta Z^{\theta-k_0+\omega},\qquad
 J_\eta(Z)-f_\eta(Z)\ll_\eta Z^{\beta-k_0-\sigma_0}.
 \qquad\text{(I.4)}
$$

*Then these hypotheses contradict the definition of $\beta$.*

*Proof.* Put $m=\min(\beta-\theta-\omega,\sigma_0)>0$. The two bounds on the same probe give $f_\eta(Z)\ll_\eta Z^{\beta-k_0-m}$, so

$$
F_\eta(s)=\int_0^\infty f_\eta(Z)Z^{k_0-s}\frac{dZ}{Z}
$$

is locally uniformly holomorphic for $\Re s>\beta-m$: use this bound at infinity and arbitrary decay at zero, also after logarithmic differentiation. Absolute-line Fourier--Mellin inversion identifies it with the Gaussian quotient in [(I.3)](#init:signal); meromorphic identity continues throughout this connected half-plane.

Since $\beta-m\ge\theta+\omega>\theta$, the numerator is holomorphic and nonzero ($|H_\eta|\ge1/2$). Any denominator zero, of any multiplicity, would give an impossible pole. Euler deletions change no such zero by Lemma [B.9.1](#init:primitive-supremum); the principal pole creates no reciprocal pole.

Thus every primitive target is zero-free for $\Re s>\beta-m$, with common $m$ despite target-dependent constants. Lemma [B.9.1](#init:primitive-supremum) at $\varepsilon=m/2$ supplies a forbidden zero, since $\beta-m/2>\theta\ge1/2$. ◻
