#### Whole kernels and allocation normalizers

On a retained dyad the nonseparated kernel contains

$$
\omega_K(q_h/U^K)\widehat\Psi(H_0q_h/(q_eq_rq_aq_b))
                  (q_aq_b)^{-1/2}.
$$

Multiply by common log-row and whole-column cutoffs, shared by both rectangles. For the resulting compact logarithmic kernel,

<a id="sr:full-kernel"></a>

$$
\qquad\text{(125)}
 \mathcal K(\mathbf x)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\widehat{\mathcal K}(\mathbf u)
       e^{2\pi i\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf x}\,d\mathbf u,\qquad
 \int(1+\|\mathbf u\|)^J|\widehat{\mathcal K}(\mathbf u)|\,d\mathbf u<\infty.
$$

Bounded Euler derivatives of $\widehat\Psi$ and integration by parts of order $>J+d$ give live-column-independent seminorm control. Separate the second full kernel/roots in the same order.

Extend [(120)](#sr:first-poisson) off coprimality using separate Gauss sums, fixed bicharacter and original masks. Insert complete $\sum_{s\mid(a,b)}\mu(s)$ before factorwise estimates; artificial primes gain no common-support restrictions. Expand the ray factor and apply joint Cauchy after [(125)](#sr:full-kernel), giving

<a id="sr:gauss-column"></a>

$$
\qquad\text{(126)}
 \sum_h\omega_K(q_h/U^K)
 \left|U^{-(A_0-c)/2}\sum_{s\mid a}
       A_C(a)\tau'_C(a)q_a^{it}\mathfrak g(a,h)\right|^2,
$$

and similarly on the right. Set

$$
B_c=(3c-5d-R_1)_+/6,\qquad B_d=(3d-5c-R_1)_+/6,
$$

<a id="sr:target-exponents"></a>

$$
\qquad\text{(127)}
 S_C=p+A_0-c+R_1+E_1+B_c,\quad
 S_D=p+A_0-d+R_1+E_1+B_d,\quad
 O_0=M-A_0-R_1/2-E_1.
$$

By [(MF3.56)](#mf:eq:B3.56), $O_0+(S_C+S_D)/2\le M$. A fixed divisor width $s_0$ leaves column allowance $A_0-c+R_1+E_1+B_c-s_0$; one common-label count $p+s_0$ gives $S_C$. Keep that count inside joint weights.

Let $j$ index actual first columns, divisors and ray characters in a common box, with chosen common ideal $C_j$. An allocation $B=(B_i,B_1,B_2)$ extracts each factor's complete $C_j$-part, $\prod_iB_iB_1B_2=C_j$. Freeze supplying slots; survivors keep coefficients. Divide both rectangle scales of each plain by the same $q_{B_k}$ and puncture all residual factors at complete support, even if exponents cancel.

Let $F_B$ be the actual frozen coefficient with profiles, $M_B=\prod_{i\,\mathrm{frozen}}M_i$ its bound. Retain $F_B=0$ before enlargement. For slot support bound $b$ and ambient count $N$, allocation Cauchy gives

<a id="sr:allocation-weight"></a>

$$
\qquad\text{(128)}
 \lambda_{j,B}=
 \begin{cases}
 |\rho_j|^2(\max(1,b))^N
       \dfrac{\#\operatorname{Alloc}(C_j)}{q_{C_j}}M_B^2,&F_B\ne0,\\
 0,&F_B=0.
 \end{cases}
$$

Let $I_B$ be the surviving slots. The actual child volume and exact central scalar are

$$
V_{j,B}=\frac{X_1X_2}{q_{B_1}q_{B_2}}\prod_{i\in I_B}P_i,\qquad
 \frac{V_{j,B}}V=\frac1{q_{C_j}}\prod_{i\notin I_B}\frac{q_{p_i}}{P_i}.
$$

Factoring $F_B$, the original normalized sum is exactly $F_B\sqrt{V_{j,B}/V}$ times the $V_{j,B}^{-1/2}$-normalized child. Since $q_{p_i}/P_i\le b$, its squared scalar is $\le(\max(1,b))^NM_B^2/q_{C_j}$, yielding [(128)](#sr:allocation-weight). Actual child volume divides its energy; the first allocation weight stays undivided.

The scalar $\rho_j$ retains the first Poisson coefficient. For original complex block scalar $a_j$, including [(121)](#sr:physical-mass)'s phase, an asymmetric split is

$$
\rho_{C,j}=a_jU^{-O_0-S_C/2},\qquad \rho_{D,j}=U^{-S_D/2}.
$$

Five geometry coordinates vary by $\le\log_U2$ per box; the positive-part allowance varies by at most $3/2$ times this width. Cross-label Cauchy costs $U^{5\log_U2}$, a constant, after freezing common coordinates—not the square of the label count.

For extracted datum $s$, let $\beta_s$ be [(118)](#sr:beta)'s residual coefficient without $F_B$, $\tau_s$ its whole character and $V_s$ its actual volume. Define

<a id="sr:normalized-gauss"></a>

$$
\qquad\text{(129)}
 G(s;\Omega,L)=\frac1{V_s}\sum_{h\in\mathcal O}\Omega(q_h/L)
 \left|\sum_u\beta_s(u)\tau_s(u)q_u^{it}\mathfrak g(u,h)\right|^2 .
$$

The side budget is $\mathcal L=\sum_{j,B}\lambda_{j,B}G(s_{j,B};\Omega,L_j)$, with fixed annular majorant on $[1/8,2]$, including all columns/allocations.

The column window has an independent Mellin coordinate: left/conjugate-right raw heights are $t+2\pi(u-v)$, $t+2\pi(u+v)$. Window densities have common finite weighted $L^1$ norms by integration by parts; Minkowski integrates the polynomial-height $\mathcal L$ bound through both full windows. Bounded row-profile parameters and partition scalars contract the joint norm.

<a id="sr:amplifier"></a>


#### Uniform analytic closure

Choose geometric cells, mesh, strict scalar reserves and support padding
before live scales, and the mesh before the dictionary. Then choose one
finite profile order over subsets and the four derivative pairs, with
no error charged separately to each slot. Choose seminorm and height
orders backwards through both full kernels and functional equations,
before live labels and heights.

Integrate retained heights against (125)'s full densities. For external
cutoffs, fix the height degree before the tail order that dominates it
and the raw counts. Discard genuine Poisson tails before separation,
using their arguments at least \(U^{\xi/4}\),
\(|\mathfrak g|\le\sqrt{q_u}\), and \(|F|\le q_uq_v\).
This gives arbitrary decay with both independent ordinary heights.

The physical mass (121) and the first allocation weights (128) enter
the joint divisor and physical-column budget proved in Appendix C.8.
Its diagonal, fixed-inducing and tail parts are proved in Appendix C.9;
Appendix C.10(30)–(35) converts the remaining packed price and combines
them with that budget. This contracts the actual first labels once,
keeps the artificial divisor inside joint Cauchy, and retains all zeros,
original masks, prefixes and shortened volumes. No obsolete numerical
amplifier budget or additional density payment is a premise of this route.


### C.6. Masked packed twins and inducing invariance


Fix either first-side orientation. Let \(C_s\) be its first common ideal, \(Z_0\) its exponent-zero prime product, \(V_0\ne0\) its packed multiplier, and \(j_0\) its finite dictionary index. The required first-side facts are
\[
 Z_0\mid C_s,\qquad C_s\mid R,
\tag{T1}
\]
and, for supported \(I\) coprime to \(Z_0\),
\[
 h_{\mathrm{base}}(t,I)
 =h_{\mathrm{anchor}(\eta,j_0)}(t,I)\chi_I(V_0)
 \quad(t\in\mathbb R).
\tag{T2}
\]

Take the actual retained second family over
\(\mathrm{childCharacter}(\mathrm{base},\xi)\). Its supplying contract includes genuine Hecke characters \(\tau_\chi\) and
\[
 h_{\tau_\chi}(t,I)
 =
 h_{\mathrm{childCharacter}(\mathrm{base},\xi)}(t,I)
 \chi_I(A_2)\chi(\mathrm{primary}(I))
\tag{T3}
\]
for supported \(I\) satisfying
\((C_2,I)=1\) or \((D_2,I)=1\), uniformly for every \(t\). Here
\[
 A_2=\mathrm{commonFrequencyGenerator}(C_2,D_2)
       \,\mathrm{nonunitFrequencyGenerator}(C_2,D_2,U)\ne0.
\]
The family also supplies the all-element row realization identifying its original nonexceptional predicate with
\[
 z\ne0\ \land\
 \neg\mathrm{FixedInducingRow}_{\tau_\chi,Q}(m_0,1,z),
 \qquad m_0=\mathrm{fixedBadMask}.
\tag{T4}
\]
This use requires the original mask \(m\ne0\), with \(\lambda\mid m\) and \(2\mid m\), as in that realization.

Put
\[
 j=j_0\xi\chi,\qquad \sigma=\mathrm{anchor}(\eta,j),
 \qquad V=V_0A_2\ne0.
\]
Combining (T2), (T3) and the finite-ray multiplication identity gives
\[
 h_{\tau_\chi}(t,I)=h_\sigma(t,I)\chi_I(V)
\tag{T5}
\]
when \(I\) avoids \(Z_0\) and either second common ideal. This remains only a masked identity.

##### Existence of the twin

Choose a genuine Hecke character \(\widetilde\tau\), once for \((\sigma,V)\), with
\[
 a_{\widetilde\tau}(I)=a_\sigma(I)\chi_I(V)
 \quad\text{for every supported }I.
\tag{T6}
\]
It exists by the retained second-height construction with base \(\sigma\), trivial additional ray character and multiplier \(V\). Its hypotheses are precisely: \(\sigma\) is a genuine Hecke character, \(V\ne0\), and \(m_0\ne0\) contains \(\lambda\) and \(2\).

To see the construction, realize the multiplicative periodic element row
\[
 n\longmapsto
 \mathrm{rowTwist}_{\mathrm{childCharacter}(\sigma,1)}
                         (m_0,1,V;n)
\]
as a finite-modulus, unit-invariant character. On a supported ideal, the \(m_0^6\) factor equals one with its original coprimality mask, and the trivial ray factor equals one. This proves (T6), and multiplication by \((NI)^{it}\) proves its height version for **all** \(t\). The choice is independent of profiles and heights.

Its explicit conductor bound is
\[
 N\mathfrak q_{\widetilde\tau}
 \le
 N\mathfrak q_{\mathrm{childCharacter}(\sigma,1)}
 N(m_0)N(72)\,N(V).
\tag{T7}
\]
Thus the moving \(N(V)\) is retained. This construction introduces no additional independent character-width charge after packing.

##### Why the original masked polynomial agrees with the twin

Let \(G=C_2\) or \(G=D_2\), and let \(c(J)\) denote the **original** finite column coefficient, with its cube-free test, seed, ordinary and marked holes, prefixes and centered profiles intact. Define
\[
 b(I)=1_{(G,I)=1}\,1_{D\mid I}\,c(GI).
\tag{T8}
\]
A nonzero original column satisfies
\[
 c(J)\ne0\Longrightarrow(J,R)=1.
\tag{T9}
\]
Indeed, its finite tuple sum then has a nonzero summand, and that summand contains the original coprimality indicator against \(R\).

By (T1), a nonzero coefficient in (T8) therefore has
\[
 (I,Z_0)=1,\qquad(G,I)=1.
\]
Consequently (T5) and (T6) imply
\[
 b(I)h_{\tau_\chi}(v,I)
 =b(I)h_{\widetilde\tau}(v,I)
 \quad\text{for every residual column and every }v.
\tag{T10}
\]
If a mask fails, or \(c(GI)=0\), both sides vanish. Thus the two complete original masked polynomials agree. No column mask has yet been removed.

##### Exact fixed-inducing invariance

The comparison also preserves the physical keep predicate. The needed finite-mask statement is:

> If genuine characters \(\rho,\rho'\) satisfy
> \[
> a_{\rho'}(n)=1_{(n,w)=1}a_\rho(n),\qquad w\ne0,
> \]
> then existence of a primitive inducing character whose conductor divides the fixed ideal \(Q\) is equivalent for \(\rho\) and \(\rho'\).

Here is the descent argument. The forward implication from an inducing character of \(\rho\) to the masked character follows directly from the zero-extension formula. Conversely, suppose the masked character is induced from a primitive character of modulus \(\mathfrak f\). For a unit residue of \(\rho\)'s modulus that is \(1\) modulo the image of \(\mathfrak f\), choose a representative \(a\) with these two congruences. It is coprime to both moduli. By changing \(a\) by a multiple of their product, CRT permits a representative also coprime to \(w\): at primes dividing that product coprimality is automatic, and at every other prime divisor of \(w\) one avoids one residue class. On this representative, the character value is \(1\). Hence \(\rho\) descends through the image of \(\mathfrak f\). Its primitive presentation has conductor dividing \(\mathfrak f\), and therefore dividing \(Q\). This proves the equivalence.

For row characters this statement applies when
\[
 m\ne0,\quad w\ne0,\quad Az\ne0,\quad
 \lambda\mid m,\quad2\mid m.
\]
The row construction supplies genuine characters for both masks, and
\[
 \mathrm{rowTwist}(mw,1,Az;n)
 =1_{(n,w)=1}\mathrm{rowTwist}(m,1,Az;n).
\]
Thus adding or deleting the finite mask \(w\) preserves the literal `FixedInducingRow` predicate, with the same \(Q\).

Apply this with a nonzero generator \(w\) of \(Z_0G\). Away from \(w\), (T5)–(T6) identify the two base coefficients. After adjoining \(w\) to \(m_0\), the complete row functions agree: supported unmasked terms agree, masked terms are zero, and unsupported terms are killed by \(m_0\). Mask invariance then gives
\[
 \mathrm{FixedInducingRow}_{\tau_\chi,Q}(m_0,1,z)
 \iff
 \mathrm{FixedInducingRow}_{\widetilde\tau,Q}(m_0,1,z).
\tag{T11}
\]
For the twin, (T6) gives directly
\[
 \mathrm{FixedInducingRow}_{\widetilde\tau,Q}(m_0,1,z)
 \iff
 \mathrm{FixedInducingRow}_{\sigma,Q}(m_0,1,Vz).
\tag{T12}
\]
At \(z=0\) both nonfixed keeps are false. Hence, for every \(z\),
\[
 \mathrm{keep}_{\tau_\chi}(z)
 =\mathrm{keep}_{\widetilde\tau}(z)
 =\mathrm{initialKeep}_{\sigma,Q}(Vz).
\tag{T13}
\]
The fixed unit-generator factor in the definition of `initialKeep` is removed by the same exact mask invariance.

Equations (T10) and (T13) prove equality of the literal label energies for all \(v\), without an inequality or an analytic loss.

##### Order of height absorption, packing and restoration

Use the following order:
\[
 \boxed{
 \text{original masked }\tau_\chi\text{-row}
 \ \xrightarrow{\text{height absorption}}\
 \text{same masked row}
 \ \xrightarrow{\text{T10--T13}}\
 \text{masked twin row}
 \ \xrightarrow{y=Vz}\
 \text{masked }\sigma\text{-row}
 \ \xrightarrow{\text{restoration}}\
 \text{native }\sigma\text{-leaves}.}
\tag{T14}
\]
The height absorption retains the phase
\[
 \left(\frac{X_1X_2}{Ne_1Ne_2\,NG}\right)^{iv},
\]
shifts the slot height to \(t+v\), and shifts each ordinary profile parameter to \(t_j+v/(2\pi)\).

The twin satisfies the restoration packing interface with auxiliary mask \(1\): its supported coefficient identity is global, and
\[
 (G,I)=1\Longrightarrow(I,(1))=1
\]
is automatic. The temporary comparison mask \(Z_0G\) is **not** used as that auxiliary mask.

Multiplication by \(V\) gives an exact bijection onto \(V\mathcal O\). Therefore, with the original masked polynomial still present,
\[
 \sum_{\mathrm{keep}_{\widetilde\tau}(z)}
 |\mathcal R^{\rm orig}_{\widetilde\tau,z}|^2\Phi(Nz/K)
 =
 \sum_{\substack{V\mid y\\\mathrm{initialKeep}_{\sigma,Q}(y)}}
 |\mathcal R^{\rm orig}_{\sigma,y}|^2
 \Phi\!\left(\frac{Ny}{NVK}\right).
\tag{T15}
\]
There is no Jacobian or additional power loss.

### C.7. Cube-free restoration and fixed-inducing contribution


Write \(\mathcal O=\mathbb Z[\omega]\), and write \(NI\) for the absolute norm of a nonzero integral ideal. Every character below has its original zero extension. In particular, a coefficient that vanishes because its ideal meets the presented modulus remains zero after every identity.

Fix a finite slot set \(\mathcal I\), a common prime profile \(W\) supported in \([1,2]\), and a compact ordinary-profile interval \([a,b]\), where \(a>0\). The genuine slot coefficients have the form
\[
 \beta_i(\mathfrak p)=
 \nu_i(\mathfrak p)\,
 W(N\mathfrak p/P_i)
 (N\mathfrak p/P_i)^{-\sigma_i+i f_i},
\]
with the original relative finite-ray character \(\nu_i\), its natural zeros, its finite hole set, and its inherited norm height. The real powers \(\sigma_i\) lie in a fixed compact interval. Consequently
\[
 |\beta_i(\mathfrak p)|\leq B_f
\tag{1}
\]
with one \(B_f\geq1\) independent of the slot frequencies and inherited heights.

All constants in the restoration statements are chosen after the fixed field, slot number, profile \(W\), real-power interval, hole-cardinality bound and fixed polynomial caps, but before the moving characters, prime pools, rows, ordinary profiles, heights, allocations and positive shortened scales.

##### 1. Exact local and labelled identities

Put
\[
 F=\frac1{(1-x)(1-y)},\qquad B=(1-x)(1-y),
\]
\[
 T_3=1+x+y+x^2+xy+y^2,\qquad H_3=BT_3.
\]
Multiplication gives
\[
 H_3
 =1-(x^3+x^2y+xy^2+y^3)
   +(x^3y+x^2y^2+xy^3).
\tag{2}
\]
Thus \(T_3\) represents the literal condition
\[
 v_{\mathfrak p}(I)+v_{\mathfrak p}(J)<3.
\]
Here \(I,J\) are the ordinary indices of the stored source. Any original prefix ideals remain in their profiles and extraction scalars; they are not silently inserted into, or removed from, this condition.

Let \(\zeta^2=0\) represent one supplying marked prime. The unrestricted marked local factor is \(F+\zeta F\); the restricted factor is \(T_3+\zeta\), because a supplying prime must divide neither ordinary index. Define
\[
 K_3=H_3+\zeta(B-H_3).
\]
Then
\[
 K_3(F+\zeta F)=T_3+\zeta,
\tag{3}
\]
and
\[
 K_3^{-1}
 =H_3^{-1}+\zeta(H_3-B)H_3^{-2},
\qquad
 K_3^{-1}(T_3+\zeta)=F+\zeta F.
\tag{4}
\]
For example, the marked coefficient in (3) is
\(H_3F+(B-H_3)F=BF=1\). In (4), it is
\[
 H_3^{-1}+(H_3-B)H_3^{-2}T_3=F,
\]
using \(H_3=BT_3\).

These are formal-series identities: analytic division is unnecessary. For the labelled global identity, each prime either supplies no marked label or supplies exactly one label. The corresponding supplying map is injective. Square-zero notation alone does not assert that different marked labels choose different primes.

The forward marked polynomial is
\[
 B-H_3
 =-x-y+xy+x^3+x^2y+xy^2+y^3
   -x^3y-x^2y^2-xy^3.
\tag{5}
\]
The inverse marked series is exactly
\[
 (H_3-B)H_3^{-2}.
\tag{6}
\]
It multiplies \(T_3\) in (4). Replacing it by a coefficient obtained from a punctured ordinary series would change the source.

Taking coefficients and then products over the finite prime enclosure proves the ideal-pair divisor identities. Reindexing by the extracted ideal pair \(d=(d_1,d_2)\) gives the ordinary scales
\[
 X_1/Nd_1,\qquad X_2/Nd_2.
\tag{7}
\]
At a kernel-frozen marked prime, the remaining marked coefficients acquire the cross-assignment hole excluding that prime. In the inverse identity, this does **not** introduce an extra ordinary puncture there: the remaining restricted ordinary local factor is \(T_3\).

Every coefficient, finite-ray phase, original natural zero and prefix is retained in these finite identities.

##### 2. Central inverse norm

Write
\[
 H_3^{-1}=\sum_{i,j\geq0}q_{ij}x^iy^j.
\]
The constant coefficient is \(q_{00}=1\). Since the seven nonconstant monomials of \(H_3\) have total degree at least three,
\[
 q_{ij}=0\quad(0<i+j<3).
\tag{8}
\]
There is no larger rectangular zero region.

The recurrence obtained from \(H_3H_3^{-1}=1\) also gives
\[
 |q_{ij}|\leq2^{i+j}.
\tag{9}
\]
Indeed, induct on \(d=i+j\). The assertion is immediate for \(d=0,1,2\). For \(d\geq3\), the recurrence contains at most seven preceding coefficients, each of degree at most \(d-3\). Their total absolute value is at most
\(7\,2^{d-3}\leq2^d\).

For \(0\leq z\leq2/5\), put \(r=2z\leq4/5\). Equations (8)–(9) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{i,j}|q_{ij}|z^{i+j}
 &\leq1+\sum_{n\geq3}(n+1)r^n\\
 &=1+\frac{r^3(4-3r)}{(1-r)^2}\\
 &\leq1+320z^3
 \leq1+400z^3.
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
The penultimate inequality follows from
\[
 \frac{4-3r}{(1-r)^2}
 =(1-r)^{-2}+3(1-r)^{-1}\leq25+15.
\]
This proves absolute summability of the entire reciprocal, uniformly over every finite coefficient cutoff.

For the present supported primes,
\[
 N\mathfrak p\equiv1\pmod6,\qquad N\mathfrak p\geq7.
\]
Hence \(z=(N\mathfrak p)^{-1/2}\leq2/5\), and
\[
 \sum_{i,j}|q_{ij}|(N\mathfrak p)^{-(i+j)/2}
 \leq1+400(N\mathfrak p)^{-3/2}.
\tag{11}
\]
Unique ideal factorization and positivity therefore give, for every finite family of supported ideal pairs,
\[
 \sum_d\frac{|q(d_1,d_2)|}{\sqrt{Nd_1Nd_2}}
 \leq
 \exp\!\left(400\sum_{\mathfrak p\ {\rm supported}}
                 (N\mathfrak p)^{-3/2}\right)
 =:C_{\rm inv}<\infty.
\tag{12}
\]
Restrictions on the ideal pairs only reduce this positive majorant.

The inverse marked series must also be included. The ten monomials of \(H_3-B\) have absolute coefficient one and positive total degree. Thus
\[
 \|H_3-B\|_z\leq10z\leq14z.
\]
By (10), \(\|H_3^{-1}\|_z\leq27\) for \(z\leq2/5\). Submultiplicativity of absolute coefficient mass yields
\[
 \|(H_3-B)H_3^{-2}\|_z
 \leq14z\cdot27^2=10206z.
\tag{13}
\]
The supplying slot contributes one further central factor \(z\). Its complete local inverse mass is consequently at most
\[
 10206(N\mathfrak p)^{-1}.
\tag{14}
\]
For a fixed number \(m\) of frozen slots, summing all their prime choices costs an arbitrarily small power of the prime enclosure. For instance, for every \(\epsilon>0\), choose
\(\delta=\epsilon/(m+1)\). If \(N\mathfrak p\leq X\), then
\[
 \sum_{\mathfrak p\leq X}(N\mathfrak p)^{-1}
 \leq X^\delta\sum_{\mathfrak p}
                  (N\mathfrak p)^{-1-\delta}.
\]
The \(m\)-fold assignment sum is \(O_{\epsilon,m}(X^\epsilon)\). Allowing optional assignments, collisions or additional forbidden primes in this **positive majorant** preserves the upper bound. The exact source continues to use its actual admissible assignments.

Combining (12)–(14) proves the complete central inverse norm, including every frozen marked correction and every finite cutoff. No reciprocal coefficient is omitted.

##### 3. Reflected forward norm and the prime enclosure

For an ordinary monomial \(x^iy^j\), central extraction followed by the actual reflected length ratio gives
\[
 (N\mathfrak p)^{-(i+j)/2}
 (N\mathfrak p)^{(j-i)/6}
 =(N\mathfrak p)^{-(2i+j)/3}.
\tag{15}
\]
The monomial \(y^3\) therefore has weight \((N\mathfrak p)^{-1}\). The sum of the eight absolute local weights is
\[
 1+p^{-1}+p^{-4/3}+2p^{-5/3}+2p^{-2}+p^{-7/3}
 \leq1+7p^{-1},
 \qquad p=N\mathfrak p.
\tag{16}
\]

We prove the required logarithmic prime-pool estimate directly. Fixed-field ideal counting gives
\[
 \#\{I\ne0:NI\leq H\}\leq128H\qquad(H\geq1).
\]
A dyadic decomposition then gives, for \(0<t\leq1\),
\[
 \sum_I(NI)^{-1-t}
 \leq\frac{256}{1-2^{-t}}
 \leq\frac{768}{t}.
\tag{17}
\]
The last inequality follows from
\(1/(1-2^{-t})\leq3/t\).

Let \(X\geq3\), \(s=1+1/\log X\), and let \(\mathcal P\) be any finite set of nonzero prime ideals with \(N\mathfrak p\leq X\). Distinct subsets of \(\mathcal P\) have distinct ideal products, so
\[
 \prod_{\mathfrak p\in\mathcal P}
       \bigl(1+(N\mathfrak p)^{-s}\bigr)
 \leq\sum_I(NI)^{-s}
 \leq768\log X.
\]
Also
\[
 (N\mathfrak p)^{-1}\leq3(N\mathfrak p)^{-s},
 \qquad
 u/2\leq\log(1+u)\quad(0\leq u\leq1).
\]
Taking logarithms proves
\[
 \sum_{\mathfrak p\in\mathcal P}(N\mathfrak p)^{-1}
 \leq6\log\log X+6\log768.
\tag{18}
\]
Equations (16)–(18) imply the explicit source bound
\[
 \prod_{\mathfrak p\in\mathcal P}
  \sum_{\text{eight monomials}}|\text{reflected weight}|
 \leq
 e^{42\log768}(\log X)^{42}.
\tag{19}
\]

For a marked monomial \(x^iy^j\) of (5), the supplying factor and reflected ratio instead give
\[
 p^{-(i+j+1)/2}p^{(j-i-1)/6}
 =p^{-(2i+j+2)/3}.
\tag{20}
\]
Every exponent on the right is at least one. Thus the full marked local weight is at most \(10/p\), and the retained source constant \(14/p\) is valid.

For a fixed supplying map, multiply the ordinary product (19) by the corresponding marked weights. Summing its fixed number of labels adds at most a fixed power of the prime harmonic sum. Consequently every complete forward critical mass is bounded by
\[
 C(1+\log X)^{42}
       (1+\log\log(3X))^{|\mathcal I|}.
\tag{21}
\]
In particular, it is \(O_\epsilon(X^\epsilon)\), uniformly over all admissible finite prime sets and ideal cutoffs.

The actual reflected ratio uses the **whole** frozen marked product:
\[
 r(d,\mathbf p)=
 \left(\frac{Nd_2}
 {Nd_1\prod_{i\ {\rm frozen}}N\mathfrak p_i}\right)^{1/6}.
\tag{22}
\]
Multiplying a central scalar majorant by \(r\) changes its ordinary exponents to \(2/3,1/3\) and every supplying exponent to \(2/3\), exactly as in (15) and (20).

If the child energy is bounded by \(E(3+r^2)\), then
\[
 \sqrt{3+r^2}\leq2(1+r).
\]
Minkowski in the positive physical norm therefore bounds the parent energy by
\[
 4\left(\sum_{\rm actual\ allocations}
            w_{\rm central}(1+r)\right)^2E.
\tag{23}
\]
This sums mass-weighted child norm bounds; it does not pay the number of prime assignments.

For the application, every pool lies in
\[
 N\mathfrak p\leq\mathrm{Cap}\,Z^{L_{\rm cap}},
\tag{24}
\]
where \(\mathrm{Cap}\) and \(L_{\rm cap}\) are fixed before \(Z\). Given a final energy loss \(\eta>0\), use (21) with an exponent sufficiently smaller than
\(\eta/[2(L_{\rm cap}+1)]\). Squaring in (23), and absorbing the fixed power of \(\mathrm{Cap}\), costs at most \(CZ^\eta\).

Thus (24) is an essential hypothesis of the reflected transfer. A prime-pool-independent constant is unavailable.

##### 4. Complete restoration, collisions and natural holes

For completeness, the positive-norm passage used above is elementary. If
\[
 F_u=\sum_jc_j(u)G_j(u),\qquad |c_j(u)|\leq w_j,\quad w_j\geq0,
\]
and \(\rho(u)\geq0\), weighted Cauchy gives
\[
 \sum_u\rho(u)|F_u|^2
 \leq\left(\sum_jw_j\right)
       \sum_jw_j\sum_u\rho(u)|G_j(u)|^2.
\tag{25}
\]
The majorants \(w_j\) are independent of the physical row. All row-dependent character phases remain in \(c_j(u)\).

The finite forward and inverse identities of §1 supply precisely such coefficients. Their majorants are proved in §§2–3. Every child has a slot subset, the original ordinary profiles, the original character, and positive scales no greater than its parent scales. A shortened scale below one is retained literally; if its upper profile support contains no positive ideal norm, the child is zero.

Repeated prime slots are handled by the equality partition of the original slot map. For a block \(A\) of \(m\geq2\) equal slots, its complete coefficient is
\[
 \prod_{i\in A}
 \frac{\beta_i(\mathfrak p)\chi_u(\mathfrak p)}{\sqrt{P_i}}.
\]
On its nonzero annuli, \(N\mathfrak p\leq2P_i\), hence
\[
 \left|\prod_{i\in A}
 \frac{\beta_i(\mathfrak p)\chi_u(\mathfrak p)}{\sqrt{P_i}}\right|
 \leq(2B_f)^m(N\mathfrak p)^{-m/2}
 \leq(2B_f)^m(N\mathfrak p)^{-1}.
\tag{26}
\]
The original powers of the character and all coefficients remain until this positive bound is taken. Summing repeated-block primes costs a fixed power of (18). Singleton slots retain the exclusions against every frozen repeated block. Conversely, inclusion–exclusion on the finite partition lattice expresses an injective singleton polynomial in full natural products and repeated-block corrections, again with (26). The finite partition coefficients depend only on \(|\mathcal I|\).

For a common ordinary puncture \(\mathfrak R\), the exact formula is
\[
 P_{\chi,\mathfrak R}(X;W)
 =\sum_{D\mid\operatorname{rad}\mathfrak R}
   \frac{\mu(D)\chi(D)}{\sqrt{ND}}\,
   P_\chi(X/ND;W).
\tag{27}
\]
The character’s existing zeros are unchanged. A marked hole is removed by subtracting the corresponding actual prime terms; finite holes produce slot subsets and retain their original coefficients.

If \(N\operatorname{rad}\mathfrak R\leq Z^{B_{\rm mask}}\), the total coefficient mass in (27), together with these marked deletions, is \(O_\eta(Z^\eta)\). To see this without a uniform-small-prime assumption, split the prime divisors at a fixed threshold. At large primes each local factor \(1+C p^{-u}\), \(u>0\), is at most \(p^\delta\); the finitely many smaller prime factors contribute a fixed constant. The same argument bounds \(C^{\omega(\mathfrak R)}\) by \(C_\delta(N\mathfrak R)^\delta\).

Combining these exact decompositions with (25) proves:

> **Complete cube-free restoration.** Suppose a common bound \(E\geq0\) holds for every literal restricted child arising from every equality partition, repeated-block assignment, frozen supplying assignment, resulting cross-hole, slot subset, and every positive shortened ordinary pair. Then the original full natural product has physical energy at most \(CZ^\eta E\). The constant precedes all those choices.

This is a transfer statement with its child family displayed. It supplies no estimate for unrelated coefficients or inadmissible lengths.

##### 5. Quantitative reduction of an actual second label

We now prove the bridge requested for collection.

Fix one actual second label \((G,D,e)\), where \(D=t_2\) is squarefree, \(G\ne0\), \(e_1,e_2\ne0\), and the original seed satisfies \(\mathrm{seed}\mid G\). Retain the literal common puncture \(R\ne0\), ordinary-hole set \(H\), slot-hole sets \(R_{0,i}\), and the original centered finite-column coefficient.

The fixed parameters satisfy
\[
a>0,\quad b\ge1,\quad
0\le L_{\rm slot}\le L_{\rm cap},\quad
L\le L_{\rm cap},\quad
\mathrm{Cap}\ge\max(2,b),\quad B_{\rm mask}\ge0.
\]
The common slot profile is smooth and supported in \([1,2]\). The slot data satisfy
\[
P_i=Z^{w_i},\qquad 0\le w_i\le L_{\rm slot},
\qquad \mathrm{lo}\le\sigma_i\le\mathrm{hi},
\qquad |R_{0,i}|\le\mathrm{Holes}.
\]
The ordinary profiles \(W_1,W_2\) are Schwartz functions supported in \([a,b]\). All four ordinary scales are positive, at most \(Z^L\), and
\[
X_1X_2=Y_1Y_2=T,\qquad
\mathcal X=T\prod_iP_i.
\]
Put \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{enclosure}(\mathrm{Cap}Z^{L_{\rm cap}})\). Require
\[
H\subseteq\mathcal S,\qquad
\mathfrak p\in H\Longrightarrow\mathfrak p\in R_{0,i}
\quad\text{for every live slot }i,
\tag{28a}
\]
and
\[
N\!\left(\prod_{\mathfrak p\in
\operatorname{primeSupport}(RGD)\,\cup\,\operatorname{holes}(H)}
\mathfrak p\right)\le Z^{B_{\rm mask}}.
\tag{28b}
\]
The complete ordinary-prime enclosure is retained. Explicitly, every supported ideal in either ordinary support, including either rectangle and every subsequently shortened support, has its prime support in \(\mathcal S\). This follows from the displayed caps: for example,
\[
NI\le b\,X_j/NE\le \mathrm{Cap}Z^{L_{\rm cap}},
\]
since \(NE\ge1\); each prime factor has norm at most \(NI\). The same reasoning covers the \(Y\)-rectangle and all further shortenings.

The canonical physical norm has \(K>0\), nonnegative radial weight, and
\(\mathrm{keep}(z)\Rightarrow z\ne0\). In the actual application,
\[
K=\operatorname{dyadicScale}(n_1),\qquad
\Phi=\operatorname{ballProfile},
\]
with \(\Phi\ge0\) and support bounded above by \(2\).

Before removing any \(G\), \(D\), seed or coefficient-hole restriction, absorb the independent residual height \(v\) into the **original masked row**. The exact identity is
\[
\frac{E_{G,D,e}}{\mathcal X}
=
\mathcal E_{\mathrm{keep}_\tau,\Phi,K}
\bigl[\mathcal R^{\,\mathrm{orig}}_{\tau,z}\bigr],
\tag{35a}
\]
where \(\mathcal R^{\,\mathrm{orig}}\) still contains all the original masks and has heights
\[
t\longmapsto t+v,\qquad
t_j\longmapsto t_j+\frac{v}{2\pi}.
\]
Before taking its norm, the extracted scalar phase is
\[
\left(\frac{T}{Ne_1Ne_2\,NG}\right)^{iv}.
\]
Its modulus is one; both original prefixes and \(G\) remain in the identity.

At the actual second-family application, the character in (35a) is the
original \(\tau_{\rm orig}\). Before the next step, apply the shared
packed-twin bridge (T1)–(T15), proved in section Appendix C.6.
Its hypotheses include \(Z_0\mid C_s\mid R\), the actual first- and
second-height identities and the coefficient-sensitive implication
\(b(I)\ne0\Rightarrow(I,Z_0)=1\). No implication from \((G,I)=1\)
alone to \((I,Z_0)=1\) is asserted. The original masked energy and keep
equal those of the genuine twin \(\widetilde\tau\), with coefficients
\(a_{\widetilde\tau}(I)=a_{\sigma_A}(I)\chi_I(V)\) on every supported
ideal. In (35b)–(35d), \(\tau\) denotes this twin and \(w_m=1\).
The temporary comparison mask \(Z_0G\) is never used as its auxiliary mask.

Now apply the actual packing dictionary. Its hypotheses are \(V\ne0\), \(w_m\ne0\), and
\[
a_\tau(I)=a_{\sigma_A}(I)\operatorname{idealRowHom}(V;I)
\]
for supported \(I\) coprime to \((w_m)\), together with
\[
(G,I)=1\Longrightarrow (I,(w_m))=1.
\tag{35b}
\]
The dictionary transports the literal canonical keep:
\[
\mathrm{keep}_\tau(z)
\iff\operatorname{initialKeep}_{\sigma_A,Q}(Vz).
\tag{35c}
\]
On every original masked residual column, (35b) therefore identifies its natural-character coefficient at \((\tau,z)\) with that at \((\sigma_A,Vz)\). Unsupported columns vanish on both sides. Consequently
\[
\mathcal E_{\mathrm{keep}_\tau,\Phi,K}
[\mathcal R^{\,\mathrm{orig}}_{\tau,z}]
=
\mathcal E_{\substack{V\mid y\\
\operatorname{initialKeep}_{\sigma_A,Q}(y)},\,
\Phi,\,NVK}
[\mathcal R^{\,\mathrm{orig}}_{\sigma_A,y}].
\tag{35d}
\]
Multiplication by \(V\) is a bijection onto \(V\mathcal O\), and
\(N(Vz)/(NVK)=Nz/K\); there is no Jacobian factor.

The residual coefficient is still supported on
\[
(G,I)=1,\qquad D\mid I.\tag{29}
\]
**Only after (35d)** perform the genuine-\(G\) allocation, squarefree-\(D\) allocation, seed identity, kernel expansion, collision completion and hole deletion. These operate on the packed \(\sigma_A\)-row, with all original masks present at the start. First allocate the complete \(G\)-part of every tuple coordinate.  Because of \((G,I)=1\), this is the canonical prime-support decomposition, not an arbitrary allocation of a radical. Write its frozen tuple as \(B_j\), so
\(\prod_jB_j=G\). The remaining ordinary prefixes are
\[
 e_1B_0,\qquad e_2B_1.
\tag{30}
\]
At each prime, cube-freeness splits between frozen and live ordinary products because these products are coprime. Frozen marked slots impose their actual frozen restrictions; live marked slots retain their cross-holes. This proves the coefficient identity before taking a norm.

The normalization saving is the full \(NG\). Indeed, let
\[
 \operatorname{rawReduction}(B)
   =NB_0NB_1\prod_{i\ {\rm frozen}}P_i.
\]
A nonzero frozen slot has \(NB_i\leq2P_i\), while each original marked coordinate is prime. Thus
\[
 \operatorname{rawReduction}(B)\geq2^{-|\mathcal I|}NG.
\]
If \(c_B\) denotes its original frozen coefficient,
\[
 \frac{|c_B|^2}{\operatorname{rawReduction}(B)}
 \leq\frac{2^{|\mathcal I|}B_f^{2|\mathcal I|}}{NG}.
\tag{31}
\]
Together with (30), the exact full-to-live normalization gives the denominator
\(NG\,Ne_1Ne_2\).

The number of genuine \(G\)-allocations, squared, is
\(O_\delta((NG)^\delta)\). For \(k=|\mathcal I|+2\), it is bounded by a fixed power of the ideal divisor function. The bound
\(\tau(G)^A\ll_{\delta,A}(NG)^\delta\) follows prime by prime: large primes absorb \((v+1)^A\) into \(p^{\delta v}\), and the finitely many small primes have bounded remaining suprema.

Next impose \(D\mid I\) exactly. For each \(\mathfrak p\mid D\),
\[
 1_{\mathfrak p\mid\prod_jI_j}
 =\sum_{\varnothing\ne A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,k\}}
      (-1)^{|A|+1}\prod_{j\in A}1_{\mathfrak p\mid I_j}.
\tag{32}
\]
Thus an allocation may select the same prime in several coordinates. Let \(D_j\) be its selected divisors. Then
\[
 D\mid\prod_jD_j,\qquad N\prod_jD_j\geq ND.
\tag{33}
\]
All selected copies remain in the extraction denominator.

To apply (32) to the actual restricted coefficient, retain the whole \(D\)-supported part of each coordinate, including exponent two where present. The shifted cube-free test is evaluated on this frozen part. The residual coordinates are coprime to \(D\), so their cube-free test splits exactly. This is the bounded-label decomposition; it does not replace a shifted restriction by a fresh unshifted one. There are \(O_\delta((ND)^\delta)\) squared allocation and bounded-label costs: cube-free ordinary coordinates have only the exponents \(0,1,2\), and marked prime coordinates only \(0,1\), giving a fixed local number of choices per prime of \(D\). Equation (33) supplies \(1/ND\).

After the packed-row decompositions, the resulting leaves are the full normalized natural products defined below. They have no remaining extraction prefix, seed condition, cube-free restriction, extra ordinary puncture, marked distinctness condition or finite coefficient hole. Their original natural-character zeros remain.

For a positive scale \(U\), define
\[
\mathscr P_{\chi,j}(U)
=U^{-1/2}\sum_Ia_\chi(I)\,
W_j(NI/U)(NI/U)^{\,i(2\pi t_j+v)}.
\]
For each original canonical prime pool define
\[
\mathscr Q_{\chi,i}
=P_i^{-1/2}\sum_{\mathfrak p\in\mathcal P_i^{\rm can}}
a_\chi(\mathfrak p)\,
a_{\nu_i}(\mathfrak p)\,
\operatorname{annularWeight}
      (W,P_i,\sigma_i,t+v+f_i;\mathfrak p).
\]
These are the original relative-character and annular coefficients, with the inherited height absorbed. Expressing a height as \(N\mathfrak p^{\,i(t+v)}\) instead contributes the fixed unit phase \(P_i^{\,i(t+v)}\); the exact height dictionary retains this phase until the squared norm.

For \(A\subseteq\mathcal I\), the packed leaf is
\[
\mathcal L_{A,U_1,U_2}
=
\sum_{\substack{y\in V\mathcal O\\
\operatorname{initialKeep}_{\sigma_A,Q}(y)}}
\Phi\!\left(\frac{Ny}{NVK}\right)
\left|
\mathscr P_{\chi_{\sigma_A,y},1}(U_1)
\mathscr P_{\chi_{\sigma_A,y},2}(U_2)
\prod_{i\in A}\mathscr Q_{\chi_{\sigma_A,y},i}
\right|^2 .
\tag{34a}
\]
Equivalently, use \(y=Vz\), radial scale \(K\), and keep
\(\operatorname{initialKeep}_{\sigma_A,Q}(Vz)\). Every leaf uses this same packed radial norm and keep predicate.

The finite generated scale family consists of positive pairs satisfying either
\[
U_1\le X_1,\ U_2\le X_2,
\quad\text{or}\quad
U_1\le Y_1,\ U_2\le Y_2.
\]
The restoration argument proves, for every common upper bound \(E\ge0\) on all these leaves,
\[
E_{G,D,e}\le M_{G,D,e}E,
\]
where
\[
M_{G,D,e}
=
CZ^\eta\mathcal X
\frac{(NG)^\delta(ND)^\delta}
{NG\,ND\,Ne_1Ne_2}.
\tag{34b}
\]
All leaves are nonnegative and their family is finite. Hence, if that family is nonempty, a largest leaf gives
\(E_{G,D,e}\le M_{G,D,e}\mathcal L_{A,U_1,U_2}\).
Its slot subset and scale pair may depend on the actual label, both ordinary profiles, all heights and \(v\). **Only the mass constant \(C\) is uniform.** If the family is empty, apply the domination with \(E=0\).

Thus (34) is a finite positive combination with coefficient mass at most (34b). Subsequent collection must accommodate every generated leaf; no profile-independent maximizing leaf is asserted.

Let \(E_{G,D,e}\) be the literal unnormalized one-sided residual energy. The preceding argument proves domination by a finite nonnegative combination of canonical leaves \(\mathcal L_\lambda\):
\[
 E_{G,D,e}\leq\sum_\lambda a_\lambda\mathcal L_\lambda,
 \qquad a_\lambda\geq0,
\]
\[
 \boxed{\;
 \sum_\lambda a_\lambda
 \leq
 C Z^\eta\mathcal X
 \frac{(NG)^\delta(ND)^\delta}
      {NG\,ND\,Ne_1Ne_2}.
 \;}
\tag{34}
\]


Finally, retain the stated extraction gain:
\[
 gEnergy=\frac{NG\,ND\,Ne_1Ne_2\,Z^k}{\mathcal X^2}
              E_{G,D,e}.
\]
Equation (34) gives total packed-leaf mass
\[
 \boxed{\;
 C Z^{k+\eta}\,
 \frac{(NG)^\delta(ND)^\delta}{\mathcal X}.
 \;}
\tag{36}
\]
Under \(NG\leq Z^{2B}\), \(ND\leq Z^B\), its additional divisor loss is at most \(Z^{3B\delta}\). This is the complete restoration bridge; subsequent collection of these leaves is separate.

##### 6. Principal cancellation for \(0\leq\alpha<2/3\)

Fix the actual fixed-inducing ideal \(Q\ne0\). A row satisfying the literal `FixedInducingRow` predicate admits a character induced from a primitive character whose conductor divides \(Q\), together with its original natural punctures. This includes the principal primitive character. We do not substitute a condition on a separately simplified raw character.

For every positive rectangle scale \(U\), use
\[
S_{\chi,W,h}(U)
=\sum_Ia_\chi(I)\,
W(NI/U)(NI/U)^{ih}.
\tag{37a}
\]
This is the same `normPowerProfile` \(x\mapsto W(x)x^{ih}\), evaluated at **that rectangle’s own normalized argument** \(NI/U\). In the actual height dictionary, \(h_j=2\pi t_j+v\).

In particular, the first rectangle uses \(NI/X_j\), the second uses \(NI/Y_j\), and extracted children use their own shortened scales. The profile is never replaced by \(W(NI/U)(NI)^{ih}\) without its compensating scale phase.

With this convention, the lattice main term is
\[
c_\chi U\int_0^\infty W(x)x^{ih}\,dx.
\]
Hence the product of the two main terms depends on the scales only through \(U_1U_2=T\), even when \(h_1,h_2\) are independent. This is the equality used in the centered cancellation.

The fixed-ray lattice formula, followed by the exact finite puncture expansion, gives, uniformly for every \(X>0\),
\[
 S_{\chi,W,t}(X)
 =c_\chi X\,I(W,t)+
 O\!\left(Z^\epsilon
          \mathcal S(W)(1+|t|)^J\right),
\tag{37}
\]
where \(W(x)x^{it}\) is the profile and
\(I(W,t)=\int W(x)x^{it}\,dx\), with the fixed lattice measure included. The coefficient \(c_\chi\) is independent of \(X\).

To check uniformity, first apply Poisson to the finitely many primitive ray characters supported by \(Q\). Integration by parts bounds the nonzero frequencies using finitely many profile derivatives. For \(X<1\), counting and the main term give the same bounded error. If \(\mathfrak R\) is the redundant natural radical, insert
\[
 S_{\chi,W,t}(X)
 =\sum_{D\mid\mathfrak R}
       \mu(D)\psi(D)\,S_{\psi,W,t}(X/ND).
\]
Its divisor count is subpower under the presented-modulus cap. The resulting main coefficient is
\(c_\psi\sum_{D\mid\mathfrak R}\mu(D)\psi(D)/ND\), independent of \(X\). Euler derivatives of \(W(x)x^{it}\) have finite-seminorm bounds polynomial in \(1+|t|\). This proves (37) with constants preceding both ordinary profiles and both independent heights.

For two rectangles with equal product \(T\), their main terms in (37) agree. If all four scales are at least \(L\geq1\), expanding the two products and dividing by \(\sqrt T\) gives
\[
 |\text{normalized difference}|
 \ll Z^\epsilon\mathcal S(W_1)\mathcal S(W_2)
 (1+|t_1|+|t_2|)^J\,\sqrt T\,L^{-1}.
\]
For \(L<1\), absolute volume gives the same expression with \(L^{-1}\) replaced by \(1\). Therefore, for every \(0\leq\alpha\leq1\),
\[
 |\text{plain centered rectangle}|
 \ll Z^\epsilon\mathcal S(W_1)\mathcal S(W_2)
 (1+|t_1|+|t_2|)^J\,\sqrt T\,L^{-\alpha}.
\tag{38}
\]

Insert the cube-free restriction by its **forward** divisor identity. At primes avoided by the common holes and supplying marks, the local kernel is \(B\); elsewhere it is \(H_3\). If \(n=Nd_1Nd_2\), each shortened scale is at least \(L/n\), and its product is \(T/n\). The extraction scalar and child cost combine exactly:
\[
 n^{-1/2}\sqrt{T/n}\,(L/n)^{-\alpha}
 =n^{-(1-\alpha)}\sqrt T\,L^{-\alpha}.
\tag{39}
\]
Thus the required kernel mass has exponent
\[
 \sigma=1-\alpha.
\]
From (2), its ordinary local mass is at most \(1+7p^{-3\sigma}\). It is uniformly summable precisely in the used range
\[
 3\sigma>1,\qquad 0\leq\alpha<2/3.
\tag{40}
\]
At an avoided prime, the \(B\)-mass is
\((1+p^{-\sigma})^2\leq4\). If these primes divide an ideal \(F\) with \(NF\leq Z^B\), their product \(4^{\omega(F)}\) is \(O_\epsilon(Z^\epsilon)\), by the fixed-support argument already proved above. Hence the complete mass in (39) is \(O_\epsilon(Z^\epsilon)\).

For each fixed marked assignment, apply this bound with its augmented common-hole ideal. Its norm is bounded by the old hole norm times \(\prod_i2P_i\), hence by \(Z^{2B}\) under the displayed source caps. Summing the original marked coefficients absolutely costs
\[
 \sum_{\mathfrak p\in\mathcal P_i}
       \frac{|\beta_i(\mathfrak p)|}{\sqrt{P_i}}
 \leq256M_i\sqrt{P_i},
\tag{41}
\]
using ideal counting up to \(2P_i\); if that range is empty, the sum is zero.

This proves the homogeneous physical principal estimate
\[
 |\Delta\mathcal R|
 \leq
 C\,\mathcal S(W_1)\mathcal S(W_2)\,
 Z^\epsilon(1+|t_1|+|t_2|)^J
 \left(\prod_i256M_i\right)
 \sqrt{T\prod_iP_i}\,L^{-\alpha}.
\tag{42}
\]
Zero seminorms are handled by homogeneity, before any normalization.

For an original extracted prefix \(e=(e_1,e_2)\), put
\[
 n_e=Ne_1Ne_2,\qquad U_e=\max(Ne_1,Ne_2).
\]
The additional central scalar and shortened volume give
\[
 n_e^{-1/2}\sqrt{(T/n_e)\prod_iP_i}
 =\frac{\sqrt{T\prod_iP_i}}{n_e}.
\]
Combining the \(\alpha\)-estimate with its \(\alpha=0\) instance proves the literal all-scale form
\[
 |\Delta\mathcal R_e|
 \leq
 C\,\mathcal S(W_1)\mathcal S(W_2)\,
 Z^\epsilon(1+|t_1|+|t_2|)^J
 \left(\prod_i256M_i\right)
 \frac{\sqrt{T\prod_iP_i}}{Ne_1Ne_2}
 \left(\max\!\left(1,\frac L{U_e}\right)\right)^{-\alpha}.
\tag{43}
\]
Neither prefix is replaced by a genuine common ideal.

When the finite genuine-allocation budgets are combined, the explicit full marked factor retained by the source is
\[
 1024^{|\mathcal I|}\left(\prod_iM_i\right)^3.
\tag{44}
\]
Constants are not uniform as \(\alpha\uparrow2/3\); the chosen \(\alpha\) precedes the eventual threshold and height cutoff.

##### 7. Exact principal cost used by the root

Let \(A=P+S\). The separately supplied common-factor ledger gives
\[
 F_1\geq c-3u-o,\qquad F_2\geq2b_2/3,
 \qquad c,b_2\geq0.
\]
For \(0\leq\alpha\leq2/3\), (43) yields the exceptional excess
\[
\begin{aligned}
 A-\frac56-F_1-F_2
   -\alpha\max(0,\ell-c-b_2)
 &\leq A-\frac56+3u-\alpha\ell\\
 &\quad -(1-\alpha)c-(2/3-\alpha)b_2+o\\
 &\leq A-\frac56+3u-\alpha\ell+o.
\end{aligned}
\tag{45}
\]
This explains the new lower reference endpoint
\[
 \ell_{\rm low}=\frac32(A+3u_{\max}-5/6).
\tag{46}
\]

Assume the actual selection obeys \(u\le u_{\max}\), and choose the eventual threshold and small losses so that the ledger error satisfies
\[
o\le\omega
\]
uniformly over all retained labels, profiles and admitted heights.

The root reserve satisfies
\[
0<r_{\rm root}\le1/200.
\]
For \(\epsilon>0\), set

\omega=\min(r_{\rm root}/100000,\epsilon/100000),
\qquad \alpha_P=2/3-\omega/2.
\]
Thus \(\omega>0\) and
\[
0<\alpha_P<2/3,\qquad
\alpha_P\in[2/3-\omega,2/3].
\]
On the centered branch,
\[
\ell>\max(0,\ell_{\rm low})+20\omega,\qquad0<\ell<1,
\quad
\ell_{\rm low}=\tfrac32(A+3u_{\max}-5/6).
\]
For every admitted \(\alpha\in[2/3-\omega,2/3]\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
A-\frac56+3u-\alpha\ell+o
&\le A-\frac56+3u_{\max}-\frac23\ell
      +(2/3-\alpha)\ell+o\\
&<-\frac{40}{3}\omega+\omega+\omega\\
&=-\frac{34}{3}\omega\le-9\omega.
\end{aligned}
\tag{47'}
\]
Thus the root margin includes both the replacement \(u\mapsto u_{\max}\) and the uniform error \(o\). On the uncentered branch,

A+3u_{\max}-5/6\le-10\omega
\]
gives the same final bound \(-9\omega\) after adding \(o\).

The midpoint-reference adapter remains restricted to

0\le R\le2,\qquad \rho\ge3\omega/2,
\]
together with its stated reference geometry. For \(\alpha=\alpha_P\),

(2/3-\alpha_P)R=\omega R/2\le\omega\le2\rho/3.
\]
The midpoint-reference reserve and length bound are

P+S-\frac{5R}{6}+\frac{7d}{3}-\frac{2\ell}{3}\le-\rho/3,
\qquad \ell\le R/2.
\]
The displayed width condition therefore proves the required inequality
\[
(2/3-\alpha)\ell+P+S-\frac{5R}{6}+\frac{7d}{3}
                 -\frac{2\ell}{3}\le0.\tag{48}
\] No assertion for unrestricted \(R\) or smaller \(\rho\) is made. The fixed factor \(c_\star^{-\alpha_P}\) remains when the reference length is \(c_\star Z^\ell\).

These calculations pay the weaker cube-free principal theorem. They do not reuse the fifth-free \(\alpha<4/5\) range.


### C.8. Joint divisor and physical packed-row collection


The joint-divisor reduction and packed-row collection can be written without a new arithmetic assumption beyond the separately assigned cube-free restoration and priced-leaf estimates. Three normalizations are essential:

\[
K_{\rm child}=16K\Bigl(\prod_{j\in J}2P_j\Bigr)^4,\qquad
E_x=NG_x\,NL_x\,N d_{1,x}N d_{2,x}\frac{Z^k}{X^2}e_x,
\qquad
w_x=\frac{\rho(G_x)|p_x|}{NL_x}.
\]

The second artificial divisor \(L_x\) need not divide the packed row. Its reciprocal norm must remain in the weight.

This section proves the joint-divisor and packed-row collection. Its leaf and diagonal inputs are supplied in Appendix C.7, §4 and Appendix C.10 and Appendix C.9.

**1. Data, scope, and inherited inputs.**

Work in the retained Eisenstein ring \(\mathcal O\), with its fixed primary generators, completed sextic Gauss rows, reciprocity conventions, and finite ray characters. Write \(NI\) for ideal norm and \(N(z)=N((z))\). A supported ideal is nonzero and avoids the inherited bad primes.

The physical coefficients remain the original finite tuple coefficients:
\[
\beta_u(I)=
 \sum_{\substack{\mathbf a\in\mathcal T\\\prod\mathbf a=I}}
 \mathbf1_{\rm tuple\ restriction}(\mathbf a)\,
 \operatorname{profileCoefficient}_{u}(\mathbf a).
\tag{1}
\]
Here the tuple restriction retains the cube-free ordinary product, injective marked primes, ordinary/marked coprimality, punctures, exterior ideal, and all original seed conditions. The profile coefficient retains both ordinary reference pairs
\[
X_1X_2=Y_1Y_2>0,
\]
both original prefixes, every marked coefficient, and independent ordinary heights. All four ordinary lengths are positive and at most \(Z^L\), with fixed \(L\); they may be smaller than \(1\).

For the eventual grouped estimate, the marked coefficients are the literal relative-character coefficients with
\[
P_i=Z^{w_i},\qquad 0\le w_i\le\mathfrak m,\qquad
\sigma_i=\frac{33}{50}.
\]
Holes have a fixed cardinality cap; frequencies satisfy \(|\nu_i|\le V_f\). Ordinary profiles are Schwartz functions supported in \([a,b]\subset[1/4,9/4]\). The ray modulus, subgroup containing global units, fixed internal reference \(Q\), slot count, enclosure exponent, and mask exponent are structural data. They precede the constants and eventual threshold.

The reused analytic inputs are the retained local Gauss/CRT table, sextic reciprocity, multiplicative primary-generator convention, fixed-inducing mask invariance, whole-kernel Fourier estimate, and primitive-sieve/finite-profile estimates. Their hypotheses remain part of every application below.

The cube-free restoration-to-leaf estimate is stated explicitly in paragraph 8. Its written proof is in Appendix C.7. The subsequent price assigned to a canonical leaf and the diagonal payment are separate dependencies.

**2. Keep the first artificial divisor inside the first Cauchy inequality.**

Let \(\mathcal U\) be a finite family of squarefree ideals. The first physical expression is a sum
\[
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}\mu(u)\,\mathcal M_u,
\]
where \(\mathcal M_u\) uses the actual residual coefficient restricted by \(u\mid I\). After the inherited Fourier representation of the whole kernel, the relevant bilinear expression has joint row index \((u,z)\):
\[
\sum_{u,z}\mu(u)\,\omega_z
          L_{u,v_L}(z)\overline{R_{u,v_R}(\pm z)},
\qquad |\omega_z|\le1.
\]
Cauchy therefore gives
\[
\left|\sum_{u,z}\mu(u)\omega_z
 L_{u,v_L}(z)\overline{R_{u,v_R}(\pm z)}\right|
\le
\left(\sum_{u,z}|L_{u,v_L}(z)|^2\right)^{1/2}
\left(\sum_{u,z}|R_{u,v_R}(\pm z)|^2\right)^{1/2}.
\tag{2}
\]
There is no factor \(\#\mathcal U\) and no preliminary reciprocal-divisor completion.

For either side assume, uniformly for every real \(v\),
\[
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}E_u(v;K)\le E(1+|v|)^{2J}.
\tag{3}
\]
The compact logarithmic window has Fourier moments of every order. Fourier inversion, Minkowski, and (3) bound the windowed side by
\[
\operatorname{windowBudget}_J(t,E)
=\sqrt E\,\operatorname{heightEnvelope}(t)^J
  \operatorname{profileMoment}_J.
\]
The right conjugate window changes its Fourier parameter to its negative. Reflection \(z\mapsto-z\) is a bijection and preserves the radial weight. Thus the two sides retain their independent heights and radii.

This is the mathematical content of `First/JointKernel.summed_kernel_from_raw`. The finite ray projector is applied after (2), with its fixed coefficient mass.

**3. Exact regrouping inside the second physical block.**

Let \(C_2,D_2\) be supported ideals with equal prime support. Its sector columns satisfy
\[
(I,C_2)=(J,D_2)=(I,J)=1.
\]
For squarefree \(u\),
\[
u\mid C_2I,\quad u\mid D_2J
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad u\mid C_2.
\tag{4}
\]
Indeed, a prime dividing \(u\) but absent from the common support would have to divide both \(I\) and \(J\). Conversely, squarefreeness and equality of supports imply that every squarefree divisor of \(C_2\) also divides \(D_2\).

Suppose \(\mathcal U\) contains all squarefree divisors of \(C_2\), and contains only squarefree ideals. Then
\[
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}
 \mathbf1_{u\mid C_2I}\mathbf1_{u\mid D_2J}
=\rho(C_2),\qquad
\rho(G):=2^{\omega(G)}.
\tag{5}
\]

Put
\[
A_2=\operatorname{commonFrequencyGenerator}(C_2,D_2)
       \operatorname{nonunitFrequencyGenerator}(C_2,D_2,U).
\]
The actual physical block is the finite sum of
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\mathbf1_{\rm canonical\ partition}(z)\,
 \mathbf1_{(I,J)=1}\,
 \operatorname{Corr}(C_2I,D_2J;A_2z)\\
&\quad{}\times
 \beta(C_2I)h_\eta(t,I)
 \overline{\beta(D_2J)h_\eta(t,J)}
 \,\mathcal K(C_2,D_2;A_2z,I,J)
 \prod_{\ell=0}^{3}\mathcal D_{n_\ell}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
The four dyadic weights use the actual effective scale, \(N(z)\), \(NI\), and \(NJ\). Every factor except the two seed indicators is independent of \(u\). Substituting (5) termwise proves
\[
\boxed{\quad
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}\operatorname{Block}[\mathbf1_{u\mid\cdot}\beta]
=\rho(C_2)\operatorname{Block}[\beta].
\quad}
\tag{7}
\]
No phase, normalization, angular sector, or coefficient is replaced.

Because (7) holds for every finite row set, it commutes with any row filter. In particular it holds separately for fixed-inducing and nonfixed rows. This identity occurs after the first Hilbert-space Cauchy step; \(\rho(C_2)\) is a positive multiplicity, not a surviving signed Möbius sum.

At a common prime, write the two multiplicities as \(l,r\). The retained local correlation table states that an unequal pair can be nonzero only if \(6\mid\min(l,r)\). The literal cube-free restriction gives \(l,r\in\{1,2\}\). Therefore \(l\ne r\) kills the local correlation at every frequency. CRT then kills the whole summand.

Consequently a nonzero second common contribution has \(C_2=D_2=G\). This conclusion does **not** identify the two first common factors.

For equal second factors, the common frequency generator spans \(G\), and the retained normalized local table gives
\[
|\operatorname{Corr}(G,G;g\,w)|
\le \frac{NG}{N U_{\rm id}}
\quad\text{on the canonical \(U\)-partition},
\tag{8}
\]
where \((g)=G\) and \(U_{\rm id}=\prod_{P\in U}P\). The complementary primes supply the nonunit multiplier in \(A_2\). Both local unit and nonunit cases remain in the exhaustive partition.

**4. Genuine allocation, residual seeds, and fourth-power averaging.**

First extract the genuine first common ideal into the tuple components. Each tuple has a unique prime-by-prime allocation \(\mathcal B\). Thus, on the actual coprime residual sector,
\[
\beta(CI)=\sum_{\mathcal B}
 b_{\mathcal B}\,\beta_{\mathcal B}(I),
\tag{9}
\]
with the frozen tuple restrictions included in \(b_{\mathcal B}\). The live marked prefixes are now \(1\). The artificial condition \(u\mid I\) remains on the whole live product.

Cauchy over genuine allocations costs exactly
\[
\#\mathcal B\sum_{\mathcal B}|b_{\mathcal B}|^2(\cdots).
\tag{10}
\]
The elementary bound \(\#\mathcal B\le\tau(C)^{N+2}\) is paid only later, using the fixed slot count and polynomial norm cap.

Fix one live allocation and selected slot set \(J\). For an assignment \(y\), put
\[
\Delta_y=\prod_{j\in J}y_j,\qquad d_y=\operatorname{primary}(\Delta_y).
\]
The exact selected scalar is
\[
s_y=
\mathbf1_{y\ {\rm injective}}\,
\operatorname{selAmp}(y)\,
\mathbf1_{(\Delta_y,R)=1}\,
h_\tau(t,\Delta_y).
\tag{11}
\]
For squarefree \(u\), let \(v(u,\Delta_y)\) be the product of primes of \(u\) absent from \(\Delta_y\). Primewise,
\[
u\mid\Delta_y I\iff v(u,\Delta_y)\mid I.
\tag{12}
\]
The map \(u\mapsto v(u,\Delta_y)\) has fibers of cardinality at most
\(2^{\omega(\Delta_y)}\le2^{|J|}\).

The retained fourth-power Gauss identity, applied to the **whole** residual vector, gives
\[
Q_u(k)=
\sum_{y,\chi,\xi}
 s_y\,c_{\chi,\xi}\,
 \chi(d_y)\,\mathcal G_{\Delta_y}(k)\,
 Q^{\rm rest}_{v(u,\Delta_y),\,\tau\xi}(d_y^4k).
\tag{13}
\]
Here \(c_{\chi,\xi}\) is the fixed first reciprocity-phase table coefficient. The residual vector depends on \(y\) only through its residual seed. The deleted coprimality restriction in the transferred expression is justified by the inherited Gauss zeros, rather than by arbitrary coefficient enlargement.

The scalar satisfies
\[
|s_yc_{\chi,\xi}\chi(d_y)\mathcal G_{\Delta_y}(k)|^2
\le |c_{\chi,\xi}|^2|s_y|^2.
\]
Set
\[
A_{\rm sel}=\sum_{y,\chi,\xi}|c_{\chi,\xi}|^2|s_y|^2.
\tag{14}
\]
This is the exact Cauchy mass. If slot amplitudes have bounds \(M_j\), then
\[
A_{\rm sel}
\le c_{\rm phase}\Bigl(\prod_{j\in J}M_j\Bigr)^2
             \prod_{j\in J}256P_j.
\tag{15}
\]
It has one selected-width factor.

Define the common width
\[
W_J=\prod_{j\in J}2P_j.
\]
Then \(N\Delta_y\le W_J\), and on live assignments
\[
W_J\le2^{|J|}N\Delta_y.
\]
Since \(N(d_y^4)=N(\Delta_y)^4\), the original ball \(N(k)<2K\) maps inside the ball
\[
\boxed{K_{\rm child}=16K W_J^4.}
\tag{16}
\]
The majorizing ball profile equals \(1\) on the transferred support. This is a fourth-power radius; replacing \(W_J\) by \(\prod P_j\) would omit a fixed but real factor.

For nonzero \(z\), the number of pairs \((y,k)\) with \(d_y^4k=z\) is at most
\[
\#\{y:d_y^4\mid z\}\le\tau((z))^{|J|}.
\tag{17}
\]
For a given \(y\), multiplication by \(d_y^4\ne0\) is injective. Each selected prime ideal divides \((z)\), proving the last bound.

If \(J\ne\varnothing\), the zero row is killed **before** replacing coefficients by their norm bounds: an injective nonempty product of primes is not a sixth power, whereas its Gauss row at zero can be nonzero only for a sixth-power ideal. If \(J=\varnothing\), there is exactly one assignment, its multiplier is \(1\), and the zero row remains.

Combining (12)–(17), for any finite squarefree set \(\mathcal V\) containing the residual seeds,
\[
\boxed{
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}E_u(K)
\le A_{\rm sel}\,2^{|J|}\,M_J
 \sum_{\chi,\xi}\sum_{v\in\mathcal V}
 E^{\rm rest}_{v,\tau\xi}(K_{\rm child}),
}
\tag{18}
\]
where \(M_J\) bounds (17) on the child ball, with the preceding zero-row convention. There is no remaining sum over selected assignments on the right.

Now, and only now, positivity permits completion of \(\mathcal V\) to include all squarefree divisors needed by (7). This is the corrected selected-row average in `ConcreteTotalMult` and `ConcreteAssemblyAvg`.

**5. All four Poisson contributions remain.**

Apply the retained second Poisson identity to each residual energy in (18). Define:

- \(Z_0\): the absolute value of its actual zero-frequency term;
- \(Z_f\): the absolute fixed-inducing retained contribution;
- \(Z_t\): the absolute discarded tail;
- \(Z_{\rm nf}\): the sum of absolute nonfixed physical blocks after (7).

Then
\[
\sum_{v\in\mathcal V}E^{\rm rest}_v
\le Z_0+Z_f+Z_t+Z_{\rm nf}.
\tag{19}
\]
In \(Z_{\rm nf}\), every block has the original coefficient with seed \(1\), multiplied by \(\rho(C_2)\). The seed has been removed by (7), not by estimating individual seed rows.

Thus the complete side reduction is
\[
\sum_u E_u^{\rm original}
\le
\#\mathcal B\sum_{\mathcal B}|b_{\mathcal B}|^2
 A_{{\rm sel},\mathcal B}2^{|J_{\mathcal B}|}M_{\mathcal B}
 \sum_{\chi,\xi}(Z_0+Z_f+Z_t+Z_{\rm nf})_{\mathcal B,\xi}.
\tag{20}
\]
Unit rows have norm \(1\) and remain in their actual fixed/nonfixed class. Empty common supports have \(\rho(1)=1\). Empty selected sets and zero-slot sources are covered by the stated conventions.

The separate diagonal supplier must pay \(Z_0+Z_f+Z_t\). Nothing in the packed nonfixed argument pays these terms automatically.

**6. Exact first-side packing and \(q_C\).**

Let the first common parts have multiplicities \(l_P,r_P\in\{1,2\}\). Put
\[
n_P=(l_P-r_P)\bmod6.
\]
At active primes \(n_P\ne0\), the only possibilities are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
(l_P,r_P)&n_P&(1+n_P)\bmod6&(1+5n_P)\bmod6\\ \hline
(2,1)&1&2&0\\
(1,2)&5&0&2 .
\end{array}
\tag{21}
\]
Let \(\pi_P\) be the retained primary generator, let
\(r=\epsilon\prod_{\rm active}\pi_P\) be the actual active conductor, and let \(e\) be the first common subset generator. Define
\[
V_C=e\epsilon\prod_{\rm active}\pi_P^{(1+n_P)\bmod6},
\qquad
V_D=e\epsilon\prod_{\rm active}\pi_P^{(1+5n_P)\bmod6}.
\tag{22}
\]
The unit \(\epsilon\) is retained in the character identity.

The table gives, at active primes,
\[
k_{C,P}+r_P=1+l_P,\qquad
k_{D,P}+l_P=1+r_P,
\]
and inactive primes have \(l_P=r_P\). Multiplication therefore proves
\[
NV_C\,N c_D=Ne\,Nr\,N c_C,\qquad
NV_D\,N c_C=Ne\,Nr\,N c_D.
\tag{23}
\]
For \(Z>1\), putting
\[
c=\log_ZNc_C,\quad d=\log_ZNc_D,\quad
q=\log_Z(Ne\,Nr)
\]
gives exactly
\[
\boxed{q_C=\log_ZNV_C=q+c-d,\qquad q_D=q+d-c.}
\tag{24}
\]

The \(e\)-part divides either common part. The remaining packed exponent is at most the corresponding common exponent. Hence
\[
\boxed{(V_C)\mid c_C^2,\qquad(V_D)\mid c_D^2.}
\tag{25}
\]
This proves polynomial support and divisor control for the actual packed multiplier.

For a primary column \(a\) coprime to \(P\), sextic reciprocity gives
\[
(a/P)_6^{n_P}
=\operatorname{phase}(\pi_P,a)^{n_P}\chi_{(a)}(\pi_P)^{n_P}.
\]
Multiplying the existing \(\pi_P\)-row symbol and reducing its exponent modulo six yields (22). On the right, conjugation replaces the exponent \(n_P\) by \(5n_P\); the reciprocity phase is real and remains unchanged.

If the reduced exponent is zero, the prime must remain in the puncture mask: \(0^6=0\), while the reduced zeroth power equals \(1\). Let \(Z_C,Z_D\) be precisely these exponent-zero prime products. On supported columns avoiding them,
\[
h_{\tau_C}(t,I)=h_{\sigma_C}(t,I)\chi_I(V_C),\qquad
h_{\tau_D}(t,I)=h_{\sigma_D}(t,I)\chi_I(V_D)
\tag{26}
\]
for every real \(t\). The anchors \(\sigma_C,\sigma_D\) belong to the fixed finite ray dictionary obtained by multiplying the original ray twist by the phase of \(\prod\pi_P^{n_P}\). They do not grow with the common ideals.

After the second ray expansion, the multiplier is \(V_CA_2\), respectively \(V_DA_2\), and the mask includes \(Z_CC_2\), respectively \(Z_DD_2\).

The independent-height absorption is also exact. If the inherited ordinary prefix is \(\mathbf d=(d_1,d_2)\), then multiplication by \(NI^{iv}\) changes the slot heights by \(v\), the two profile parameters by \(v/(2\pi)\), and leaves the scalar
\[
\left(\frac{X_1X_2}{Nd_1Nd_2\,NG}\right)^{iv},
\tag{27}
\]
of modulus \(1\). Neither prefix norm nor either independent height may be omitted.

**7. Canonical keep transfers to the packed row.**

Suppose, on supported columns avoiding a finite mask \(w\),
\[
\operatorname{coeff}_{\tau}(I)
=\operatorname{coeff}_{\sigma}(I)\chi_I(V),\qquad V\ne0.
\tag{28}
\]
Enlarge the fixed bad mask by \(w\), using the retained fixed-inducing mask-invariance lemma. On unmasked elements, multiplicativity gives
\[
\operatorname{coeff}_{\tau}(I)\chi_I(z)
=\operatorname{coeff}_{\sigma}(I)\chi_I(Vz).
\]
Both sides vanish on masked or unsupported elements. Their masked row characters therefore agree as functions. Consequently, for \(z\ne0\),
\[
\operatorname{FixedInducingRow}_{\tau,Q}(z)
\iff
\operatorname{FixedInducingRow}_{\sigma,Q}(Vz).
\tag{29}
\]
The internal reference \(Q\) is unchanged.

At \(z=0\), both nonfixed keep predicates are false. Thus for every \(z\),
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{canonicalKeep}_{\tau,Q}(z)
\iff\operatorname{initialKeep}_{\sigma,Q}(Vz).}
\tag{30}
\]
Natural characters agree on the same actual masked columns. This preserves their natural zeros.

For the actual second-family application, first use the shared packed-twin
bridge (T1)–(T15) in section Appendix C.6. The first exponent-zero
ideal \(Z_0\) divides the first common factor and the retained residual
puncture \(R\); it need not divide the second common \(G\). Original
nonzero residual coefficients avoid \(Z_0\). Hence the original masked
energy and keep equal those of the genuine twin, whose supported
coefficients are globally \(a_\sigma(I)\chi_I(V)\) and whose auxiliary
mask is \(1\). This is the frame character used below.

The injective substitution \(y=Vz\) transforms this ORIGINAL MASKED
polynomial at scale \(K\) into the exact sublattice energy
\[
\sum_{\substack{V\mid y\\\operatorname{initialKeep}_{\sigma,Q}(y)}}
 |\mathcal R^{\rm orig}_{\sigma,y}|^2\,
 \Phi\!\left(\frac{Ny}{NV\,K}\right).
\tag{31}
\]
Here \(\mathcal R^{\rm orig}_{\sigma,y}\) retains every original
common-factor, exponent-zero, tuple and puncture restriction. Only the
subsequent restoration produces unrestricted canonical leaves. There is
no Jacobian factor in this discrete sum.

**8. Restoration contract and extraction normalization.**

The separately required cube-free restoration statement is the following uniform contract. For a genuine common ideal \(G\), second artificial squarefree divisor \(L\), and inherited ordinary prefix \(\mathbf d\), the literal one-sided energy \(e_x(v)\) is dominated by a finite positive combination of canonical packed leaves, over every surviving slot subset and shortened ordinary pairs below either original pair, of total mass
\[
\mathcal M_x=
C_{\rm red}Z^\eta X
 \frac{(NG)^\delta(NL)^\delta}
      {NG\,NL\,Nd_1Nd_2}.
\tag{32}
\]
Here \(X=X_1X_2\prod_iP_i\). The seed divides \(G\); all prefixes are nonzero; the radical of the exterior ideal, \(G,L\), and punctures has norm at most \(Z^B\); the prime enclosure is fixed at \(\mathrm{Cap}\,Z^{L_{\rm cap}}\). Heights, holes, original coefficients, and all shortenings are uniform.

The frame character is the packed twin, with auxiliary mask \(1\),
whose raw energy equals the original second-character energy. Apply the
the restoration of Appendix C.7 only after packing the original masked polynomial.
Its exact hypotheses are: nonnegative canonical radial weight and positive
radial scale; keep excluding zero; nonzero prefixes and exterior ideal;
seed dividing \(G\); squarefree \(L\); the stated radical cap;
\(0\le w_i\le L_{\rm slot}\le L_{\rm cap}\) and
\(\mathrm{Cap}\ge\max(2,b)\); complete ordinary-prime enclosure; and
every ordinary-hole prime belonging to each original live slot-hole set.
No hidden mask is assigned to a restored leaf. A largest positive leaf may
be selected separately for each label, profiles and height \(v\); only
its mass constant is uniform. Empty or zero-energy families contribute zero.
Appendix C.7 supplies this exact
contract; a bound for unrelated unrestricted coefficients would not suffice.

Use the normalized energy
\[
E_x(v)=NG\,NL\,Nd_1Nd_2\,Z^{k-2a}e_x(v),
\qquad X=Z^a.
\tag{33}
\]
With \(NG\le Z^{2B}\), \(NL\le Z^B\), and
\(\delta=\varepsilon/(48\max(1,B))\),
\[
NG\,NL\,Nd_1Nd_2\,\mathcal M_x
\le C_{\rm red}Z^{\eta+\varepsilon/16}X.
\tag{34}
\]
The three extraction gains cancel before collection. Moving them into the label weight would destroy the harmonic fiber bound.

**9. Divisor fibers before completion.**

Fix the ray and dyadic class. Restrict to the actual finite frame image, with source, first-side,
ray and dyadic data frozen. On this image a frame label is determined by
\[
\bigl(G,(A_2),L\bigr).
\tag{35}
\]
Indeed \(A_2\) is exactly the multiplicative primary generator of
\[
\prod_P P^{\min(l_P,r_P)}
 \prod_{P\in\text{nonunit partition}}P.
\]
Thus its ideal determines the element, including its normalization.
The raised dyad is determined by \(A_2\); the anchor is fixed by the ray
class; the twin, mask \(1\), exterior ideal, seed, holes, prefixes and
prefactor are then prescribed frame data. This is image-restricted code
injectivity, not an assertion about arbitrary frame-label records.

Even before using unequal-multiplicity vanishing, cube-freeness gives
\[
G\mid(A_2)^2.
\tag{36}
\]
At a row \(y\ne0\) with \(A_2\mid y\), both code ideals in (35) divide \((y)^2\). Also \(\rho(G)\le\tau((y)^2)\). For fixed \(L\), there are at most \(\tau((y)^2)^2\) codes. Therefore, if \(|p_x|\le1\),
\[
\sum_{\substack{x\\A_{2,x}\mid y}}
 \frac{\rho(G_x)|p_x|}{NL_x}
\le
\tau((y)^2)^3
 \sum_{0<NL\le Z^B}\frac1{NL}.
\tag{37}
\]
The retained ideal counting bound gives
\[
\sum_{0<NL\le Z^B}\frac1{NL}
\le256\bigl(\lceil\log_2 Z^B\rceil+1\bigr).
\tag{38}
\]
This is the required completion of the second-divisor sum. It uses reciprocal weights, not divisibility of \(L\) into \(y\).

For \(Ny\le Z^{M_{\max}+2}\), the fixed-field divisor bound and (38) make (37) at most \(Z^{\varepsilon/8}\), eventually uniformly in \(y\). One can allocate \(\varepsilon/32\) to the divisor power, \(\varepsilon/32\) to the logarithm, and \(\varepsilon/16\) to their fixed constants.

There is a separate multiplicity when original physical labels map to the same frame label. For fixed chosen common factor \(G\), both original common ideals divide \(G^2\), and their unit/nonunit partition has at most \(\rho(G)\) choices. Hence
\[
M_{\rm physical}\le\tau(G^2)^2\rho(G)\le\tau(G^2)^3.
\tag{39}
\]
It is paid separately under the common-ideal norm cap. It is not an extra free label count.

**10. Common profiles and total grouped energy.**

For an ordinary profile \(W\), let \(f(v)=W(e^v)\). It is smooth and compactly supported, so
\[
W(e^v x)=\int_{\mathbb R}\widehat f(\tau)
 e^{2\pi i\tau v}x^{2\pi i\tau}\,d\tau.
\tag{40}
\]
Choose a fixed smooth two-piece partition on \([1/8,9/4]\), with scales
\(c_0=1/4,c_1=3/2\). The common profiles
\[
W_{e,\tau}(u)=\psi_e(c_eu)u^{2\pi i\tau}
\]
are supported in \([1/4,9/4]\), and every required seminorm grows polynomially in \(|\tau|\).

For two ordinary factors the exact scalar includes
\(\sqrt{c_{e_1}c_{e_2}}\), as well as the dilation phases. Its positive majorant is
\[
M_e(\tau_1,\tau_2)
=\sqrt{c_{e_1}c_{e_2}}\,
 |\widehat f_1(\tau_1)||\widehat f_2(\tau_2)|.
\tag{41}
\]
Repeated integration by parts bounds every polynomially weighted integral of (41) by finitely many seminorms of the original profiles.

Discard zero-energy children before grouping. A positive child with
ordinary support in \([a,b]\) has \(X_i'\ge1/b\), because a supported
nonzero ideal has norm at least one. Together with \(X_i'\le Z^L\),
this gives the finite dyadic range counted below.
Group shortened ordinary lengths into dyadic cells
\(X_i'\in[Y_i/2,Y_i]\). The dilation is \(v_i=\log(Y_i/X_i\prime)\in[0,\log2]\). Their central-normalization ratio is
\[
\sqrt{\frac{Y_1Y_2}{X_1'X_2'}}\le2.
\]
For a fixed anchor, surviving slot subset, and dyadic length cell, write the common-profile row as \(P_{e,\tau}(y)\). Cauchy in the Fourier integral, followed by the row fiber bound \(D\), yields
\[
\sum_xw_x E_x^{\rm leaf}
\le4D\,L_0L_J\,T,
\tag{42}
\]
whenever the common-profile energy is at most
\(T\operatorname{pairWeight}_J(\tau)\). Here
\(L_j=\sum_e\int M_e\operatorname{pairWeight}_j\).
To verify (42), first use
\[
\left|\int a(\tau)P(\tau)\,d\tau\right|^2
\le\left(\int|a|\right)\int|a||P|^2,
\]
then interchange nonnegative sums/integrals and apply (37) at each common row. This never sums a separate source bound over all labels.

Assume a canonical leaf at row-scale exponent \(H\) has the uniform price
\(Z^{H+p(w_0,P,s,H)+\varepsilon/8}\), where \(p\) is nonnegative, monotone in \(P,s\), and Lipschitz with constant \(K_p\). Put
\[
P=\max\{\ell(X_1)+\ell(X_2),\ell(Y_1)+\ell(Y_2)\},
\quad \ell(x)=\max(0,\log_Zx),\quad s=\sum_iw_i.
\]
For a group with packed envelope within \(\mathfrak m\) of \(H\), the exact dual cutoff gives
\[
H\le q_0+2a-k+2\mathfrak m.
\]
Consequently (32)–(42) give
\[
\boxed{
\sum_xw_xE_x(v)
\le C\,\mathcal A_J\,(1+|v|)^{2J}
 Z^{a+q_0+p(w_0,P,s,H)+\varepsilon},
}
\tag{43}
\]
where
\[
\mathcal A_J=
\bigl(\|W_1\|_{\mathcal S}\|W_2\|_{\mathcal S}\bigr)^2
(1+|t|+V_f+|t_1|+|t_2|)^J.
\]
The constants and finite seminorm set precede the variable profiles, heights, lengths, labels, and \(Z\).

A sufficient explicit fee allocation is:

| Cost | Exponent |
|---|---:|
| Restoration | \(\varepsilon/8\) |
| Extraction mass | \(\varepsilon/16\) |
| Weighted row fibers | \(\varepsilon/8\) |
| Finite anchors/subsets/dyadic length cells | \(\varepsilon/16\) |
| Canonical leaf bound | \(\varepsilon/8\) |
| Mesh | \(\varepsilon/8\) |
| Fixed scale enlargements and price variation | \(\varepsilon/16\) |

Their sum is \(11\varepsilon/16\). It suffices to choose
\[
\mathfrak m\le\tfrac12,\qquad
(3+K_p)\mathfrak m\le\varepsilon/8,
\qquad
(1+3K_p)\log_Z3\le\varepsilon/16.
\]
The mesh choice precedes the growing family. For fixed slot count, the class count is bounded by
\[
|\mathrm{Dict}|\,2^N
 \bigl(L\log_2Z+\log_2b+2\bigr)^2.
\]
This also shows why fixed structural size and eventuality cannot be interchanged silently.

**11. Return to the physical blocks and the six-width identity.**

In this paragraph, \(K\) denotes the SECOND Poisson/Gauss scale
\(K_{\rm child}=K_{\mathcal B}\), with \(Z^k=K\). It is not the
pre-selection scale denoted by \(K\) in (16).

The literal physical scalar is
\[
\operatorname{outerScalar}
=\frac{K}{\sqrt{NC_2}\sqrt{ND_2}
               \sqrt{\operatorname{dyad}_2}\sqrt{\operatorname{dyad}_3}}.
\]
Let \(p_d=Nd_1Nd_2\). The actual nonzero-column support gives
\(c_{\rm low}X\le p_dN(C_2I)\), and similarly on the right.
Consequently the coefficient \(c_0\) in the following display is
\(p_d/c_{\rm low}\), not a prefix-independent constant.
If actual column support gives
\(X\le c_0NC_2\operatorname{dyad}_2\) and
\(X\le c_0ND_2\operatorname{dyad}_3\), then
\[
\operatorname{outerScalar}\le c_0X\frac K{X^2}.
\tag{44}
\]
The common normalizer supplies the factor bounded by either \(NC_2\) or \(ND_2\). In the surviving equal-second-common sector this is \(NG\). Combining
\(\operatorname{outerScalar}\le p_dK/(c_{\rm low}X)\), that common
normalizer, and the factor \(NG\,NL\,p_dZ^k/X^2\) in (33) cancels
the complete prefix and common factors. The resulting scalar is precisely
\(X/c_{\rm low}\) after the retained frequency normalization, as displayed
in (45). Explicitly, with \(p_d=Nd_1Nd_2\),
\[
w_xE_x=\rho(G_x)|p_x|\,NG_x\,p_d\frac K{X^2}\,e_x;
\]
the second divisor \(NL_x\) cancels against its reciprocal label weight.
Hence
\[
\rho(G_x)|p_x|\,\operatorname{outerScalar}\,
 \operatorname{normalizer}\,e_x
\le\frac X{c_{\rm low}}w_xE_x.
\]
No prefix is replaced by one.

To sum absolute block values, multiply each block by its own unit complex phase and apply the whole-kernel estimate to the joint index \((\text{label},z)\). This gives one Cauchy inequality between the two summed side energies. Both orientations use (43); no number-of-labels factor appears.

For a dyadic box \([-M,M]^4\), the resulting bound has the explicit form
\[
Z_{\rm nf}\le
(2M+1)^4 C_{\rm ker}\frac{X}{c_{\rm low}}
 M_{\rm physical}B_0\,
 \operatorname{profileMoment}_J^2
 (1+2\pi)^{4J}(1+|t|)^{2J},
\tag{45}
\]
when \(B_0(1+|v|)^{2J}\) bounds both grouped frame energies. The dyadic box and (39) are separate subpower fees. Substitution into (20), together with the separately supplied diagonal bound, bounds the total first raw side.

Finally, in exact side coordinates
\[
a=A-c-u,\qquad
k=2A-c-d+q-1-t+4u,\qquad q_C=q+c-d,
\]
direct cancellation gives
\[
\boxed{2a-k+q_C=1+t-6u.}
\tag{46}
\]
The two losses of selected width in \(2a\), together with the four-power frequency enlargement, account for the coefficient \(6\).

Literal physical scales require care. With \(u=\sum_{j\in J}w_j\),
\[
\log_ZK_{\rm child}
=\log_ZK+4u+(4+4|J|)\log_Z2.
\]
Frozen marked primes can also produce a volume correction
\[
\Delta_a=\sum_{\rm frozen\ j}\log_Z(NP_j/P_j),
\qquad0\le\Delta_a\le N\log_Z2.
\]
Thus, for nominal coordinates with corrections \(\Delta_a,\Delta_k\), the exact identity is
\[
2a-k+q_C=1+t_0-6u+2\Delta_a-\Delta_k.
\]
Defining the actual defect \(t=t_0+2\Delta_a-\Delta_k\) recovers (46). The raised Poisson envelope is then
\[
H=1+(t+\mathfrak m)-6u.
\]
A permitted interval for this actual defect is a geometric input, not a consequence of cancellation. `ProviderGeometry3.branch_window` explicitly requires that defect window. The fixed padding must remain in its slop.

The restoration input (32) is proved in Appendix C.7; the uniform priced leaf for (43) is proved in §4 and Appendix C.10; the actual defect window, support bounds and payment of \(Z_0+Z_f+Z_t\) are proved in Appendix C.9. The complete assembly is Appendix C.10. No angular or arbitrary-coefficient extension is inferred. Attribution remains with Sil, ArviFoxy, Hailey Collet, OpenAI, and the inherited source authors.
