### C.9. Diagonal, reference and root geometry


The stricter principal range is compatible with the diagonal and root budgets. The decisive identity is that the reference correction cancels the actual ordinary minimum \(L\), leaving the root margin
\[
\log_Z V+3u_{\max}-\frac56-\alpha\ell\le-9\omega,
\qquad \alpha=\frac23-\frac{\omega}{2}.
\]
This remains valid after every genuine common allocation and ordinary-prefix shortening.

The cube-free principal estimate is proved in Appendix C.7. The reference inlet is the general common-product, two-orientation estimate proved in Appendix C.4, §§1–4, equations (A.23), (A.34)–(A.35). Here it is applied with its parameters R=1+ω and d=ω under the explicit gates (12) below. That general estimate is distinct from the more specialized midpoint-selected theorem at the end of C.4. No additional reference theorem is imported.

**1. Uniform statement and notation.**

Fix step data with child face
\[
P+\Lambda S\le B,\qquad s_0\le S\le c,
\]
and the literal scalar hypotheses of §4.1 and Appendix C.10(13), including \(B<1\), \(\Lambda>1\), \(c<1/6\), the monotone selection function \(\operatorname{sel}_\varepsilon\), the full perturbed packed-price ledger, and the four reference inequalities below.

Use the root coordinates
\[
P=\log_Z(X_1X_2),\qquad S=\sum_iw_i,\qquad
V=X_1X_2\prod_iP_i,
\]
so \(\log_ZV=P+S\). Fix \(\varepsilon>0\). The root mesh is chosen
before the ambient finite slot set. After fixing that set, the ray data, slot profile, base characters and fixed inducing modulus, there are a height degree \(J_0\), finite ordinary-profile control \(\mathcal S_0\), and constant \(C_0\). For every larger degree and control and every \(C_{\rm side}\ge C_0\), one eventual threshold works for:

- every root shape and its surviving slot subset;
- every admitted root source, including its independent ordinary heights;
- every retained first block and both orientations;
- every genuine allocation and selected subset;
- every \(0\le M_c\le Z^{\varepsilon/4}\) satisfying the selected-row multiplicity bound.

Write
\[
\mathcal A=C_{\rm side}
 \bigl(\|W_1\|_{\mathcal S}\|W_2\|_{\mathcal S}\bigr)^2
 \operatorname{height}(t_0,V_f,t_1,t_2)^J.
\]
The diagonal contribution on a side with first common factors \(C,D\) is at most
\[
\frac12\,\mathcal A\,
 \frac{N\mathfrak f_\tau\,V^2}{NC\,ND}\,
 Z^{b(C,D;Z)+3\varepsilon}(1+|v|)^{2J}.
\tag{1}
\]
Here \(V\) is the original root volume, \(\mathfrak f_\tau\) is the actual presented modulus of the side character, and \(b(C,D;Z)\) is the retained nonnegative allowance. It is retained literally. The proof below uses only its nonnegativity.

The root source has unit original ordinary prefixes, exterior ideal \(1\), common puncture product \(1\), and the literal restored coefficients. Its allocated descendants generally have nonunit prefixes. Those are retained.

**2. Choose the reference before the common labels.**

Let \(\rho_{\rm ref}>0\) be the `ReferenceAt` reserve. Its four inequalities are, for every admitted \(S\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\rho_{\rm ref}&\le1-B+(\Lambda-2)S-\frac92\operatorname{sel}_\varepsilon S,\\
\rho_{\rm ref}&\le\frac1{20}+\frac32(1-B)
 +\left(\frac32\Lambda-\frac52\right)S
 -\frac92\operatorname{sel}_\varepsilon S,\\
\rho_{\rm ref}&\le1-B+(\Lambda-1)S-4\operatorname{sel}_\varepsilon S,\\
\rho_{\rm ref}&\le\frac13-2S-3\operatorname{sel}_\varepsilon S.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
Put
\[
\rho=\frac12\min\{\rho_{\rm ref},1-B,1/100\},
\quad
\mathfrak m=\min\{\rho/1024,\varepsilon/1024,\mathfrak m_{\rm ledger}\},
\]
\[
\omega=\min\{\rho/100000,\varepsilon/100000\},
\qquad
u_{\max}=\operatorname{sel}_\varepsilon S+\mathfrak m.
\tag{3}
\]
Choose the common frame mesh before the number of slots, with
\(0<\mathfrak m_F\le\mathfrak m\), also satisfying the separately proved
collection and leaf tolerances. Thus both meshes are independent of the
eventual number of slots. Monotonicity of selection ensures that every allocation’s selected width is at most \(u_{\max}\).

Define
\[
L_-=\frac32\left(P+S+3u_{\max}-\frac56\right),\quad
U_1=\frac{P-S-1/2}{2},\quad U_2=\frac3{10}-S.
\tag{4}
\]
Substitution of \(P\le B-\Lambda S\) into (2), followed by
\(\mathfrak m\le\rho/1024\), gives
\[
U_1-L_-\ge\rho,\qquad U_2-L_-\ge\rho,\qquad
\frac13-2S-3u_{\max}\ge\rho.
\tag{5}
\]
Also
\[
P+S\le1-\rho,\quad
5u_{\max}\le1,\quad P+S+4u_{\max}\le1.
\tag{6}
\]
The last inequality follows from the third line of (2); the middle one follows from \(u_{\max}\le S+\mathfrak m\), \(S<1/6\), and the mesh bound.

The high branch is
\[
P+S+3u_{\max}>\frac56-10\omega.
\]
On this branch choose \(\ell\) as the midpoint of
\[
\left(\max(0,L_-)+20\omega,\ 
      \min(U_1,U_2)-20\omega\right).
\tag{7}
\]
This interval is nonempty. If \(L_-\ge0\), (5) proves it. If \(L_-<0\), put
\(T=P+S+3u_{\max}-5/6>-10\omega\). Then
\[
U_1=\frac T2+\frac12\left(\frac13-2S-3u_{\max}\right)
>\frac{\rho}{2}-5\omega,
\]
which also leaves the required buffers. Moreover \(U_1<U_2\), and
\[
0<\ell<P/2,\qquad
\ell>L_-+20\omega,\qquad
\ell<U_i-20\omega,\qquad \ell<1.
\tag{8}
\]

Choose
\[
\alpha=\frac23-\frac{\omega}{2}.
\tag{9}
\]
Then \(0<\alpha<2/3\), and (8) gives
\[
P+S+3u_{\max}-\frac56-\alpha\ell\le-9\omega.
\tag{10}
\]
Indeed the loss from replacing \(2/3\) by \(\alpha\) is at most \(\omega\ell\le\omega\), whereas the lower-end buffer contributes more than \(40\omega/3\).

On the low branch take \(\ell=0\); its defining inequality gives the stronger margin \(-10\omega\). Thus (10) holds on both branches.

The actual comparison rectangle uses
\[
L_* = Z^\ell.
\]
The source minimum supplied to the diagonal estimates is bounded below by
\[
L_{\rm ref}=\frac29 Z^\ell.
\tag{11}
\]
These are different quantities, and the factor \(2/9\) must remain.

**3. The same reference also meets the retained reference theorem.**

In this section only, assume the HIGH/NeedsCentering branch. The low
branch uses the uncentered root and the direct low exceptional margin in
(10); it invokes neither (14) nor the reference triangle below. In
particular, \(\ell=0\) alone does not imply the third reference gate.

Set \(R=1+\omega\), \(d=\omega\), and use reference tolerances \(\delta_{\rm ref}=\xi_{\rm ref}=\omega\). Equations (5) and (8) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
P+2S+4\omega&<1+\omega,\\
\ell+\frac{1+2\omega}{2}+S+2\omega
 &\le\frac45(1+\omega),\\
1+2\omega+2\ell-P+S+2\omega
 &\le\frac12(1+\omega).
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
For example, the second follows from
\(\ell<3/10-S-20\omega\); the third follows from
\(2\ell<P-S-1/2-40\omega\).

These are precisely the scalar gates of the retained homogeneous two-orientation reference estimate. Its application also requires one event, chosen before the moving rectangles, which pays
\[
\left(\frac94+4\right)\frac94\,2^N\le Z^\omega,
\quad b_\Phi Z\le Z^{1+\omega},
\]
and
\[
\max\{1,C_{\rm cond}(\eta)\,b_\Phi Z\}\le Z^{1+2\omega}.
\tag{13}
\]
All factors on the left are fixed before \(Z\). Hence (13) holds eventually.

For every rectangle of the original product, in the original enclosure, with either side at most \(L_*\), the resulting kept reference energy is
\[
\le \operatorname{radialControl}(\Phi)\,
 C\bigl(\|W_1\|_{\mathcal S}\|W_2\|_{\mathcal S}\bigr)^2
 \operatorname{height}(0,0,t,t)^J
 Z^{1+\omega+\varepsilon/100}.
\tag{14}
\]
The actual predicate is `initialKeep` with the original internal reference. Its exclusion of fixed-inducing rows is used, rather than an unrestricted reference average.

If either original side is already at most \(L_*\), (14) applies directly. Otherwise use the reference rectangle
\[
(L_*,\,X_1X_2/L_*).
\]
Equation \(\ell<P/2\), together with both original sides being at least \(L_*\), keeps it inside the inherited enclosure. The exact centered-source identity and
\(|x+y|^2\le2|x|^2+2|y|^2\) give the original energy as at most twice the sum of the centered raw energy and (14).

The changed principal exponent also fits the inherited first-reference reserve. Put \(\kappa_\alpha=2/3-\alpha=\omega/2\). For every reference width \(R'\le2\) and reserve \(\rho'\ge\rho/2\),
\[
\kappa_\alpha R'\le\omega\le\frac23\rho'.
\tag{15}
\]
For the retained midpoint reference, its reserve is
\((R'-P-2S-4d)/3\ge\rho'/3\), while its exponent is less than \(R'/2\). Thus (15) pays \(\kappa_\alpha\ell\). This verifies the cube-free `AlphaReferenceMargin`; using the old \(\alpha\ge2/3\) argument would be invalid.

The analytic content of (14) is the retained two-orientation reference theorem. The new work here is its exact admission, including (12)–(15).

**4. Allocation-dependent second scales.**

Fix an actual first common pair \(C,D\), a common subset \(E\), and a retained first frequency dyad \(2^n\ge1/2\). Let
\[
K=2^n Z^\kappa,\qquad \kappa=\operatorname{cutoffLoss}(N,\varepsilon)>0.
\tag{16}
\]
For each genuine allocation \(\mathcal B\), let \(r_{\mathcal B}\) be the actual residual source after selected-slot removal, before ordinary-prefix renormalization. Put
\[
W_{\mathcal B}=\prod_{j\in J_{\mathcal B}}2P_j,\qquad
K_{\mathcal B}=16K W_{\mathcal B}^4,
\]
\[
Y_{\mathcal B}=\max\{1,\operatorname{normCap}(r_{\mathcal B})\},
\qquad
T_{\mathcal B}=\frac{Y_{\mathcal B}^2}{K_{\mathcal B}},
\qquad
R_{\mathcal B}=T_{\mathcal B}Z^{\mathfrak m_F/2}.
\tag{17}
\]
This is the literal `Tfreq`. The tail condition
\(Y_{\mathcal B}^2/K_{\mathcal B}\le T_{\mathcal B}\) holds with equality.

These choices are uniform over all allocations, but their values depend on the allocation. Replacing them by an unrelated common second scale would require a new argument.

The root has
\[
Z\le K_{\rm root}\le Z^2,\qquad
N\mathfrak f_\eta\le Z,\qquad
NC,ND\le Z^8,\qquad V\le Z.
\tag{18}
\]
First common factors divide original columns, proving their norm bounds. Their common exponents are at most two, so either orientation satisfies the weaker condition \(ND\le(NC)^3\) required below.

The retained first-frequency cutoff gives
\[
K\le4\,T_{\rm first}Z^{3\kappa/2},
\quad
T_{\rm first}=\frac{Ne\,Nr\,V^2}{K_{\rm root}NC\,ND}.
\tag{19}
\]
The exact character presentation is
\[
\mathfrak f_\tau
=\mathfrak f_\eta\,(m_{\rm bad})\,(72)\,(er).
\tag{20}
\]
Therefore
\[
K\le
4Z^{3\kappa/2}\frac{N\mathfrak f_\tau\,V^2}{NC\,ND\,Z}.
\tag{21}
\]

All descendant pool caps are at most \(Z^8\). The residual norm caps satisfy
\[
\operatorname{normCap}(r_{\mathcal B})
\le \left(\frac94\right)^2 2^N V.
\tag{22}
\]
Eventually \(Y_{\mathcal B}\le Z^8\), \(1\le W_{\mathcal B}\le Z^2\), and
\(1/2\le K\le Z^{33}\). Thus
\[
T_{\mathcal B}\le Z^{16},\qquad R_{\mathcal B}\le Z^{17}.
\tag{23}
\]
The diagonal theorem is invoked with norm cap exponent \(8\), radial exponent \(17\), and a generous polynomial scale cap \(40\).

The family-conductor budget is bounded by a fixed constant times
\[
N\mathfrak f_\tau\cdot N(r_{\mathcal B}.R)\,
 \operatorname{poolCap}(r_{\mathcal B})^2
 Z^{16}R_{\mathcal B}.
\]
Here \(r_{\mathcal B}.R=C\), and the child ray character adds only the fixed \((12)\)-factor. Substitution of (18), (22), and (23), followed by payment of the fixed conductor factor, bounds this by \(Z^{80}\). The common puncture product is still \(1\), and the surviving marked product is at most the original marked product. This checks every cap used by the uniform principal estimate.

**5. The three per-seed bounds.**

Let \(v\) now denote a residual squarefree seed, and let \(h\in\mathbb R\) be the independent row height.

For zero frequency, the inherited column divisor bound gives
\[
|\beta_v(I)|\le C_{\rm col}\operatorname{prof}(r)\,Y^{\eta/2},
\]
on nonzero coefficients, with \(NI\le Y\) and \(v\mid I\). The retained zero-correlation divisor estimate then gives
\[
|Z_0(r,v)|
\le C_0\operatorname{prof}(r)^2\frac{Y^{1+\eta}}{Nv},
\qquad C_0=128C_{\rm col}^2.
\tag{24}
\]
The physical zero-frequency contribution is
\(K_{\mathcal B}|\widehat\Phi(0)|\) times (24). Heights have modulus at most one in this estimate.

The cube-free principal input, for \(0\le\alpha<2/3\), retains every prefix and supplies the common-saving factor
\[
(\mathcal C\mathcal D)^{-1/3}
 \min\left\{
  \max(1,x/\mathcal C)^{-\alpha},
  \max(1,x/\mathcal D)^{-\alpha}
 \right\}.
\]
For \(\mathcal C,\mathcal D\ge1\), this is at most \(x^{-\alpha}\). To prove it, set \(m=\min(\mathcal C,\mathcal D)\). Then
\[
(\mathcal C\mathcal D)^{-1/3}
\le m^{-2/3}\le m^{-\alpha},
\]
and \(m\max(1,x/m)\ge x\).

Take \(x=L/H\), where \(H=\max(Nd_1,Nd_2)\) is the actual inherited prefix maximum. For \(0<L_{\rm ref}\le L\),
\[
(L/H)^{-\alpha}
\le (L/H)^{-2/3}\,
 \underbrace{(L/L_{\rm ref})^{2/3}
  \max(1,L_{\rm ref})^{2/3-\alpha}}_{\mathcal R_\alpha}.
\tag{25}
\]
This remains valid when the shortened length is below \(1\).

The important point is that the diagonal estimates use the unrenormalized `restOf` source. Its prefix is shortened, but its \(L\)-field is the original root \(L\). Hence \(\mathcal R_\alpha\) is the same for all genuine allocations.

After the retained fixed-row count, whole-kernel integration and second common sum, the per-seed fixed-inducing contribution is bounded by

The priced nonfixed result of §4 supplies the other half of the same balanced budget. ### C.10. Complete generic source assembly


The generic native step closes with the repaired cube-free blocks. Its leaf price is exactly
\[
\frac34\,\mathrm{deletionNeed},
\]
and its LOW root uses the fixed lower scale \(2/9\). It does not obtain a principal saving from an arbitrarily large original minimum. The half-price source of §4 enters the same closure through its full priced leaf and the scalar ledger proved in §5.

The statement below uses the retained Gauss/reciprocity lemmas, the repaired packing–restoration block, and the repaired diagonal supplier as explicit dependencies. It supplies the complete source assembly used in §§4–5.

**1. Exact generic statement and uniformity.**

Write \(G(B,L,c)\) for the existing ordinary `GlobalSource`: the literal normalized two-ordinary-factor, finitely marked natural-row energy is \(O(Z^{1+\epsilon})\) whenever
\[
\ell_Z(X_1)+\ell_Z(X_2)+L\sum_iw_i\le B,\qquad
\sum_iw_i\le c,
\quad
\ell_Z(X)=\log_Z\max(1,X).
\tag{1}
\]
The marked coefficients remain
\[
\operatorname{idealCoeff}(\chi_{\eta_0,\theta_i},I)\,
\operatorname{annularWeight}(W,Z^{w_i},33/50,v_i,I),
\tag{2}
\]
with the original height coefficient, ray family, and natural zero convention. This is not an arbitrary-coefficient theorem.

For every \(\epsilon>0\), the mesh is chosen before the arbitrary ambient finite slot type. After that type, ray modulus/subgroup, smooth marked profile \(W\), radial support cap, fixed anchor characters, \(\eta_0\), and fixed \(Q\) have been fixed, choose the height degree, finite Schwartz-seminorm set, constant, and threshold. They then work simultaneously for:

- every slot subset, collision partition and inverse-restoration subset;
- all allowed ray labels, widths, independent frequencies and heights;
- all original ordinary profiles and all positive shortened ordinary lengths;
- every finite set of retained rows and every allowed nonnegative radial profile.

The exact shared source contract requires
\[
Q_{\rm int}=Q\cap\operatorname{modulus}(\eta_0),\quad
Q\subseteq\mathfrak m_{\rm ray},\quad Q_{\rm int}\ne0,\quad
Q_{\rm int}\ne\mathcal O,\quad Q_{\rm int}\subseteq(72).
\]
Require \(\mathfrak m_{\rm ray}\ne0\), the ray subgroup to contain
global units, and the marked profile to be smooth supported in \([1,2]\).
Fix \(b_\Phi\ge2\) before the constants. After constants and onset,
allow every Schwartz \(\Phi\) supported in \(( -\infty,b_\Phi]\)
with \(\Re\Phi\ge0\), controlled only by the displayed
\(\operatorname{diagControl}(\Phi)\) factor. The live widths are
nonnegative and at most the chosen mesh; the real slot power is \(33/50\),
and the nonnegative height bound dominates every individual slot frequency.
The admitted clipped ordinary lengths satisfy the stated fixed cap.

The main step is
\[
G(B_0,L_0,c_0)+\mathrm{StepGates}(D)
+\mathrm{PricedPackedSource}(D.\mathrm{price})
\Longrightarrow G(B,L,c),
\tag{3}
\]
under \(51/100\le\beta\), with envelope interval
\([H_{\min},H_{\max}+1]\) and ordinary length cap \(4\).

The analytic dependencies in (3) are precisely the repaired:

1. joint first-divisor and physical second-column identities;
2. original-masked packing, followed by cube-free restoration and grouped energy;
3. diagonal supplier, including fixed inducing rows, zero frequency and tails.

Their hypotheses are checked below rather than replaced by an abstract `StepInputs` assumption.

**2. The native leaf, including its parent-domain fallback.**

Let
\[
d(P,s,H)=
\max\!\left(0,\min\!\left(s,
\max\!\left(s-c_0H,\frac{P+L_0s-B_0H}{L_0}\right)\right)\right).
\tag{4}
\]
Here \(P=\ell_Z(X_1)+\ell_Z(X_2)\), \(s=\sum_iw_i\), and
\[
H=\log_Z(N(V)K).
\]
The exact packed row is evaluated at \(Vz\), retained with
\(\mathrm{initialKeep}_\eta(Q_{\rm int},Vz)\), and radially weighted at scale \(K\).

The injection \(z\mapsto Vz\) and nonnegativity give
\[
E_{\rm packed}(V,K)\le E_{\rm canonical}(N(V)K).
\tag{5}
\]
There is no lattice-density compensation in this inequality. The scale changes to \(N(V)K=Z^H\).

The original OpenAI bound \(\beta\le7/8\) supplies
\[
2\beta-1\le\kappa,\qquad \kappa=\frac34.
\tag{6}
\]
This is proved from the original moments and literal probe in Appendix B.9; neither the endpoint nor the new child face is used.

For a deleted subset \(D_{\rm del}\), factorization of the normalized slot product is literal:
\[
R_A(z)=
\left(\prod_{i\in D_{\rm del}}\mathrm{normalizedSlot}_i(z)\right)
R_{A\setminus D_{\rm del}}(z).
\tag{7}
\]
The retained natural-slot estimate, applied with zero widths outside \(D_{\rm del}\), gives
\[
\left|\prod_{i\in D_{\rm del}}\mathrm{normalizedSlot}_i(z)\right|^2
\le C(1+|t|+V_{\rm ht})^J
 Z^{\epsilon_1+\kappa\sum_{D_{\rm del}}w_i}
\tag{8}
\]
on every retained row. It applies because the keep excludes the fixed inducing family, the natural conductor has the required polynomial cap, and the coefficient in (2) is unchanged. Multiplying (8) by the nonnegative radial weight and summing proves partial deletion without changing the remaining keep, ordinary profiles or lengths.

Suppose first \(P\le B_0H\), with \(B_0,c_0>0\). Greedily delete whole slots until their total width \(d'\) first reaches (4). Each slot has width at most \(m\), so
\[
d\le d'\le d+m,\qquad s_{\rm ret}=s-d'\ge0.
\]
The definition of \(d\) then gives
\[
s_{\rm ret}\le c_0H,\qquad P+L_0s_{\rm ret}\le B_0H.
\tag{9}
\]
Apply the parent source at base \(Z^H\), with widths divided by \(H\). Since \(H\ge H_{\min}>0\), choosing the original mesh at most \(H_{\min}\) times the parent mesh makes this application uniform over the entire envelope.

For leaf loss \(\epsilon\), put \(M_{\max}=H_{\max}+1\).
Request the parent theorem with loss
\(\epsilon/[4\max(1,M_{\max})]\), before choosing its unit mesh and
the finite arithmetic/live data. On base \(Z^H\) this costs at most
\(H\epsilon/[4\max(1,M_{\max})]\le\epsilon/4\) in the original
base. The deletion loss is \(\epsilon/8\), and \(m\le\epsilon/8\).
Thus
\[
E_{\rm packed}\ll
\mathcal A\,Z^{H+\kappa d+
  \epsilon/4+\epsilon/8+\kappa\epsilon/8}
\le
\mathcal A\,Z^{H+\kappa d+\epsilon}.
\tag{10}
\]
Here \(\mathcal A\) is the prescribed radial diagonal control, the square of the two-profile control, and a polynomial height factor.

If \(P>B_0H\), then \(d=s\). The parent face cannot be applied even after deleting every slot; instead the retained native canonical-energy theorem gives
\[
E_{\rm packed}\ll\mathcal A Z^{H+\kappa s+\epsilon}.
\tag{11}
\]
This fallback is essential.

For the formally allowed degenerate case \(B_0\le0\) or \(c_0\le0\), (4) equals \(s\) on the evaluated nonnegative domain. Again (11) supplies the price. Consequently the generic native leaf is valid for every `NativeGates` instance, not only the positive faces in the actual chain.

This proves the native priced leaf, with the stated parent fallback and choice order.

**3. Scalar gates and actual perturbed geometry.** The direct native initiation in
§4.2 and the complete open-family induction in §5 prove the actual price,
height, parent-cap and reference inequalities. They replace the numerical
native-chain table. The assembly below applies to each of those steps
with its own fixed positive reserves; no numerical intermediate endpoint
is a premise. Here is the entire geometric domain to which those prices
are applied. If \(S\) is the root marked width, \(w\) its live width,
\(f=S-w\) its frozen width, \(u\) the selected width and \(s\) the
retained width, the actual clipped frame defines \(c_g\ge f\) and
\[
\begin{gathered}
 P_C+(c_g-f)+LS\le B+\tau,\quad P_C\ge0,\\

 \quad0\le s\le w-u,\\
 -\tau\le t\le1+6u+\tau,\qquad H=1+t-6u.

In particular \(P_C\le B-Lw+\tau\), because \(c_g-f\ge0\),
\(S\ge w\) and \(L>0\). Thus the full perturbed ledger (UF18)–(UF19)
applies with its \(W=w\); §4.2 proves the native alternative on the
same domain. The height envelope and the four positive reference reserves
are part of those local proofs. Below the positive width floor the native
all-slot estimate pays the error, as shown in section 5 below. The symbol

price and reference inequalities together with the fixed contract in
section 1; it introduces no separate theorem or unproved code assumption.

**4. Root reference, LOW principal input, and profiles.**

For a literal restored root, use its actual shortened ordinary lengths \(Y_1,Y_2\), and set
\[
P=\log_Z(Y_1Y_2),\qquad
S=\sum_{\text{surviving singleton slots}}w_i,\qquad A=P+S.
\tag{20}
\]
Thus \(P\) is an actual logarithm; it need not equal the clipped ordinary width. Nevertheless shortening and subset inclusion give
\[
P+LS\le B,\qquad s_0\le S\le c.
\tag{21}
\]

Choose a positive reference reserve \(r_{\rm ref}\) for the four expressions
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_1(S)&=1-B+(L-2)S-\tfrac92\operatorname{sel}(S),\\
R_2(S)&=\tfrac1{20}+\tfrac32(1-B)
 +(\tfrac32L-\tfrac52)S-\tfrac92\operatorname{sel}(S),\\
R_3(S)&=1-B+(L-1)S-4\operatorname{sel}(S),\\
R_4(S)&=\tfrac13-2S-3\operatorname{sel}(S).
\end{aligned}
\tag{22}
\]
For native steps one may take
\[
r_{\rm ref}=\min\{1-B,\tfrac13-(2+3a)c\}>0.
\]
The four gate inequalities above prove (22) uniformly.

Put
\[
r_*=\tfrac12\min(r_{\rm ref},1-B,1/100),\quad
m_*\le\min(r_*/1024,\epsilon/1024,m_{\rm ledger}),
\]
\[
\omega=\min(r_*/10^5,\epsilon/10^5),\quad
\alpha=\tfrac23-\omega/2,\quad
u_{\max}=\operatorname{sel}(S)+m_*.
\tag{23}
\]
Selection monotonicity bounds every later allocation’s selected width by \(u_{\max}\).

The HIGH branch is
\[
A+3u_{\max}>5/6-10\omega.
\]
Only there choose
\[
\ell_-=\tfrac32(A+3u_{\max}-5/6),\quad
\ell_1=(P-S-\tfrac12)/2,\quad \ell_2=\tfrac3{10}-S,
\]
\[
\ell=\tfrac12\left(\max(0,\ell_-)+20\omega+
                  \min(\ell_1,\ell_2)-20\omega\right).
\tag{24}
\]
From (21)–(23),
\[
0<\ell<P/2,\quad

Work in \(\mathcal O=\mathbf Z[\omega]\), with \(\omega=e^{2\pi i/3}\), ideal norm \(NI\), and element norm \(|u|^2\) in the fixed embedding.  s:=S(r)-u=H S_R+u/k. \tag{A9}
\]
After selecting width \(u\), erasing the excess over the rescaled old anchor costs exactly \(k(s-HS_R)=u\). This pays LOW rows. HIGH rows cost at most the same \(u\), using earlier anchors. These costs occur on disjoint positive row sets and combine by their maximum. The stage proves \(\mathrm{Anchor}(r,Y(r)-D)\), with \(D=1/25000000\).

### 5. HIGH rows and the floored detector price

Let \(\nu\in[k,3/4]\) be a buffered zero-bin exponent and \(e\in[0,\nu]\) its lower slot-mean amplitude. Pay the actual ordinary pair, or inverse factor, pointwise at exponent \(\nu P\), retaining the slot product inside the row sum; its amplitude price is \(eS\). Replacing this by the cruder \(\nu S\) loses the gain.

For a line \(l(w)=a_0-a_1w\) below earlier proved gains, put
\[
 \sigma(w)=\max(0,(1-w)/2+l(w)-10^{-7}),\quad
 w\in[2/3,79/100]. \tag{A10}
\]
The same-zero detector and largest-amplitude whole-slot selection give a short count exponent
\[
 C_{\rm short}=M-\nu Mw-e\min(S,M\sigma(w)). \tag{A11}
\]
To see this, select whole slots of total width at most the cap. Their common lower product is \(U^{ez-O(\mathrm{mesh})}\), the inverse or paired-ordinary witness gives \(U^{\nu w-O(\epsilon)}\), and their marked moment is \(O(U^{1+\epsilon})\). Divide the summed energy by the two lower bounds. Derivatives through order two and real shifts in \([0,1]\) stay inside the detector energy inequality. Both witnesses arise from the same actual zero.

The long-inverse count, at \(t=3w/2+10^{-6}\), has exponent
\[
 C_{\rm long}=M/6+(5/6-\nu)M(3w/2+10^{-6}). \tag{A12}
\]
The supported-witness theorem permits an unbounded height index \(i\) under the actual budget
\[
 (3+(3i+2)Z^\tau)^4\le(Z^d)^\eta;
\]
this does not permit an unbounded number of prime slots.

For tiny sixth-free cores of norm at most \(Z^{2/25}\), the count and pointwise price give excess
\[
 E_{\rm tiny}=M/6+1/15+(3/4)P+S-M. \tag{A13}
\]
For the other cores use
\[
 E(\nu,e,w)=\nu P+eS+\max(C_{\rm short},C_{\rm long})-M. \tag{A14}
\]
Every row is restored as \(u_0b^6\), including its extra Euler mask and every cofactor; \(u_0,b\) need not be coprime. The sixth-power cofactor sum restores radius \(M\) with arbitrarily small divisor loss. It explains the \(M/6\) and \(1/15\) terms and cannot be omitted.

The HIGH price is the maximum of zero, (A13), and \(\sup_{\nu,e}\inf_w E\). At stage \(n\) the infimum is constrained by
\[
 w\ge R_n+10^{-6}. \tag{A15}
\]
The floor raises the price. Below the top \(311/400\), every short witness must use an earlier stage \(j<n\); above it the line is nonpositive and native sources suffice. An unfloored optimization does not prove this induction.

Here is the scalar price proof at \((P,S,M)=(r,s,H)\) of (A9). Write \(D_1=1/2-a_1\ge1/10\) and
\[
 G_\nu=\frac{r+s-H/2-Ha_0-u/\nu}{D_1},\qquad
 w_\nu=G_\nu/H+10^{-6}. \tag{A16}
\]
Since \(l(R)\le z\),
\[
 D_1(G_\nu-r)=H(z-a_0+a_1R)+u(1/k-1/\nu)\ge0. \tag{A17}
\]
Thus \(w_\nu\ge R+10^{-6}\). It increases with \(\nu\); its endpoint gates put it in \([2/3,79/100]\). Before paddings the short excess over \(H+u\) is
\[
 \nu(r-G_\nu)+e\{s-(H-G_\nu)/2-Ha_0+a_1G_\nu\}-u\le0. \tag{A18}
\]
The braces equal \(G_\nu-r+u/\nu\ge0\); replacing \(e\le\nu\) by \(\nu\) makes the expression zero. The width and capacity paddings are paid because \(a_1\le2/5\) and
\[
 (1/2+a_1)10^{-6}+10^{-7}\le10^{-6}.
\]
The positive part in (A10) only helps. Hence the short excess is at most \(u\).

For the long branch put
\[
 \mathcal G(\nu)=H+u-H/6-(5/6-\nu)(3G_\nu/2)-\nu(r+s).
\]
At \(\nu=k\), \(G_k=Hw_b\), \(\mathcal G(k)=HF_0\), where
\[
 w_b=(R/2+z-a_0)/D_1,\quad
 F_0=5/6-(5/4-3k/2)w_b-k(1+R)/2-kz. \tag{A19}
\]
Its exact difference is
\[
 \mathcal G(\nu)-\mathcal G(k)=(\nu-k)
 \{\tfrac32G_\nu-\tfrac32(5/6-k)u/(k\nu D_1)-(r+s)\}.
\]
It is nonnegative if \(r/2-s-\tfrac32(5/6-k)u/(k^2D_1)\ge0\). The certificate supplies this with reserve \(1/10\) and \(HF_0>3\cdot10^{-5}\). Long-cutoff paddings cost at most \(1/400000\), leaving excess at most \(u-11/400000\). The tiny-core gate gives excess at most \(u-3/100\). Thus the **floored** HIGH price is at most \(u\). Monotonicity in free/marked widths and the cofactor radius comparison extend the ledger to the required shortened children.

### 6. Actual inverse selection, Poisson and restoration

The inverse step re-runs the actual initialization with injective prime marks. Overlapping canonical pools cannot first be coloured into arbitrary prime subsets and then be treated as canonical sources. Instead expand injective tuples; collision restoration afterwards recovers the full product, with a fixed finite combinatorial cost and small divisor loss. The initialized dictionary keeps the actual Möbius coefficients and natural zeros.

For a live-mark state with column width \(N\) and label width \(V\), put \(F=N+V\), \(K=2F-1\). The native canonical energy supplies the Gauss-row ball of exponent \(K\), enlarged by a small slack. If live width is at least \(u\), greedily select whole slots of width \(u'\in[u-O(\mathrm{mesh}),u]\), one distinct prime per selected slot. For their prime product \(D\), use the exact Gauss identity
\[
 \gamma_2(U'D)=\gamma_2(U')\gamma_2(D)\chi_{U'}(D)^4. \tag{A20}
\]
The injective tuple split moves \(D\) into the row \(kD^4\). The residual squarefree column avoids those selected primes; its other primes remain free even if they occur in the selected slots' pools. The zero \(\chi_{U'}(D)=0\) at a common prime stays. The selected coefficient is
\[
 \gamma_2(D)\Psi(D)\mathbf1_{(D,m)=1}
                  \chi_D(f)^4\chi_D(k)\,\mathrm{mark}_{\rm selected}(D).
\]
Cauchy and compact logarithmic separation leave one common residual row at column width \(N'=N-u'\), Gauss radius \(K'=K+4u'\). A second masked Poisson summation on that physical row yields a child radius
\[
 H_c=2(N'+V)-K'+\text{slack}=1-6u'+\text{slack}. \tag{A21}
\]

For labels \(Nf\le Z^V\) and nonnegative weights \(D_f\le D_{\max}\), a bound \(B\) for all physical inverse children gives
\[
\begin{split}
 E_{\rm selected}\le{}&CZ^{K'-N'-V+\epsilon}D_{\max}
                        (1+|s_0|)^{2J}B\\
 &+CZ^{K'+\epsilon}D_{\max}(Z^{-V}\#\{f\})
       [Z^{-N'}\sum_U|\mathrm{mark}_{\rm inj}(U)|^2
                           |W(NU/Z^{N'})|^2].
\end{split} \tag{A22}
\]
The second line is the already paid positive diagonal. The first line's child is the physical Möbius column
\[
 \sum_A\mu(A)\psi(A)\mathbf1_{(A,m)=1}\chi_A(y)^{\pm1}
       \mathrm{mark}_{\rm residual}(A)\Phi(NA/X_c)/\sqrt{NA},
\]
summed over all nonzero \(Ny\le Z^{H_c}\). It includes both orientations, every residual projector puncture, every shortened \(0<X_c\le X_{\max}\), and every member and height of the fixed finite profile family. The ray \(\psi\) belongs to a fixed finite ray-twist family.

For completeness, (A22) follows by expanding the squared canonical row, separating its common and coprime squarefree parts, applying the admitted masked Poisson identity to the row variable, and grouping the resulting Gauss and quadratic cross phases by the finite ray dictionary. The zero frequency is the displayed diagonal. On the child ball the grouped row is precisely the displayed Möbius column, so its positive sum is bounded by \(B\), retaining all puncture terms and label weights. Outside the ball the radial Fourier argument is at least \(Z^\kappa/b^2\). Choose decay order after the fixed height degree; lattice counting with a fixed polynomial envelope pays the complement. Divisor bounds and finite profile separation account for \(Z^\epsilon\). The primitive Poisson and Gauss identities are the foundational inputs in section 1, rather than consequences of a theorem name or successful source import.

At zero slack the bookkeeping identities are
\[
 K'-N'-V=K-F+5u,\qquad H=1-6u,\qquad
 (K-F+5u)+(H+u)=F. \tag{A23}
\]
A child of size \(Z^{H+u+\epsilon}\), rather than \(Z^H\), suffices. This is precisely the excess paid by the LOW identity (A9) and HIGH ledger.

Restoring that child to the actual inverse is substantive. For a finite prime pool \(S\), write
\[
 C_S(X)=\sum_{A\subseteq S}\prod_{p\in A}c_p\,
             \Phi(\prod_{p\in A}Np/X),\quad
 c_p=-\psi(p)\chi_p(y)/\sqrt{Np}.
\]
For \(p\notin S\),
\[
 C_{S\cup\{p\}}(X)=C_S(X)+c_pC_S(X/Np). \tag{A24}
\]
Iterating solves the avoided-prime column by a finite reciprocal Euler series of unrestricted columns. The remainder vanishes when \(X/(Np)^J<1/b\), since \(\Phi\) is supported in \([a,b]\subset(0,\infty)\) and all ideal norms are at least one. Required primes are restored by the corresponding difference in (A24). For overlapping pools group injective tuples by exact image before the recursion; do not factor that tuple sum as independent slot sums.

The unrestricted column is the actual inverse with profile \(\Phi(x)x^{-1/2}\), since \(X^{-1/2}(NI/X)^{-1/2}=(NI)^{-1/2}\). Mellin separation makes the profile independent of frozen tuple scales. Use a bump equal to one on \([a',2^{2K+1}b']\) and Schwartz Fourier weights for the finite child profiles and their conjugates. Their weighted integrals absorb auxiliary heights, leaving a polynomial in the original row and slot heights. Choose the source mesh first; restoration uses at most \(\min(m_{\rm child}H_{\rm lo},1)\), independent of later classes and child profiles. Small column scales receive a bounded finite-support estimate, not an assertion that every such scale is empty.

The Euler recursion retains its damping: \(|c_p|\le(Np)^{-1/2}\), so its \(j\)-th term carries \((Np)^{-j/2}\). It is not an undamped count of prime powers. Finite required-prime restorations use this factor; the potentially large puncture support is treated by the following norm-power bound.

The puncture/mask restoration costs satisfy, for every fixed \(K\) and \(\eta>0\),
\[
 \mathrm{cost}\le C_{K,\eta}(Nt\,|m|^2)^\eta. \tag{A25}
\]
Indeed the product norm of distinct primes in \(t\cup\{p:p\mid m\}\) is at most \(Nt|m|^2\). A fixed exponential in their number is absorbed into an arbitrary norm power; the additional fixed-order polynomial combinatorics is absorbed likewise. There is no hypothesis that the full small-prime primorial has polynomial norm. Negative orientations use conjugated profiles with the same masks.

For parent caps \(P_{\max},S_{\max}\) and slack \(\kappa>0\), the literal normalized child is
\[
 \left(\frac{P_{\max}+2\kappa}{1-6u-\kappa},
       \frac{S_{\max}-u+3\kappa}{1-6u-\kappa}\right), \tag{A26}
\]
with excess \(u/(1-6u-\kappa)\). Its gates are
\[
 P_{\max}+S_{\max}+4u+10\kappa<1,\qquad6u+2\kappa<1. \tag{A27}
\]
States with insufficient live width use the native canonical-energy estimate; the other states use (A20)–(A26). Their positive union closes the initialization oracle.

At a stage put \(P_{\max}=r-d\), \(S_{\max}=S(r)-D-d\), \(\kappa=d/8\). The old anchor with decrement \(d/2\) covers the child's free cap. For the marked cap its LOW erasure ledger is
\[
 k(S_{\rm child}-S_{\rm old})H_c
 \le u-kD-kd/2+k(3+S_R+d/2)\kappa\le u. \tag{A28}
\]
The stage bounds make the last inequality valid; HIGH children have the same \(H+u\) budget from section 5. Positive reserves absorb all mesh, profile and divisor losses. Principal inverse rows use their principal-character bound; they and fixed-inducing rows were never silently deleted. All roots and units remain in the all-row moment. This proves the inverse half of the new anchor.

### 7. Ordinary rectangle and reflected reference lane

The target is \(G(r-d,0,S(r)-D-d)\), a rectangle with marked slope zero. Substituting \(L=0\) into the old centered-reference proof is insufficient: its reference interval is empty at \(P+2S>1\). PR137 forks the assembly and supplies a new reference lane.

The inherited assembly still performs the actual common-divisor factorization, complete collision and cube/ray restoration, first and second divisors, zero frequency, fixed-inducing diagonal and tails. The following calculation pays every packed first-common side; the stage-point identity (A9) alone would not suffice.

It is enough to treat \(0<d\le1/1000\); larger endpoint decrements follow by rectangle restriction. Distinguish the stage target \(u_0=(1-r/R)/6\), \(H_0=r/R=1-6u_0\), from a side's actual selected width \(u_{\rm s}\). Let \(\Sigma\) be its original marked width, \(f\) its frozen marked width, \(c_g\) its extracted common-norm width, \(P_C\) its ordinary width, and \(s_{\rm s}\) its retained marked width. The exact side geometry gives
\[
\begin{gathered}
 \Sigma\le S(r)-D-d,\quad 0\le f\le c_g,\quad
 0\le P_C,\quad P_C+(c_g-f)\le r-d+\tau,\\
 w=\Sigma-f,\quad
 \min(u_0,w)\le u_{\rm s}\le\min(u_0,w)+\mu,\quad
 0\le s_{\rm s}\le w-u_{\rm s},\quad t\ge-\tau .
\end{gathered}
\]
Here \(\mu\) is the slot mesh and \(\tau\) the frequency tolerance. Choose both at most
\[
 m=\min\{d/64,\epsilon/[256(L_{\rm high}+1)]\},
\]
where \(L_{\rm high}\ge0\) is the HIGH price's Lipschitz constant. Set \(\xi=\tau+6\mu\). Then \(0\le\xi\le7d/64\), and the packed row exponent satisfies
\[
 H_{\rm s}=1+t-6u_{\rm s}\ge H_0-\xi.
\]
The side's upper frequency bound \(t\le1+6u_{\rm s}+\tau\) also gives \(H_{\rm s}\le2+\tau\le3\). The stage bound \(u_0\le1/10000\) gives \(H_0-\xi>1/2\), so the packed radius lies in the assembly's required interval.

Soften the old rectangle by
\[
 d_1=\min(D,d)/4,\quad B_1=R-d_1,\quad
 c_1=S_R-d_1,\quad \ell=d/4>0.
\]
The source \(G(B_1,\ell,c_1)\) is a restriction of the old rectangle \(G(B_1,0,c_1)\): adding the nonnegative term \(\ell s\) only shrinks its admission domain. The stage bounds give \(B_1\ge0\) and \(0\le c_1\le1\). Its LOW price is \(k\) times the clipped deletion need: erase whole slots until both \(s\le c_1H\) and \(P+\ell s\le B_1H\), with the native zero-slot bound as the delete-everything fallback.

First suppose \(w\ge u_0\). Then \(u_{\rm s}\ge u_0\) and
\[
 P_C\le r-d+\tau,\qquad
 s_{\rm s}\le\bar s:=S(r)-D-d-u_0.
\]
The deletion need increases with \(P,s\), decreases with the radius for \(B_1,c_1\ge0\), and is bounded above by the positive part of its two defects. Therefore
\[
\begin{split}
 \mathrm{need}(P_C,s_{\rm s},H_{\rm s})
 \le\max\left(0,\max\left\{
  \bar s-c_1(H_0-\xi),\
  \frac{r-d+\tau+\ell\bar s-B_1(H_0-\xi)}{\ell}
 \right\}\right).
\end{split}
\]
For the cap defect, identity (A9) gives the exact equality
\[
 k[\bar s-c_1(H_0-\xi)]
 =u_0+k(H_0d_1-D-d+c_1\xi)\le u_0.
\]
Indeed \(H_0\le1\), \(d_1\le d/4\), \(c_1\le1\), and \(\xi\le7d/64\), so the bracket is at most \(-D-41d/64<0\). For the budget defect, \(RH_0=r\) gives
\[
\begin{split}
 r-d+\tau+\ell\bar s-B_1(H_0-\xi)
 &=-d+\tau+\ell\bar s+d_1H_0+R\xi-d_1\xi\\
 &\le-d+d/64+d/24+d/4+7d/64\\
 &=-7d/12<0.
\end{split}
\]
Here \(\bar s\le S(r)<137/1000<1/6\), hence \(\ell\bar s\le d/24\); also \(R<1\) and \(d_1\xi\ge0\). Division by \(\ell>0\) preserves negativity. The second defect therefore contributes nothing, and the first one's positive part satisfies
\[
 k\,\mathrm{need}(P_C,s_{\rm s},H_{\rm s})\le u_0\le u_{\rm s},
\]
including the case where that first defect is nonpositive. This is the complete packed-side LOW payment.

For the HIGH part, \(s_{\rm s}\le S(r)-u_0\). Monotonicity in \(P,s\), antitonicity in the radius and the same Lipschitz bounds compare the side with the stage point:
\[
\begin{split}
 \mathrm{high}(w,P_C,s_{\rm s},H_{\rm s})
 &\le\mathrm{high}(w,r,S(r)-u_0,H_0)
                  +L_{\rm high}(\tau+\xi)\\
 &\le u_0+\epsilon/32\le u_{\rm s}+\epsilon/32.
\end{split}
\]
The error bound follows from \(\tau+\xi\le8m\) and \(L_{\rm high}m\le\epsilon/256\). Thus the maximum of the LOW and HIGH prices is at most \(u_{\rm s}+\epsilon/16\), as required.

If \(w<u_0\), the greedy bounds instead give \(u_{\rm s}\ge w\), hence \(s_{\rm s}=0\). The clipped deletion need is zero, and the HIGH price at \((r,0,H_0)\) is zero; the same comparison costs at most \(\epsilon/32\). At the analytic leaf this is the erase-all-slots/native-zero-slot payment, not an application of the old marked source outside its ordinary cap. These two cases exhaust all sides above the positive live-width floor \(\epsilon/12\). Below that floor, use no selection and the native all-slot price: its coefficient \(3/4\) makes the cost at most \((3/4)(\epsilon/12)=\epsilon/16\), including zero marked width.

This is the calculation in the pinned Price/Gates.lean stage_ledger, with its \(\beta=d\), tl \(=\tau\), mesh \(=\mu\), \(x=\xi\), and \(u_0\) distinguished from the actual side selection. It preserves the source's softened face, clipped fallback and full frequency tolerance.

The new reference parameters are
\[
 l_{\rm ref}=7/50,\quad \alpha=3/5,\quad P_{\rm ref}=2/3.
\]
Use a separately proved parent \(G(99/100,49/20,7/50)\). Forward \(K_3\) packet expansion dominates the complete reference rectangle by native leaves at shortened lengths, with one factor at most \(Z^{l_{\rm ref}}\). If the long factor has exponent at most \(1/2\), the parent pays it directly. Otherwise naturally reflect it; the dual exponent is at most \(1/2+\delta+\xi\). For stage cap \(c<137/1000\),
\[
 \frac7{50}+\frac12+\frac{49}{20}c+\frac1{100}<\frac{99}{100},
 \quad c\le\frac7{50},\quad\frac7{50}+c\le1. \tag{A29}
\]
Choose reflection paddings below this reserve. Retain natural conductor zeros and the fixed-inducing predicate. Choose finite profile controls before Fourier heights, estimate original tails with a fixed envelope, and preserve the height factor \(1+2|t|+V\). This pays every native leaf; positivity and the \(K_3\) kernel bound restore the whole reference rectangle.

The corrected reference contract chooses its mesh before ambient data, but degree, controls and constant **after** the fixed radial cap, characters and internal ideal \(Q_0\). An older stronger ordering put these constants before that data and omitted slot-frequency dependence; this route does not prove that stronger statement. The actual consumer fixes the data early and so needs only the corrected contract.

Finally the fixed preceding parent \(G(1-10^{-12},2+10^{-11},3/20)\) pays inheritance below crossing \((B_0-(r-d))/L_0\); above it use the new reference and priced leaf. The completed common-divisor/second-divisor/diagonal assembly from section 1 remains an explicit dependency. The finite stage gates verify its exceptional, root-reference and second-diagonal reserves. Consequently the output is the full ordinary source (A6) on (A4), including all shortened lengths and complementary sectors, rather than a bound only for favorable packed rows.

### 8. Finite chain and acyclicity

Start from \((R_0,z_0,a_{0,0},a_{1,0})=(311/400,0,0,0)\). The inverse decremented base rectangle satisfies \(P+2S<1\), \(2P+8S<3\); the native theorem supplies it even for arbitrary bounded slot coefficients. The ordinary base is covered by reserve-parametric sources approaching \((B,L,c)=(1,2,3/20)\). Cycle068's complete family already supplies these parents; the accepted PR137 proof uses its inherited PR103/PR129 sources.

For \(n=0,\ldots,175\), put \(R_{n+1}=R_n-1/4000\). Compute \(w_b\) by (A19), then

 T_n=\frac{5w_b/4-5/6}{3w_b/2-(1+R_n)/2-z_n},\quad

Use (A8) with \(k=k_n\), and set
\[
 z_{n+1}=10^{-10}\lfloor10^{10}(Y_n(R_{n+1})-D)\rfloor. \tag{A31}
\]
The next line is the affine function through \(Y_n(r)-D-2\cdot10^{-7}\) at the two stage endpoints. The exact certificate checks it is a strict \(10^{-7}\) minorant on every earlier stage, is negative at \(311/400\), has slope in \((0,2/5)\), and is below the next entry gain. The initial line is zero.

For audit, the fourteen strictly positive endpoint quantities are the following, with \(s=S-u\), \(H=r/R\), \(u=(1-H)/6\), \(w_{\rm lo}=w_k\), \(w_{\rm hi}=w_{3/4}\):

| Gate | Quantity required positive |
|---|---|
| 1 | \(HF_0-3/100000\) |
| 2 | \(137/1000-S\) |
| 3 | \(14/100-S/H\) |
| 4 | \(9/10-r-S-4u\) |
| 5 | \(91/100-r-S-4u\) |
| 6 | \(5/6+21/250-r-S-3u-1/100\) |
| 7 | \(3H-2r-8s-1/5\) |
| 8 | \(r-1/2-Y+u-1/5\) |
| 9 | \(r/2-s-\tfrac32(5/6-k)u/(k^2(1/2-a_1))-1/10\) |
| 10 | \(H+u-H/6-1/15-(3/4)r-s-3/100\) |
| 11 | \(w_{\rm lo}-2/3\) |
| 12 | \(79/100-w_{\rm hi}\) |

The certificate also checks \(R\le w_b\), \(45457/125000\le k<1/2\), \(k>9/25\), and nonnegative next gain. Gates transfer through each interval by affine dependence, multiplying by positive \(H\), and treating the two affine branches of gate 13 separately. The own line and return line are affine, so endpoint minorants imply full-interval minorants. The independent rational reconstruction checks these endpoint facts and all earlier-line inequalities; it does not certify the analytic foundations.

Strong induction now proves every whole stage. Its entry anchor follows from the preceding stage and downward rounding (A31). Short HIGH witnesses below the top use strictly earlier stages by (A15); above the top the nonpositive line permits native sources. Sections 6 and 7 prove both new halves. Thus no stage assumes its own moment and no limiting source is invoked. The 176 intervals cover \(I\), since \(311/400-176/4000=1467/2000\). The return line (A7) is below each \(Y_n-D\), with the stated positive pad. Rectangle restriction gives Theorem A.

This is the fixed-decrement PR137 construction. Removing its fixed \(D\), or replacing the fixed \(10^{-6}\) cutoff padding by a variable debit, requires the separate PR141 analytic extension; it is not a consequence of sending \(D\) to zero in this finite certificate.

### 9. Consumer transfer, strict gain and retained suppliers

Compact logarithmic Fourier separation converts inverse reference profiles to detector inverse profiles with both orientations, all log-derivatives \(n\le2\), shifts \(s\in[0,1]\), and heights \(|t|\le h\), with \(C(1+h)^J\). Its degree may depend on the fixed row data. The estimate
\[
 (1+|\theta|+h_v)^{2J}\le(1+h_v)^{2J}(1+|\theta|)^{2J}
\]
lets Schwartz Fourier integrals absorb auxiliary heights. The constant does not acquire arbitrary dependence on a live height. The physical slot is the conjugate direct slot at the physical real part \(17/50\): conjugating its annular shift gives real exponent \(-33/50\), with the exact ray-character and zero masks. No substitute coefficient vector occurs.

For a detector fiber at scale \(U\), the new inverse inlet is \(r\in I\) and selected marked width at most \((1-r)/2+g(r)-\nu_0\). The ordinary inlet is **doubled** per-factor width \(2m\in I\), cap evaluated at \(2m\), and derivative tests \(j+k\le2\). All original row subsets, profiles, natural zeros, real shifts and height tests remain.

To make constants uniform over live \(r\), use a finite grid just to the right of each requested width, with a smaller common decrement; take the minimum mesh and maximum/union of degrees and controls over that grid. The native extension above \(311/400\) covers the top cells. The consumer's fixed positive slack pays the capacity loss. This gives one mesh before weighted-source data and polynomial-height constants before scale. Choosing unrelated constants separately for every real \(r\) would not prove this inlet.

There is a strict source enlargement. At \(r=3/4\),
\[
 g(r)=413619/400000000>0.
\]
With \(d=1/100000\), its admitted corner is
\[
 P=74999/100000,\quad S=50409619/400000000,\quad
 P+2S-1=407619/200000000>0. \tag{A32}
\]
It is outside every Cycle068 complete source \(G(B,L,c_s)\), \(B<1\), \(L>\max(1,2B)\): old admission would imply \(P<B(1-2S)<1-2S\), contradicting (A32). It also violates the first native inverse gate, while the second has reserve \(24591381/50000000>0\). This is a genuine supplier improvement outside the union of the old complete family, regardless of whether a particular endpoint certificate uses that corner.

The positive affine gain holds only for \(r<5524290/7227847\); the line is negative near the top, where native inputs already suffice. The immediate new consumer is the selected-mark capacity in the same-zero detector, not an arbitrary larger sloping global source without a domain-cover proof. The theorem does not pay unrelated residual inverse bilinear targets, admit arbitrary prime subsets or row-dependent coefficients, remove moving presentation zeros, allow a live growing slot number, or make boundary constants uniform.

The anchor theorem changes source admission, not the physical return's prime-shift damping. Any return using it must retain the original shift weights, root restoration, intrinsic floor, tails and conductor sectors; their payment is not implied by (A32).

Keep the older arbitrary-coefficient native inverse theorem, inverse-specific stronger special moments, coherent inverse products, zero-width complements and useful source geometries. The new source does not dominate all of them. This section is ready for source/anchor integration; the count and physical-return lane must verify its own guards before a new endpoint can be reported.

### A. The variable-tolerance HIGH price

Fix a strict curve, a right endpoint \(R\), and \(r\le R\) as in
RESEARCH.md §2. Use
\[
z=W(R),\quad v=W'(R),\quad H=r/R,\quad u=(1-H)/6,\quad
s=H((1-R)/2+z)+u/k,
\]
\[
k=\{2+6(z-Rv+R\gamma)\}^{-1},\quad
a_0=z-Rv-q/5,\quad a_1=-v,\quad
0<q\le\min(10^{-12},\gamma/1000).
\]
The strict-curve bounds give
\[
3/4\le R\le7/9,\quad .9\le H\le1,\quad 0\le z\le.0011,
\quad .363656\le k<.5,\quad0\le a_1\le.1,\quad u\le10^{-4}.
\tag{A1}
\]
Here \(s\) is the child mark width after removing the bare \(u\) term; it
is not the total \(S=s+u\) of the ordinary source.

Write \(B=1/2-a_1=1/2+v>0\), and define
\[
w_b=(R/2+z-a_0)/B,\qquad
F_0=5/6-(5/4-3k/2)w_b-k(1+R)/2-kz.
\]
The unpadded reserve has the exact identity
\[
B_0:=5/6-5R/4+k(R-1/2-z)
 =\frac{kR(15R-10)}2\{v-\gamma-F(R,z)\}.                  \tag{A2}
\]
The cutoff relation defining \(k\) proves the equality simply by expansion.
The differential reserve is at least \(3\gamma\). Since
\(kR(15R-10)\ge1/3\), (A2) gives \(B_0\ge\gamma/3\).
The actual padded line satisfies
\[
w_b=R+\frac{q}{5(1/2+v)},\qquad
F_0=B_0-\frac{(5/4-3k/2)q}{5(1/2+v)}\ge B_0-q.
\tag{A3}
\]
The inequality follows from \(v\ge-4/45\), \(k\ge0\), \(q\ge0\).
Thus \(F_0\ge\gamma/4\), and
\[
HF_0\ge9\gamma/40>30q.                                   \tag{A4}
\]
This is the actual positive reserve after the source-pad debit.

For each non-tiny HIGH class \(k\le\nu\le3/4,\ 0\le e\le\nu\), choose
\[
g_\nu=\frac{r+s-H/2-Ha_0-u/\nu}{B},\qquad
w_\nu=g_\nu/H+q,\qquad
\sigma_q(w)=\max(0,(1-w)/2+a_0-a_1w-q/10).                \tag{A5}
\]
The identity
\[
B(g_\nu-r)=H(z-a_0+a_1R)+u(1/k-1/\nu)\ge0
\tag{A6}
\]
gives \(w_\nu\ge R+q\). Also \(g_\nu\) increases with \(\nu\).
Its formula and (A1) give \(g_{3/4}/H\le R+.01\); hence
\(2/3<w_\nu\le.79\). Positivity and the earlier-anchor inequality
\(a_0-a_1R\le z\) imply
\[
H\sigma_q(w_\nu)\le H((1-R)/2+z)\le s.                   \tag{A7}
\]
In particular this is actual mark supply, not a free selected-width parameter.
Since \(a_0\le1\), \(w_\nu\ge0\) and \(a_1\ge0\), one may use the conservative
\(\sigma_q\le3/2\), so \(w_\nu+\sigma_q<6\).

The two detector counts at this cutoff are
\[
C_{\rm short}=H-\nu Hw_\nu-e\min(s,H\sigma_q(w_\nu)),
\]
\[
C_{\rm long}=H/6+(5/6-\nu)H(3w_\nu/2+q).
\tag{A8}
\]
Their price is
\(\nu r+es+\max(C_{\rm short},C_{\rm long})-H\).
Both counts, including both positive pads, must be paid.

For the short count let
\[
X_0=(H-g_\nu)/2+Ha_0-a_1g_\nu,\qquad
c_q=(1/2+a_1)q+q/10.
\]
Then \(0\le c_q\le q\), and the raw selected expression has
\[
H\{(1-w_\nu)/2+a_0-a_1w_\nu-q/10\}=X_0-Hc_q.
\]
It is bounded above by both \(s\) and \(H\sigma_q\). Moreover (A5) gives
\[
s-X_0=g_\nu-r+u/\nu\ge0,\qquad
\nu(r-g_\nu)+e(s-X_0)\le u.
\]
Consequently the short price is at most
\[
\nu(r-g_\nu)+e(s-X_0)-\nu Hq+eHc_q\le u,
\tag{A9}
\]
using \(e\le\nu\), \(c_q\le q\). The lost cap is explicitly paid by the
positive witness shift; it has not disappeared.

For the long count define
\[
G(\nu)=H+u-H/6-(5/6-\nu)(3g_\nu/2)-\nu(r+s).
\]
Direct expansion gives
\[
G(k)=HF_0,
\]
\[
G(\nu)-G(k)=(\nu-k)
\left\{\frac32g_\nu-r-s
 -\frac32(5/6-k)\frac{u}{k\nu B}\right\}.                 \tag{A10}
\]
The braces are nonnegative: \(g_\nu\ge r\), \(\nu\ge k\), and the derivative
gate is
\[
r/2-s-\frac32(5/6-k)\frac{u}{k^2B}\ge0.                  \tag{A11}
\]
For completeness, (A1) bounds its left side below by
\[
H(R-1/2-z)-u/k-30u
\ \ge\ 27/125-3u-30u>0.
\]
Thus \(G(\nu)\ge HF_0>30q\). Substituting \(Hw_\nu=g_\nu+Hq\)
in the long count shows that its extra padding cost is
\[
(5/6-\nu)H(5q/2)\le5q/2.
\]
The long price is therefore at most
\[
u-G(\nu)+5q/2<u-55q/2<u.                                \tag{A12}
\]
Finally, the tiny class has reserve at least \(3/100\): its gate is
\[
H+u-H/6-1/15-(3/4)r-s>3/100.
\]
Its left side equals
\(H(1/3-R/4-z)+u-u/k-1/15\), which exceeds \(3/100\) by (A1).
Equations (A9)–(A12) prove the class price bound, including tiny cores.

The recentering used by the physical analytic consumer is exact. Put
\[
\widetilde a_0=a_0+10^{-13}-q/10.
\]
Then
\[

=\sigma_q(w).
\tag{A13}
\]
The generic consumer is instantiated with the same actual witness shift

The fixed PR137 pad is therefore not being silently used at a new value.

The remaining zero-fixed-loss adapter retains the requested rectangle

## H.2. Signed centering on a fixed inducing row

**Lemma H.2.** Consider the actual cube-free two-ordinary source on a fixed inducing row, with fixed primitive inducing characters \(\psi_1,\psi_2\). They may coincide or both be principal. Fix the live prime assignment first and delete its supplying primes in both ordinary variables. Keep all other original holes, seeds, congruences and fixed bad places. Compare ordinary scales \((X_1,X_2)\) and \((Y_1,Y_2)\) satisfying
\(X_1X_2=Y_1Y_2=T\), using the same two scaled profiles and their same independent normalized heights. If \(L=\min(X_1,X_2,Y_1,Y_2)\), their normalized signed difference is
\[
 \ll_\epsilon U^\epsilon\mathcal S(W_1)\mathcal S(W_2)
 (1+|h_1|+|h_2|)^J\sqrt T\max(1,L)^{-3/5}.
 \tag{H8}
\]
The implied constants may depend on the fixed character dictionary and source caps. A polynomial norm cap on the combined exceptional radical is required.

**Proof.** The exact good-prime restricted generating function, after extracting the two ordinary Euler factors, has numerator
\[
 H_3(x,y)=1-(x^3+x^2y+xy^2+y^3)
             +(x^3y+x^2y^2+xy^3),
 \tag{H9}
\]
where \(x=\psi_1(\mathfrak p)(N\mathfrak p)^{-s_1}\) and
\(y=\psi_2(\mathfrak p)(N\mathfrak p)^{-s_2}\). Thus the complete series is
\[
 L(s_1,\psi_1)L(s_2,\psi_2)\,
 \prod_{\mathfrak p\ {\rm good}}H_3(x,y)
 \prod_{\mathfrak p\ {\rm exceptional}} E_{\mathfrak p}(s_1,s_2).
 \tag{H10}
\]
Remove exceptional Euler factors from the displayed \(L\)'s first, and let \(E_{\mathfrak p}\) be the actual polynomial of permitted residual valuations. This prescription covers deletion in just one coordinate and never divides by \(H_3\) or a character value. On \(\Re s_i\ge2/5\), the good product converges absolutely, since its first nonconstant terms have degree three. The exceptional product costs \(C^{\omega(\mathfrak f)}\ll_\epsilon U^\epsilon\) under the stated polynomial radical cap. The ordinary fixed-character \(L\)-functions have polynomial vertical growth there, apart from their possible principal poles at one. No zero-free reciprocal estimate is needed for this lemma.

Write \(\Phi_i(u)=W_i(u)u^{ih_i}\). On the first arm the double Mellin weight is
\(\widehat\Phi_1(s_1)\widehat\Phi_2(s_2)X_1^{s_1}X_2^{s_2}\); on the second it is exactly the same pair of transforms with \(Y_i\). If the incoming height is written as \((NI)^{it_i}\), take its outside phase \(X_i^{it_i}\) **before** installing a reference arm. With actual prefixes \(d_1,d_2\), genuine common ideal \(G\), and common residual height \(v\), the remaining common phase is
\[
       (T/(Nd_1Nd_2NG))^{iv}.
 \tag{H11}
\]
A profile prefix introduces no ray character unless that ideal was literally extracted from the character's argument. This is necessary for independent \(t_1,t_2\).

Shift both Mellin lines to \(2/5\). If both characters are principal, the double residue equals
\[
 T\widehat\Phi_1(1)\widehat\Phi_2(1)
 \operatorname{Res}_1 L(\cdot,\psi_1)
 \operatorname{Res}_1 L(\cdot,\psi_2)\mathcal H(1,1),
\]
where \(\mathcal H\) includes this row's actual punctures. It cancels exactly between the equal-product arms. Different puncture densities in the two coordinates cause no problem: both arms use the same two densities. The single residues and shifted double integral on either arm are bounded by
